Bernstein, Honorary Adviser to Films Division, Ministry of Information, 1940-42; Editorial Secretary, British Paramount News, 1942-47; Temporary Executive Officer, subsequently Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Films Division, Central Office of Information, 1947-51; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 17th October 1951; Assistant Information Officer 14th January 1959; Information Officer 1st August 1959.

BICKFORD, William Reginald, MBE (1943); born 14th September 1911; educated Cheltenham College and Wadham College, Oxford; Lit Hum. Part I Class I, Part II Class II; m. 1939 Elizabeth Edwards (1 s. 1948; 1 d. 1952); Indian Civil Service 1934; served in Burma as Assistant Commissioner until 1939; posted to Home Department April 1939; Civil Affairs Staff, Burma, February 1944; commissioned into A.B.R.O. from same date; served in India and Burma; released with rank of Major October 1945; Secretary, Defence and External Affairs Department, October 1945 to March 1947, and Additional Secretary, Finance Department, to May 1947; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th April 1948; Delhi April 1948 to May 1950; Karachi January 1955; Dacca November 1956 to June 1958 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner February to May 1958); Canberra 5th March 1962.

BISHOP, Major-General Sir Alec (William) Henry (Alexander), KCMG (1964; CMG 1961), CB (1946), CVO (1961), OBE (Military), Commander, Order of St. John of Jerusalem (1951); born 20th June 1897; educated Plymouth College 1907-14 and Royal Military College, Sandhurst, 1914-15; m. 1925 Mary Corbett (1 s. 1926); joined Dorset Regiment (2nd Lieutenant) April 1915; served in Iraq and Palestine 1915-18; India 1919-25; England, and attended Army Staff College, Camberley, 1926-29; Germany 1930; G.S.O. 3, War Office, 1931-34; R.A.F. Staff College 1935; Staff Officer (G.S.O. 2) to Inspector-General, African Colonial Forces, Colonial Office, 1936-39; Brevet Lieutenant-Colonel 1938; Chief Staff Officer, East Africa Force, 1939-40; Liaison Officer with War Cabinet Offices, Dominions Office, 1940-41; Colonel 1941; Brigadier 1941; Principal Administrative Staff Officer, West Africa, 1941-42; Brigadier, Inter-Allied Planning Staff, North Africa, 1943; Major-General 1944; Director of Quartering, War Office, 1944; Acting Director-General, Political Intelligence Department, Foreign Office, 1945; Foreign Office (Control Commission for Germany) 1945-50 (Chief, Information Services Division, 1945-46, Deputy Chief of Staff 1947-48, Commissioner 'Land', North Rhine-Westphalia, 1948-50); Assistant Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, with seniority from 1st July 1948, 1st January 1951; Principal Staff Officer to Secretary of State July 1953; visited Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, India, Pakistan, Ceylon and Malaya 1956-57, Canada, Nigeria, Ghana and Sierra Leone 1962-63; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta. October 1957 to July 1962; local Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st October 1957; Director of Information Services and Cultural Relations July 1962 to April 1964; High Commissioner in Cyprus April 1964.

BLAIR, Oliver Robin; born 7th October 1925; educated Winchester College, West Hill High School, Montreal, 1939-43 and King's College, Cambridge, (Colonial Service Course) 1947-48; Called to Bar 1959; Coldstream Guards 1944-47 (Lieutenant); Administrative Officer Class IV, Gold Coast, 19th January 1949; Class III 1954; Class II 1957; retired from Overseas Civil Service (Ghana) 23rd December 1958; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th June 1959; Calcutta July 1960 to September 1962; Principal (local) July 1960; Principal 1st December 1960; Karachi September 1962.
Blanchard, Arthur, MBE (1962); born 8th November 1906; m. 1938 Catherine Gladys Hunt (dec. 1959) (1 d. 1946); enlisted Royal Signals October 1926; served in India 1926–32 and Northern China 1934–38; Instructor to Supp. Reserve 1938–39; B.E.F., September 1939 to June 1940; Mentioned in Despatches; Commissioned 1941; India 1941–42; East Africa and British Somaliland 1943–44; India and Burma 1944–45; released 1945 (Major); Tempy. Appts. Officer, Min. of Lab. & Nat. Service, 1945–48; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th February 1948; Executive Officer 24th May 1951; Bombay 1953–55; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

Booker, Eleanor Milford, MBE (1951); born 28th June 1918; educated St. Mary's School, Calne, 1930–36 and Westfield College, London University, 1937–40; Class IIA Honours in History; BA 1940; secretarial work, War Office, (Regional Headquarters, Birmingham) March to September 1941; Temporary Assistant Principal, India Office, 22nd September 1941; special duty with Cabinet Mission to India March to July 1946; Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer, Colombo, August 1954 to November 1955; Press Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, April 1957; Senior Information Officer 20th January 1958; Principal Information Officer (temporary) 1st April 1960, (acting) 1st April 1963.

Boothby, Ernest Edward; born 22nd August 1923; m. 1948 Nina Hurt (2 s. 1949, 1953; 1 d. 1956); Telegraphist, Central Telegraph Office, 1939; military service, Royal Signals, 1941–47; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1952; Executive Officer December 1954; Wellington July 1958 to August 1961; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

Borthwick, James, MBE (Military); born 31st May 1913; educated Whitehill School, Glasgow, 1925–28, Rutherglen Academy 1928–30 and Glasgow University 1930–33; MA; m. 1941 Anne Stewart McKiddie (1 d. 1944; 2 s. 1946, 1950); journalist, Southern Reporter, 1930–32; Courier & Advertiser, Dundee, 1932–35; assistant editor, The Weekly News 1935–40; enlisted Black Watch 1940; commissioned Black Watch 1941; served Middle East, North Africa, Sicily and Italy 1943–44 (Mentioned in Despatches), and in North-West Europe 1944–46; P.R.O., 51st Highland Division, 1943–45; DADPR, 2nd Army and 21st Army Group and BAOR, 1945–46; DADPR, H.Q. Western Command, 1946–52; Major; released 1952; Senior Information Officer, H.Q. Western Command, 1952–56; Deputy Director, Information, South Africa, 1956–61; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st December 1957; Principal Information Officer 1st Army 1958; Deputy Director of Information, Lagos, 1961–63; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, 1963 to March 1964.

Bottom, Doreen Joan; born 5th February 1923; educated Glendale County Grammar School, Wood Green, 1934–39; Clerical Assistant, Dominions Office, 17th July 1939; Clerical Officer 28th February 1940; Executive Officer 5th February 1948; Higher Executive Officer 2nd January 1956; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

Bottomley, James Reginald Alfred; born 12th January 1920; educated King's College School 1933–38 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1938–40; m. 1941 Barbara Vardon (2 d. 1943, 1946; 2 s. 1944, 1963 and 1 s. dec.); military service 1940–46; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 21st October 1946; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 29th March 1947; Capetown/Pretoria January 1948 to March 1951; Principal 20th September 1949; Karachi September 1953; seconded to Foreign Office and posted to British Embassy, Washington, September 1953; U.K. Mission to the U.N., New York, February to July 1959; Assistant Secretary 2nd February 1959; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur, (local Assistant Under-Secretary of State) September 1963.

Boulton, John Terence Tyson; born 15th July 1929; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th February 1950; Madras 1957–58; Karachi 1959–63; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963; Kuala Lumpur June 1964.

Bourn, James; born 30th August 1917; educated Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Darlington; m. 1944 Isobel Mackenzie (1 s. 1947); military service 1939–46; served in India, North Africa and Italy; P.O.W.; Captain; Executive Officer, Ministry of Health, 7th September 1936; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, 1947; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1947; Principal November 1949; Secretary to the Salaries Commission, Bahamas, 1948–49; seconded to Tanganyika 1953–55; Commonwealth Relations Office 28th June 1961; seconded to Central African Office March 1962; Dar es Salaam June 1963; Deputy High Commissioner, Zanzibar, August 1964.

Bowley, Brian Ernest; born 26th June 1932; educated Coalville and Loughborough Grammar Schools 1941–48; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1950–51; National Service at Joint Services Schools of Languages and with Intelligence Corps 1951–53; Services' Diploma as Interpreter in Russian Language from University of Cambridge 1952; Executive Officer, Crown Agents, 1953–62; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations
Office, 24th April 1962; Madras 1962–63; Delhi 1963–64; Calcutta (local Higher Executive Officer) May 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

BRANNEY, Louis; born 28th January 1916; educated the Royal Liberty School, Gidea Park, Essex, and King's College, University of London; 1st Class Hons. in Modern History 1938; BA; Inglis Post-graduate research student in University of London 1938–39; University of Belgrade 1939; m. 1949 Margaret Brittain (4 d.); joined R.A. 1940; commissioned 1941; Political Intelligence Department of Foreign Office/SHAEC 1943; Foreign Office Research Department 1945; Deputy British Editor of the joint Foreign Office/U.S.A. State Department Publication Documents on German Foreign Policy 1919–45, 1946–48; Research Officer to Colonial Office 1948–63; Research Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd September 1963.

BRIGGS, John Levi; born 24th April 1916; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th June 1951; Executive Officer 8th July 1953; Freetown April 1961 to July 1964; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 1st September 1963; Lusaka August 1964.

BRIND, Arthur Henry; born 4th July 1927; educated Barry Grammar School 1938–44 and St. John's College, Cambridge, 1944–47; Historical Tripos Class II Division 1; m. 1954 Barbara Harrison (1 s. 1961; 1 d. 1964); military service 1947–49; Colonial Administrative Service and H.M.O.C.S. 1950–60; served in Gold Coast and Ghana; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th August 1960; Principal 1st August 1961; Ottawa February 1963.

BRISTOW, Peter Bernard; born 17th November 1923; educated Shooters Hill School, Woolwich, 1935–39; m. 1951 Primrose Norman; (2 d. 1954, 1958); Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Supply, 1940–42; served with Royal Navy September 1942 to February 1946; Temporary Clerk, Crown Agents, 4th February 1946; Clerical Officer 25th April 1947; Executive Officer 23rd March 1953; seconded to Government of Uganda as Treasury Accountant June 1958 to August 1961; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th May 1962; Dar es Salaam 5th September 1963; Nairobi 9th July 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Britten, George Vallette, Brigadier (retd.), CBE (1947; OBE 1942; MBE 1940), American Legion of Merit (1946), West German Grosses Verdienst Kreuz (1959); born 19th March 1909; educated Wellingborough and R.M.C., Sandhurst; m. 1937 Shirley Stewart-Wink (3 s. 1938, 1940, 1949); Commissioned in the Northamptonshire Regiment 1929; served in United Kingdom and Ireland 1929–39; Staff College 1939; North-West Europe 1939–40; Staff Appointments in England and Ireland 1940–41; Commanded an Airborne Battalion, United Kingdom, North Africa and Sicily, 1942–43; Deputy Chief of Staff, 5th U.S. Army, Italy, 1943–44; Planning Staff, H.Q. 21 Army Group, North-West Europe, 1944 to end of war; three times Mentioned in Despatches; Assistant Chief of Staff, Military Government/Civil Affairs (later Control Commission for Germany), 1945–47; Regimental duty, Berlin and Austria, 1947–48; War Office Staff 1949–51; Commandant, Small Arms School, Hythe, and Chairman, Army Rifle Association, 1952–54; British Instructor, U.S. Army Staff College, Fort Leavenworth, U.S., 1954–55; N.A.T.O. Staff, Fontainebleau, 1956–58; Military Attaché, British Embassy, Bonn, 1959–61; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1961; Enugu August 1962 to November 1963; Kaduna February 1964.

BRITTEN, Rae Gordon; born 27th September 1920; educated Liverpool Institute High School 1932–39 and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1939–41 and 1945–47 (Classical Exhibitioner); Hon. Mods. Class II 1940; Philosophy, Politics and Economics Class II 1947; m. 1952 Valentine Alms (3 d. 1953, 1955, 1959; 1 s. 1956); military service 1941–45; Research Assistant with Common Ground, Ltd. October 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd May 1948; Calcutta October 1948; Delhi October 1949 to November 1950; Principal 20th August 1951; United Kingdom delegation to G.A.T.T. Review Session in Geneva 1954–55; Bombay April 1955 to July 1958; Karachi June 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, March 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, June 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963 to July 1964; Kingston October 1964.

BROADFOOT, Alexander William; born 29th January 1924; educated Possilpark School and North Kelvinside School, Glasgow, 1935–40; m. 1953 Kathleen Mary Warner (1 s. 1956; 1 d. 1960); Post Office 1941; Royal Corps of Signals 1943–47; rejoined Post Office; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1950; Madras February to October 1953; local Executive Officer November 1953; Canberra November 1953 to November 1956; Executive Officer December 1954; Wellington February 1959 to January 1962; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 23rd May 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

BROCKETT, Frank Neil; born 24th January 1916; educated Portsmouth Grammar School; Associate, Institute of Bankers; Fellow, Chartered Institute of Secretaries; m. 1940 Doreen Lois Tweed (3 s. 1942, 1946, 1949); Lloyds Bank 1933–39; commissioned in Royal Naval Reserve 1938;
war service: Dunkirk (Mentioned in Despatches), R.N. College Dartmouth and cruiser H.M.S. London 1939-46; Reserve Decoration 1952; retired as Lieutenant Commander 1954; Colonial Audit Service: Tanganyika 1946, London 1948, Aden 1951, Kenya 1954; Senior Assistant Secretary, Treasury, Kenya, 1956; Under-Secretary 1959; Deputy Director of Personnel 1963; retired from H.M. Overseas Civil Service 1963; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1964; Nairobi 1964.

BROMAGE, James Richard Vincent Arthur, CBE (1961); born 12th June 1914; educated Rugby School 1927-33 and New College, Oxford, 1933-37; Lit. Hum. Class II; MA; m. 1948 Frances Charlotte Kerr (3 s. 1949, 1952, 1955); Colonial Administrative Service, Nigeria, 1938-60; Nigeria Regiment 1939-43; Senior District Officer 1953; Resident 1955; Staff Grade 1957; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Western Region, Nigeria, 1958-60; Temporary Principal, Colonial Office, 1961; Temporary Principal, Department of Technical Co-Operation, 1961-64; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th July 1964; Accra July 1964.

BROWER, David Russell Francis; born 12th September 1918; educated Liverpool College; enlisted in ranks, R.A. (T.A.), 1938; mobilized September 1939; B.E.F., France and Belgium, 1940; seconded to London University, School of Oriental Studies, for 18 months' study of Japanese 1942; commissioned 1944 into Intelligence Corps and posted G.H.Q. (India) as Army Interpreter in S.E.A. theatre; demobilized 1946; India Office 13th December 1946; Information Officer (temporary Senior Information Officer) with seniority from 1st August 1949; Regional Information Officer, Bombay, December 1946 to May 1953 (temporarily Deputy Director, British Information Services, New Delhi, July to October 1950); Regional Information Officer (and Acting Director, British Information Services), Karachi, May 1953 to January 1954; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Johannesburg, January 1954 to September 1956; Regional Information Officer, Vancouver, November 1956 to October 1961; Principal Information Officer (local) 1st April 1958; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960.

BROWN, Alan James; born 28th August 1921; educated Wandsworth School 1931-39 and Magdalene College, Cambridge, 1939-41; Class I Modern and Mediaeval languages Tripos; MA; Infantry O.C.T.U., Sandhurst, November 1941; commissioned Intelligence Corps April 1942; served in West Africa 1942-44 and in North-West Europe (mainly Germany) 1944-47; Major; released April 1947; Intelligence Officer, Grade I, Control Commission for Germany, 1947-48; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd August 1948; Calcutta November 1948 to April 1951; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 9th July 1951; Principal 1st December 1952; Dacca December 1952; Karachi August 1953 to February 1955; Kuala Lumpur July 1957 to July 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Nicosia, (local Assistant Secretary) March to September 1964.

BROWN, Benvenuto Dunelm; born 9th October 1916; educated Queen Elizabeth Grammar School, Darlington; m. 1948 Mehra Vacha; on staff of Northern Echo and Northern Despatch 1933-40; served in Royal Navy 1940-46; Private Secretary to H.E. the Officer Administering the Government of Ceylon 1946-47; Temporary Information Officer, India Office, 5th May 1947; Regional Information Officer in Calcutta August 1947 to May 1954; Information Officer 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 27th November 1951; Senior Information Officer 23rd May 1953; Information Officer, New Zealand, November 1954; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, June 1956 to April 1960; local Principal Information Officer 9th June 1957; Deputy Director, B.I.S., India, September 1960 to January 1964; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960; Director of British Information Services, Ceylon, February 1964.

BROWNE, Hablot Robert Edgar, CMG (1955), OBE (1942); born 11th August 1905; educated St. George's, Harpenden, 1914-24 and Christ's College, Cambridge, 1924-28; BA 1927; m. 1933 Petra Tainsh (1 d. 1939); Colonial Administrative Service 1928; served in Nigeria 1928-39; Assistant Colonial Secretary, Barbados, 1939; Assistant Secretary, Jamaica, 1943; Deputy Colonial Secretary 1945; Administrative Officer, Class I, Nigeria, 1950; Civil Secretary, Northern Region of Nigeria, 1951-55; Acting Governor, Northern Region of Nigeria, 1954; retired from Colonial Service 1955; Assistant Adviser to the Government of Qatar, Persian Gulf, 1956-57; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1959.

BROWNLee, George; born 21st July 1922; educated St. Mary's College, Great Crosby; Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 26th June 1939; war service 1942-46; Parachutist Sgt., Royal Artillery, 6th Airborne Division; served in Normandy, Ardennes, Holland and Rhine; wounded; P.O.W. 1945; Executive Officer 14th November 1947; Karachi 1950-54; Information Officer, Dacca, 1957-59; Colombo June 1959 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Acting British Representative in the Maldive Islands
September to December 1961; Information Officer, Kaduna, February 1963; Regional Information Officer, Enugu, (local Senior Information Officer) September 1964.

**Burns**, Kevin Francis Xavier; born 18th December 1930; educated Finchley Grammar School 1938-48 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1950-56; Historical Tripos; BA 1953; m. 1963 Nan Pinto (1 s. 1963); National Service 1948-50; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th October 1956; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State January 1958 to September 1959; Colombo October 1959 to February 1963; Principal 18th April 1960.

**Bustin**, Frederick William; born 27th February 1904; educated Colfe's School, London, 1916-22 and University College, London; w.; Staff of the Civil and Military Gazette, Lahore, 1926-51; Punjab Light Horse (A.F.I.) 1931-44, Commissioned; part-time head of Journalism Department, Punjab University, 1947-49; Information Services, Government of the Federation of Malaya, 1952-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 30th May 1960; Madras 1960 to May 1962; Bombay (Temporary Principal Information Officer) October 1962.

**Butterfield**, Charles Harris, QC (Singapore); born 28th June 1911; educated Downside School and Trinity College, Cambridge; Barrister at Law, Middle Temple, 1934; Colonial Legal Service, Crown Counsel, Straits Settlements, 1938; war service 1941-46; P.O.W. (Siam); Solicitor-General, Singapore, 1948; Legislative Council; Attorney-General, Singapore, 1955; Council of Ministers and Legislative Assembly, Singapore; retired from Her Majesty's Overseas Civil Service 1958; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1959; Temporary Legal Assistant 25th August 1961.

**Butters**, Richard; born 5th December 1924; educated St. Edward's College, Malta, and Plymouth and Mannamead College; m. 1948 Ivy Ethel Horsfield (1 d. 1957); R.N.V.R. June 1943; Midshipman February 1944; Sub-Lieutenant June 1944; released November 1946; T.C.III., Ministry of Works, February 1947; Clerical Officer November 1947; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 28th May 1956; Karachi February 1958 to February 1960; Dar es Salaam November 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th March 1964.

**Byatt**, Hugh Campbell; born 27th August 1927; educated Gordonstoun School and New College, Oxford, 1945 and 1948-51; P.P.E.; MA 1951; m. 1954 Fiona Mary MacKenzie Coats (2 s. 1955, 1962; 1 d. 1957); Royal Navy 1945-48; Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; attached Faculty of Letters, University of the Sorbonne, 1951; Nigerian Civil Service 1952-57; Provincial Administration 1952-55; Office of the Governor, Eastern Nigeria, 1955-56; on special duty in connexion with the Royal Visit to Nigeria 1956; Office of the Premier, Eastern Nigeria, 1957; Assistant Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th December 1957; Information Officer 1st August 1959; Bombay March 1961 to November 1963; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963; Principal 22nd July 1964.

**Byrne**, Mary Sarah Nora, MBE (1959); born 24th November 1902; educated King Edward's Grammar School, Camp Hill, Birmingham; Typist, India Office, 25th May 1925; Shorthand-Writer 28th February 1927; Supervisor 22nd March 1934; Supt./Typists 17th November 1939; Higher Clerical Officer (later Executive Officer) 11th June 1944; Welfare Officer (temporary Higher Executive Officer; Higher Executive Officer 18th October 1954) 8th September 1953.

**Cambridge**, Alan John; born 1st July 1925; educated Beckenham Grammar School; m. Thelma Elliot (3 s. 1948, 1952, 1961; 1 d. 1953); enlisted Fleet Air Arm July 1943; RAF April 1944; Flight-Sergeant Air Gunner, 150 Squadron, Bomber Command; released June 1947; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Pensions, 1947; Clerical Officer January 1948; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th April 1955; Madras February 1956 to March 1958; Kuala Lumpur September 1959 to July 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Salisbury June 1962; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 14th August 1964.

**Carr**, Reginald William Stanley; born 6th August 1918; educated Methodist College, Belfast; m. 1942 Hilda Wyllie (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1952); served in Royal Artillery and Royal Corps of Signals 1939-48; commissioned 1942, served in Algeria, Tunisia, Sicily, Italy and Austria 1942 to April 1948; Captain; Temporary Clerk II, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th April 1948; Delhi April 1948; Bombay May to November 1948; Delhi 1948-52; unestablished Executive Officer May 1952; Madras March 1952 to February 1953; Executive Officer 5th May 1953; Karachi June 1954 to February 1956; Bombay (local Higher Executive Officer) July 1956; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Nicosia (local Senior Executive Officer) August 1960 to July 1963; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963; Port of Spain January 1964.

**Carr-Gregg**, John Ralph Edward; born 10th January 1920; educated Seaford College 1932-38 and Downing College, Cambridge, 1939-40 and 1946-48; 2nd Class
Honours Eng. Lit Tripos 1947; m. 1949 Charlotte Rona (2 s. 1955, 1958); R.A.F. V.R. 1940-46; commissioned 1942; served with No. 139 Wing, 2nd Tactical Air Force in N.W. Europe; nominated by Foreign Office to represent U.K. on 1st United Nations International Intern Programme, Lake Success, July 1948; Editor, Dept. of Public Information, United Nations, 1948-49; News Editor, British Information Services, New York, 1949-52; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th November 1952; Information Officer, Karachi, January 1953; Regional Information Officer, Lahore, October 1954; Regional Information Officer, Melbourne, August 1956; Information Officer 27th November 1957; Senior Information Officer January 1958; Principal Information Officer (local), Melbourne, April 1959; Director of Information Services, Accra, September 1959 to June 1962; Nairobi October 1962; Principal Information Officer (acting) 1st April 1963; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1964; Director of Information Services, Nairobi.

Carter, Peter Antony; born 16th January 1914; educated Charterhouse and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, 1932-35; 2nd Class Honours, Law; m. 1946 Mary Hutchinson (1 d. 1948; 1 s. 1951); Executive Officer, Metropolitan Police Office, 1936-39; 50th Royal Tank Regiment 1939-44; Major; wounded, North Africa; Principal, Colonial Office, 19th April 1947; seconded Nyasaland Government 1951-53; Commonwealth Relations Office 21st November 1960; Dar es Salaam November 1961; Acting Deputy High Commissioner 15th June 1963.

Carville, Mervyn Thornton, MBE (Military) (1945); born 3rd January 1910; educated St. Mark's and Cheetham Grammar School, Manchester; m. 1963 Grace Kathleen Aldons; enlisted Royal Signals 1928; retired with rank of Major 1948; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th July 1948; Delhi July 1948 to July 1951; local Executive Officer 1949 to 1951; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Salisbury August 1953 to August 1956; Colombo June 1957 to June 1959; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

Ceuvorst, Anthony Paul; born 10th July 1935; educated Chatham House Grammar School, Ramsgate; m. Catherine Mary Gilmartin 1959 (2 s. 1960, 1961); Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th March 1956; Delhi 1957-60; Kuala Lumpur February 1961 to May 1964; Higher Executive Officer 26th May 1962; Salisbury August 1964.

Chadwick, Gerald William St. John, CMG (1961); born 28th May 1915; educated Lancing College 1929-34 and St. Catharine's College, Cambridge, (Open Exhibitioner, Modern Languages) 1934-37; 2nd Class Hons. Mod. Languages Parts I and II; BA 1937; m. 1938 Madeleine D'Eguilles (2 s. 1939, 1941); Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 6th October 1938; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State September 1939; following demobilization transferred to Dominions Office as Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 6th June 1940; Assistant Private Secretary to successive Secretaries of State 5th August 1940; Principal (temporary) 1st October 1941; Principal 2nd April 1943; Secretary to Parliamentary Mission to Newfoundland June to September 1943; attended Civil Aviation Conferences, Bermuda, December 1945, Newfoundland, January 1946; visited Newfoundland in connection with Economic and Financial Survey February to May 1946; attached United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations, New York, March to May 1949; Ottawa September 1949 to February 1952; Dublin (Counsellor) February 1952 to August 1953; Assistant Secretary October to December 1953; seconded to United Kingdom Delegation to N.A.T.O., Paris, January 1954 to October 1956; Assistant Secretary 6th December 1954; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 22nd August 1960.

Champion, John Stuart, OBE (1963); born 17th May 1921; educated Shrewsbury 1935-40 and Balliol College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1940-41; 2nd Class Honour Moderations in Lit. Hum.; War BA; m. 1944 Olive Holt (5 s. 1947, 1950, 1954, 1959, 1962; 2 d. 1953, 1956); military service 1941-46; commissioned 11th Hussars (PAO); Western Desert, Tunisia, Italy and N.W. Europe; Cadet, Colonial Administrative Service, Uganda, 1946; District Officer 1948; Assistant Financial Secretary 1956; Deputy Secretary 1959; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Entebbe, 1960-63; retired from Overseas Civil Service August 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

Chandler, Stanley George; born 26th October 1911; educated Prince Albert School, Winnipeg, and Brook Green School, Hammersmith; m. 1939 Miriam Price (1 s. 1945); Sorter, General Post Office, 10th September 1930; Royal Air Force 1940-46; Clerical Officer, Foreign Office (German Section), 8th September 1947; Executive Officer 1st July 1950; Rehabilitation Officer for Control Commission, Germany, July 1950 to December 1953; Commonwealth Relations Office 11th June 1956; Delhi March 1957 to February 1958; Salisbury (local Information Officer) February 1958 to December 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Kuching (local Senior Information Officer) June 1963.*

Chaplin, John Hugh, Air Commodore (retd.), DSO (1942), DFC (1940), Greek Air Force Cross (1941); born 18th June
Biographical Notes

PART V

1911; educated Eastbourne College and Emmanuel College, Cambridge; m. 1939 Simone Lorphévre (3 d. 1940, 1945, 1947; 2 s. 1948, 1961); Commissioned in Royal Air Force 3rd March 1936; served in Flying Boats until 1940; commanded special unit which blew up magnetic mines from the air 1940–41; Commanded R.A.F., Gaza (training Greek pilots); Commanded No. 38 Bomber Squadron, Middle East, October 1941 to June 1942; Middle East Staff College; Combined Naval/Air H.Q. Staff, Alexandria, 1943; Commanded No. 247 Wing near Benghazi (Acting Group-Captain); Commanded R.A.F. Station, Oban, (Flying Boats) January to October 1944; Army and Navy Staff College Course, Washington, November 1944 to June 1945; Directing Staff of Army Staff College, Camberley, August 1945 to December 1947; transport operations, including Berlin air-lift January 1948 to August 1949; Air Ministry (Air Staff Policy Branch) 1949–51; Station Commander, Gütersloh, 1951–52; Air Staff, H.Q., No. 83 Group, 1952–53; Deputy Director (Air Transport), Air Ministry, 1953–56; Senior Officers' War Course, R.N. College, Greenwich, 1956; Air Adviser (Service and Civil) to British High Commissioner, Delhi, 1956–59 (Acting Air Commodore); Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st February 1960; Ottawa April 1960; Temporary Principal Information Officer 16th August 1960; Edmonton August 1960; Assistant Information Officer 14th February 1961; substituting Senior Information Officer 12th September 1961; Information Officer 26th April 1962; Colombo (local Senior Information Officer) July 1963.*

CHEESEMAN, Bernard, OBE (1963); born 31st March 1916; educated Tollington School, Muswell Hill; m. 1942 Dorrien Wolfe (1 d. 1946); Local Government 1936–40; military service 1940–46; commissioned 1941; Staff Captain 1943; Major 1944; served with 1st and 8th Armies in North Africa, Italy and Austria; Mentioned in Despatches; Deputy Librarian, Colonial Office and Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1947; Librarian February 1954; also Librarian of the Department of Technical Cooperation 1961.

CHISHOLM, Ronald George; born 26th January 1910; educated Inverness Royal and Peterhead Academies; m. (1) 1937 Hilda Gray (dec.); (2) 1956 Susan Craik (2 d. 1958, 1961; 1 s. 1959); Clerk, Sheriff Clerk Service, Scottish Home Department, on qualifying in (Scottish) legal subjects, 1929; Sheriff Clerk Depute 1941; Staff College, Camberley, 1939; war service: Battery Commander, Royal Artillery, D.A.Q.M.G., G.H.Q., Home Forces, 1941–43 and G.H.Q., Middle East, 1944–45; Territorial Decoration 1944; Norwegian Decoration 1948; Major; released October 1945; lent to Burma Office as Principal on trial 27th December 1945; transferred as Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th August 1946; Karachi April to September 1951; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, September 1951 to August 1952; Dacca August 1952 to March 1953; on U.K. Delegation to International Sugar Conference 1953, and Volta River Project Conference 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Madras, March 1957 to January 1960; local Assistant Secretary 1st March 1957; Enugu September 1963.

CHITTY, Margaret Beryl; born 2nd December 1917; educated The Belvedere School, Liverpool, 1926–36 and St. Hugh's College, Oxford, 1936–39; 2nd Class Hons. in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; m. 1949 Keith Chitty, FRCs (dec.); Research Assistant to Reader in Colonial Administration, Oxford, 1939–40; Temporary Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd September 1940; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 1943–45; Temporary Principal 1945; resigned 1952; rejoined Commonwealth Relations Office as Temporary Principal 1st October 1958; Principal 8th December 1961; member of Secretariat, Commonwealth Education Conference, Oxford, 1959, and of Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Meeting, March 1961 and September 1962.

CHRISTIE, David Hamilton, VRD (1950); born 25th August 1911; educated privately and Trinity College, Dublin, 1930–35; 1st Class Moderator in History and Political Science; Higher Diploma in Education; Diploma in Geography; MA 1940; m. 1939 Phyllis Percy (1 d. 1947); Colonial Education Service, Malaya, October 1936; commissioned SSRNVR February 1937; war service October 1939 to May 1946; Lieutenant Commander; Headmaster, Kajang High School, 1946, Sultan Abdul Hamid College 1947; Superintendent of Education, Kedah, 1948; Headmaster, King Edward VII School, 1949; Chief Education Officer, Negri Sembilan, 1953, Kedah, 1954, Johore, 1956 and Penang, 1957; Deputy Director of Education and Chief Education Adviser, Federation of Malaya, June 1957; Chief Education Adviser 1959; resigned 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th January 1962; Principal 30th April 1963.

CHUDLEIGH, Derek Brian Lyne; born 13th February 1916; educated Blundell's, Tiverton, 1929–33 and in U.S.A.; m. (1) 1937 Evelyn Andrew-Mathews (dec.); m. (2) 1942 Doris Pilogatti; m. (3) 1949 Phyllis Heber-Jones (1 s. 1950); Editorial Staff, Western Morning News, 1935, News Chronicle, 1937; war service 1940–46;
Commissioned K.R.R.C. 1941; seconded to Army P.R. and later to Intelligence Corps; served in Middle East and East Africa from 1941; joined Near East Arab Broadcasting Station (Palestine) 1945; Editor, N.E.A.B.S., Cyprus, 1948; Public Relations Officer, Cyprus Government, London, 1957; Chief Press Officer, Public Information Office, Nicosia; Temporary Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th August 1960; Director of Information Services, Nicosia, August 1960; Temporary Senior Information Officer 22nd January 1962; Delhi May 1962; Senior Information Officer 24th April 1963.

Church, John; born 8th December 1929; educated Cranbrook School, Kent, 1942–47 and Christ’s College, Cambridge, 1950–53; Modern Languages; MA; m. 1953 Marie-Genevieve Vallette (1 s. 1956; 2 d. 1958, 1963); Army Intelligence Corps 1948–50; Reuters (Liaison Editor between Reuters and the Press Association, etc.) 1953–59; Information Officer, Central Office of Information 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th July 1961; Calcutta August 1961.

Clark, Ellen Elizabeth Nancy; born 14th July 1911; educated Walthamstow Hall, Sevenoaks; Clerical Officer, India Office, 13th August 1928; Executive Officer 23rd April 1941; Salisbury February 1951 to May 1954; Higher Executive Officer 11th May 1951.

Clark, Sir (William) Arthur (Weir), KCMG (1961; CMG 1952), CBE (1948); born 5th December 1908; educated Stewarts College, Edinburgh, 1919–26, Edinburgh University 1923–30 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1930–31; MA (Hon. Classics), Edinburgh; m. 1935 Margaret Dobbie (1 d. 1937; 1 s. 1944); appointed to Colonial Administrative Service July 1931; served in Kenya July 1931 to December 1939; seconded to Dominions Office 1st January 1940; Principal April 1940; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1941; Private Secretary 1942–45; on secretarial staff of Prime Ministers’ Meeting 1944, and on United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations Charter Conference, San Francisco, 1945; Chief Secretary to Central African Council September 1945; Chief Secretary to High Commissioner for Basutoland, Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland November 1948; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office as Assistant Secretary 4th December 1950; transferred 1st August 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 4th December 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, April 1956 to September 1958; United Kingdom Representative, Cyprus, August 1960; High Commissioner in Cyprus March 1961 to April 1964; Director of Information and Cultural Relations June 1964.

Clayden, John Elwyn Sedgwick; born 26th March 1922; educated Hillhead High School, Glasgow, and Raynes Park County School; m. 1942 Anne Biddington (2 s. 1952, 1955); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 26th July 1939; R.A.F. Navigator 1942–46; served in India and Burma 1944–45; Executive Officer 14th November 1947; Wellington January 1950 to February 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st March 1954; accompanied Mr. A. C. B. Symon on special mission to review economic and financial position of High Commission Territories in South Africa April to June 1954; Karachi 6th July 1955 to 27th October 1958; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Secretary to Inter-departmental Committee on Emigration Policy May to November 1961; Delhi 29th September 1962.

Clayton, David Anthony; born 16th October 1929; educated Scarborough High School; Royal Air Force 1947–55; Clerical Officer, Air Ministry, May 1955; Executive Officer March 1958; Air Historical Branch 1958–61; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st January 1962; Colombo April 1963; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Cleary, Denis Mackrow; born 20th December 1907; educated St. Ignatius College 1919–24, St. Olave’s School 1924–27 and St. John’s College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar: Mathematics) 1927–31; First Class Honours Parts I and II Mathematical Tripos; BA 1930; MA 1934; m. (1) 1941 Barbara Wykeham-George (dec. 1960); m. (2) 1962 Mary Kent (née Dunlop) (1 step-d. 1944); Assistant Principal, India Office, 19th October 1931; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 13th August 1936; Principal 11th October 1937; on loan to Ministry of Home Security 26th June 1940 to 27th September 1944; Deputy Principal Officer to Regional Commissioner, Cambridge, March 1943 to September 1944; on loan to Foreign Office (German Section) with rank of Assistant Secretary 28th October 1946 to 19th June 1949; Assistant Secretary, India Office, (in absentia) 2nd March 1948; Delhi July 1949 to August 1951; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, September 1955 to September 1958; member of British Delegation to the Second United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea, Geneva, 1960, and to the Inter-governmental Committee for European Migration, Geneva, 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Nicosia, November 1962 to February 1964; Acting High Commissioner June to October 1963.

Clewley, James Alfred, MBE (1956); born 7th December 1918; educated Brunts School, Mansfield, 1929–36 and Sheffield University 1937–40; First Class Honours Zoology; BSc; m. 1943 Edna Gilbert; Overseas Civil Service, Northern Nigeria, 1941–59; seconded to Royal West African
Frontier Force 1941-46; Brigade Major and G.S.O. 2, General Wingate's 'Chindits'; Second Devonshire Course, Trinity College, Cambridge, 1949-50; seconded Superintendent, Art and Visual Aids Section, and Director, Northern Region Literature Agency, Nigeria, 1952-56; special duties, Royal visits to Nigeria 1956 and 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, and Staff Officer, Commonwealth Exhibition, 7th September 1959; Information Officer (temporary Senior Information Officer) February 1961; Salisbury (local Senior Information Officer) October 1961; Regional Information Officer, Blantyre, October 1963; Director of Information Services, Blantyre, July 1964.*

Coe, William John; born 21st June 1914; educated Owens School, Islington; with Messrs. Lewis Powell Sons & Co., Stockbrokers, 1933-35; Officer of Customs and Excise 30th September 1935 to 31st August 1948; military service, R.A. (Field), May 1942 to November 1946; served in India and West Africa; commissioned May 1943; Major; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1948; Principal 13th July 1949; Bombay March 1952 to May 1954 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay, July to September 1953 and November 1953 to May 1954); Canberra May 1958 to November 1961; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 8th February 1962; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation February 1962 to April 1963; Assistant Secretary (acting) 1st January 1963; Karachi April 1963; Acting Deputy High Commissioner May 1963 to January 1964.

Cole, David Lee, mc (1944); born 31st August 1920; educated Cheltenham College (Scholar) 1934-39 and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, (Classical Exhibitioner and History Scholar) 1939-40 and 1946; 1st Class Honours History; MA; m. 1945 Dorothy Patton (1 s. 1950); served with Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers 1940-45 in Madagascar, India, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, Sicily, Italy and Austria; Captain; Instructor, Army School of Education, C.M.F., 1945; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd January 1947; Dublin August to September 1947; New York and Paris (Permanent United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations) May 1948 to January 1951; Principal 17th July 1950; Delhi September 1953 to September 1956; Private Secretary to Secretary of State January 1957 to June 1960; Assistant Secretary (Temporary) 2nd June 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st July 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Accra, July 1963 to May 1964; Acting High Commissioner August to September 1963 and October 1963 to January 1964; High Commissioner, Malawi, July 1964.

Collett, Leonard, mvo (1961); born 10th August 1910; m. 1936 Hilda Davies (2 d. 1940, 1942; 1 s. 1946); Messenger, G.P.O., September 1924; Postman 8th June 1929; Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist 30th March 1930; Clerical Officer 2nd February 1936; enlisted R.E. (Postal Section) January 1941; commissioned and took command of 2nd Divisional Postal Unit March 1944; Staff Captain, Advance Headquarters, S.E.A.C., 16th March 1945; Mentioned in Despatches; Executive Officer (in absentia) 5th October 1944; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th April 1951; Delhi (local Higher Executive Officer) February 1952; Higher Executive Officer 6th March 1953; Colombo May 1956 to July 1959; Delhi (local Senior Executive Officer) October 1959 to September 1962 Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 1st October 1962; Chief Executive Officer 1st October 1963.

Collins, Geoffrey Gowen; born 16th February 1919; educated Wellington College, Berkshire, and R.M.C., Sandhurst; m. 1954 Patricia Maude Murray; Commissioned Indian Army 26th January 1939; Royal Garhwal Rifles; 2nd in command 1947; transferred to British Army 10th May 1948; Royal Army Ordnance Corps; G.S.O. III, War Office, 1955-56; School of Oriental and African Studies, Middle East Centre for Arabic Studies, Lebanon, 1957; Aden Protectorate Levies 1958-59; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd May 1960; Accra August 1961 to May 1964; Acting Deputy High Commissioner April to May 1962.

Condon, Denis David, obe (1964); born 23rd October 1910; educated Paston Grammar School, North Walsham, Norfolk; m. 1933 Mary Marson (1 d. 1936); war service 1941-45; served in Ceylon, India and Burma; Major; India Office (Editor-in-Chief, British Information Services, Delhi) 16th December 1946; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th November 1951, with seniority from 1st August 1949; Colombo March 1952 to August 1954; Regional Information Officer, Sydney, September 1955; Principal Information Officer (temporary) 1st November 1956, (substantive) 1st December 1957; Director of Information Services (local Chief Information Officer (B)), Canberra, April 1958; Chief Information Officer (B) 1st April 1963; Director of Information Services, Nigeria, February 1964.

Connelly, David; born 23rd February 1930; educated Heath Grammar School, Halifax, 1941-48 and Queen's College, Oxford, 1950-54; 2nd Class Honours Modern Languages 1953; m. 1953 Audrey Grace Salter (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); military service 1949-50; Colonial Service Probationers' Course, Oxford, 1953-54;
Colonial Service and H.M.O.C.S., Tanganyika, 1954-62; Assistant Secretary, University of St. Andrews, 1962-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th June 1963; Delhi April 1964.

Cook, Stanley George; born 24th September 1927; educated St. Olave's 1938-43; m. 1956 Joan Veasy; military service 1945-48; Temporary Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd September 1948; Clerical Officer 30th March 1949; Karachi October 1948 to March 1951; Cape Town August 1952 to September 1955; Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Salisbury February 1957 to October 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963; Lusaka May 1964.

Cooper, Leslie William; born 29th January 1914; educated Bankstown Commercial School, Sydney; m. 1939 Mary Hyland (3 d. 1943, 1945, 1946); Clerk, British Trade Commission, Sydney, 1928-41; Chief Clerk (local), Canberra, 1941-50; Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 1st March 1946; Executive Officer (supernumerary) 30th October 1950; Executive Officer 16th April 1952; Delhi 1953-56; Dublin March 1957 to June 1962; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 22nd August 1960; Higher Executive Officer July 1962; Colombo July 1962.

Cormack, Robert Linklater Burke; born 29th August 1935; educated Trinity College, Glenalmond, and Trinity Hall, Cambridge; BA (Agric.) 1959; m. 1962 Eivor Dorotea Kumlín; National Service 1954-56 (2nd Lieutenant, the Black Watch, British Guiana); HMOCs: District Officer, Kenya, 1960; retired 1964; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 5th March 1964.

Costar, Sir Norman Edgar, KCMBG (1963; CMG 1953); born 18th May 1909; educated Battersea Grammar School 1920-28 and Jesus College, Cambridge, 1928-32; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 21st April 1932; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State, Dominions Office, October 1935 to October 1936; on Staff of Imperial Conference 1937; Canberra October 1937 to November 1939; Principal 14th November 1938; Wellington (Official Secretary) April 1945 to April 1947; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, April to December 1947; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1946; on Secretariat of Prime Ministers' Meeting October 1948, Treasury Mission to Washington August to October 1949 and Conference of Commonwealth Foreign Ministers, Colombo, January 1950; Deputy High Commissioner, Colombo, February 1953 to May 1957; Mission to Maldive Islands December 1956; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st December 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Canberra, October 1960 to July 1962; High Commissioner in Trinidad and Tobago 31st August 1962.

Costley-White, Cyril Grove, CMG (1953); born 30th October 1913; educated Eton 1926-32 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1932-35; 2nd Class Modern Greats (Philosophy, Politics and Economics); BA; Civil Service Course, London School of Economics, 1935-37; m. (1) 1938 Elizabeth Delmore (2 s. 1939, 1946; 1 d. 1942); m. (2) 1955 Elisabeth Chard (2 s. 1956, 1961); Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 4th October 1937; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Colonies 5th May 1939; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State for Colonies 4th December 1939; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State for Dominion Affairs 6th May 1940; Principal August 1940; Ottawa October 1941 to June 1944; Wellington July 1944 to September 1946; Assistant Secretary (temporary) May 1947; Assistant Secretary 3rd March 1949; Deputy High Commissioner, Colombo, March 1949 to October 1950.

Counsell, Edward Hugh Michael, CBE (1962); born 4th October 1908; educated St. Bees School 1921-27 and The Queen's College, Oxford; 2nd Class Honours Modern History; m. 1947 Barbara Malet (3 s. 1949, 1952, 1962); Colonial Administrative Service 1931; Nigeria 1931-62; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 20th August 1962; Calcutta November 1962.

Cox, Richard Charles, MBE (1961); born 27th May 1920; educated Gravesend County Grammar School 1931-37; m. 1941 Constance Goddard (1 s. 1953); Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 25th June 1937; joined R.A.F. June 1940; commissioned 1941; Squadron Leader October 1943; served in Egypt, Palestine, Syria, Libya, Tripolitania, Tunisia and Italy; Higher Clerical Officer (in absentia) 1st December 1944; Dominions Office July 1946; Colombo January 1950 to January 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1951; Calcutta January 1953 to February 1954; Bombay April 1956 to August 1959; Senior Executive Officer (local) April 1956; Senior Executive Officer 13th May 1959; Principal 19th March 1962; staff of United Kingdom Commissioner, Malta, August 1964.

Crane, Marjorie Eva; born 10th December 1918; educated School of the Sacred Heart, New Malden, and Wimbledon Day Commercial School for Girls; Telephonist, Clerical Assistant, London Telecommunications Region, January 1936; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 5th September 1949; Canberra January 1951 to December 1953; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Cape Town May 1955 to June 1958; Nicosia August 1960 to
September 1963; Higher Executive Officer (local) April 1961; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

CRAWLEY, Desmond John Chetwode, CMG (1964), CVO (1961); born 2nd June 1917; educated Kings' School, Ely, 1932-35 and Queen's College, Oxford, 1935-39; 2nd Class Honours Modern History; BA; m. 1945 Daphne Mockett (1 d. 1946; 2 s. 1949, 1955); Indian Civil Service 1938-47; served in Madras Presidency; seconded to Indian Political Service in 1946 and served as Political Agent in Baluchistan; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd August 1947; Madras and Calcutta September 1947 to April 1950; local Principal 6th July 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 18th February 1952; seconded to Foreign Office, and posted to British Embassy, Washington, 14th September 1953 to September 1955; Assistant Secretary 29th August 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, 1958-61; Imperial Defence College 1962; High Commissioner in Sierra Leone September 1963.

CRITCHLEY, Kenneth Mackay; born 14th July 1926; educated Preston Grammar School; m. 1950 Olwen Bretherton (2 s. 1957, 1959); Executive Officer, Ministry of Pensions, 13th October 1947; Higher Executive Officer 20th September 1950; loaned to Organisation and Methods Division, Treasury, January 1953; Senior Executive Officer 19th August 1955; returned to Ministry of Pensions and National Insurance September 1958; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st February 1960; Lagos April 1960 to March 1963; Chief Executive Officer 19th March 1962; Principal 22nd July 1964.

CROMBIE, George Edmond, CMG (1950); born 14th June 1908; educated Aberdeen Grammar School 1916-21, Fettes College, Edinburgh, 1921-26 and Aberdeen University 1926-31; 1st Class Honours Classics; MA; Assistant Principal, India Office, 19th October 1931; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 24th October 1935, and to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 13th August 1936; Principal 1st April 1937; resigned to take up military service 26th May 1942; commissioned in Frontier Force Regiment, Indian Army, and served in India, Middle East and Italy; Mentioned in Despatches; Lieutenant; re-instated as Principal 2nd May 1945; Assistant Secretary 1st March 1947; on deputation to Burma June 1947; Deputy High Commissioner, Rangoon, September 1947; Counsellor, British Embassy, Rangoon, January 1948 to March 1950; Deputy High Commissioner, Madras, June 1951 to September 1953; Ottawa October 1955 to June 1957; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur, November 1959 to November 1960; Counsellor, Dublin, January 1961.

CROOK, Kenneth Roy; born 30th July 1920; educated Prescot Grammar School, Lancs, and Skerry's College, Liverpool; m. 1943 Freda Vidler (2 d. 1946, 1950); Clerical Officer, Board of Trade, 30th August 1937; lent to Ministry of War Transport 29th August 1939; enlisted as signalman in Royal Navy March 1941; served in Malta, Egypt, Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and South Africa September 1941 to February 1943; commissioned June 1943; Lieutenant; released August 1946; Executive Officer, Board of Trade, 29th July 1946; Higher Executive Officer 27th July 1948; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th January 1949; Canberra February 1951 to January 1954; Principal 1st December 1952; Madras February 1956 to February 1959; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, September 1962 to May 1964; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, May 1964.

CROSTHWAIT, Timothy Leland, CMG (1964), MBE (1944); born 5th August 1915; educated Wellington College 1928-33 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1933-37; Natural Sciences and Mechanical Sciences Tripos 2nd Class Honours; m. 1959 Anne Penney; Indian Civil Service 1937; Sind 1938-42; Assistant Private Secretary to Viceroy 1942-44; Bombay 1944-47; temporary appointment, Delhi, August to December 1947; Assistant Principal and Principal, Air Ministry, 1948-55; Commonwealth Relations Office 12th September 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Colombo, May 1957 to August 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st December 1958; High Commissioner in Zanzibar, December 1963 to June 1964; Deputy High Commissioner, Zanzibar, June to August 1964; N.A.T.O. Defence College, Paris, September 1964 to January 1965.

CUMINGS, Robert Frank; born 17th December 1931; educated Glyndebourne County Grammar School, Epsom, 1942-48; m. 1961 Jane Francis (1 d. 1962); Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd August 1948; National Service, R.A.F., 1950-52; Executive Officer 19th June 1953; Canberra February 1955 to March 1958; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Madras October 1962.

CUMMING-BRUCE, the Hon. Sir Francis Edward Hovell-Thurlow, KCMG (1961; CMG 1957); born 9th March 1912; educated Shrewsbury School 1925-30 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1931-34 and April to July 1935; 1st Class Honours Part I Classics, 2nd Class Part II Economics; BA June 1934; m. 1949 Yvonne Wilson (2 s. 1952, 1962; 2 d. 1954, 1958); Assistant Principal, Department of Agriculture for Scotland, 4th November 1935; Dominions Office 24th May 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st June 1939; Wellington August 1939 to May 1944; Principal

30th October 1941; Ottawa June 1944 to August 1945; Secretariat, Meeting of Prime Ministers, London, April 1946; served with United Kingdom Delegation at Paris Peace Conference 1946 and at United Nations General Assemblies 1945 and 1948; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st October 1946; Assistant Secretary 12th December 1948; Delhi November 1949 to June 1952; Establishment Officer 1952 to 1954; Adviser on External Affairs to Governor of Gold Coast 9th February 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, April 1958 to September 1959; High Commissioner in New Zealand February 1960 to 1963; High Commissioner in Nigeria February 1964.

CURSON, Bernard Robert; born 14th November 1913; educated University College School, London, 1925-30; m. 1949 Miriam Johnson (1 s. 1950); Clerical Officer, India Office, 23rd June 1930; Executive Officer 30th May 1940; Assistant Principal 1st January 1941; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State for India 30th August 1943; Principal 6th July 1944; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations during following periods: New York October to December 1946, September to December 1947, January to April 1948, January 1949 and April to May 1949, Paris September to December 1948; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 13th December 1948; with United Kingdom delegation to United Nations November 1949 to April 1950; Colombo August 1950 to August 1952; Assistant Secretary 19th August 1952; United Kingdom delegation to United Nations Wheat Conference, Geneva, February to March 1956; United Kingdom delegation to Colombo Plan Consultative Committee Meeting, Wellington, November to December 1956, and Saigon, October 1957; Asian Nuclear Centre Working Group, Washington, July 1957; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, April 1958; Toronto August 1960 to June 1964.

CUTHBERTSON, George Hendry Brown; born 31st October 1918; m. 1943 Joyce Horswell (2 d. 1946, 1951; 1 s. 1948); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, General Post Office, 1937; war service, Royal Signals, September 1939 to April 1946; returned to General Post Office April 1946; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th July 1948; Executive Officer 24th May 1951; Dublin March 1953 to March 1957; Ottawa September 1958 to November 1961; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 4th July 1960; Higher Executive Officer 1st December 1960.

D

DALE, William Leonard, CMG (1951); born 17th June 1906; educated Hymers College, Hull; Barrister 1931; practised in London and on North-Eastern Circuit; Assistant Legal Adviser, Colonial and Dominions Offices, 1935; Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Supply (on loan), 1940 to 1945; Deputy Legal Adviser, Colonial and Commonwealth Relations Offices, 1945; accompanied Rajah Brooke on cession of Sarawak 1946; Legal Adviser, United Kingdom of Libya (on loan), 1951 to 1953; Legal Adviser, Ministry of Education, 1954 to 30th June 1964 and Commonwealth Relations Office from 1961; member of United Kingdom delegation to UNESCO 1960 and 1962; member, Law Advisory Committee, British Council, and Council of Management, British Institute of International and Comparative Law.

DALGLEISH, Margaret Lamb, MBE (1948); born 4th March 1907; educated John Street Secondary School, Glasgow, and Skerry's College; Typist, Board of Trade, 14th July 1930; Shorthand-Typist April 1932; Clerical Officer August 1937; Executive Officer October 1942; Private Secretary to Second Secretary (Overseas) 1942 and accompanied him on missions to Washington 1943 and 1945 and to Brazil, Argentine and Paris 1946; Private Secretary to Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Food, July 1946 and accompanied him to Ottawa 1947; Higher Executive Officer 1st April 1947; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st January 1949 to February 1955 and accompanied him to Commonwealth Foreign Ministers' Conference, Ceylon, 1950; Senior Executive Officer 29th January 1954; Resident Clerk November 1956 to February 1957; Chief Executive Officer 6th July 1960.

d'ARNAUD-TAYLOR, Gilbert; born 22nd June 1916; educated Robert Gordon's College, Aberdeen; m. 1940 Patricia Stephenson (2 s. 1941, 1946); on staff Madras Mail 1936-41 and 1946-48; Daily Mirror, London, 1948-49; joined Royal Indian Army Service Corps; served Eritrea, Abyssinia, Egypt and N.W. Frontier of India; Central Office of Information 4th July 1949; Temporary Senior Executive Officer (later Temporary Senior Information Officer) as Editor, Packin Service; Commonwealth Relations Office 14th February 1954; British Information Services, Delhi, as Editor-in-Chief 1954; Regional Information Officer, Delhi, May 1958; Information Officer 8th January 1958; local Senior Information Officer 8th January 1958; Regional Information Officer, Madras, April to August 1960; Lagos October 1960; Regional Information Officer (local Principal Information Officer) Kaduna, November 1960 to August 1963; Lahore (local Principal Information Officer) November 1963.

DARVALL, Frank Ongley, CBE (1954); born 16th April 1906; educated Dover College 1920-23 and Universities of Reading 1923-27 (1st Class Honours History;
BA), London (BA and PhD) and Colombia, New York, 1929-31 (Commonwealth Fund Fellow; MA); m. 1931 Dorothy Edmonds (1 s. dec.); Assoc. Sec., International Studies Dept., International Students Service, 1931-32; Director, Geneva Students International Union, 1933; Extension Lecturer in International Affairs, Cambridge and London Universities, 1933-39; Deputy Director, America Division, Ministry of Information, 1939-45; British Consul, Denver, 1945-46; established as Principal with seniority from 1940; First Secretary and Head of Reports Division, H.B.M. Embassy, Washington, 1946-49; resigned from the Civil Service 1949; Director-General, English-Speaking Union of the Commonwealth, 1949-57; Director, U.K. National Committee for the Atlantic Congress, 1958-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th July 1960; Nicosia August 1960; Senior Information Officer 15th March 1962; Acting Director, British Information Services, Cyprus, December 1961 to May 1962; Director, British Information Services, Trinidad, (local Principal Information Officer) August 1962.

D'Astugues, André Robert; born 16th September 1916; educated Newquay County School; m. 1947 Patricia Dorothy Kesby (2 s. 1949, 1952; 1 d. 1958); reporter on several papers 1934-39; war service in both British and French armies (Croix de Guerre, Medaille Coloniale); French Resistance, S.O.E., Force 136 (Laos); War Crimes Investigation (Indo-China, Burma and N.W. Europe); Army Public Relations (Hamburg, Berlin); reporter Daily Mirror 1948, Star 1949; bulletin editor, B.B.C. Foreign News, 1950; Head, Press Division, Federation of Malaya Information Services, 1950 to January 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1959; Senior Information Officer 9th March 1960; Freetown April to June 1961; Canberra August 1961; Principal Information Officer (local) April 1963.

Davey, Frank Herbert, OBE (1960), FCA; born 9th August 1900; educated City of London School; m. 1925 Dorothy Elvidge (1 d. 1929); Article to Chartered Accountant 1916; served in Artists Rifles 1918-19; admitted as a Chartered Accountant February 1922; Professional Accountant, Board of Trade (Companies (Winding-up) Department), June 1924; Accountant, Public Trustee Office, July 1925; Senior Accountant, Custodian of Enemy Property Department, September 1939; Finance Officer (Chief Executive Officer), General Register Office, September 1946; Assistant Accountant-General, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th November 1954; Deputy Accountant-General 1st April 1955; Accountant-General 7th August 1959.

Davidson, James Alford; born 22nd March 1922; educated Christ's Hospital and Royal Naval College, Dartmouth; m. 1955 Daphne Merritt (2 step-s. 1946, 1953; 2 d. 1956, 1962); Midshipman 1939; Lieutenant 1942; Lieutenant Commander 1950; Commander 1955; retired April 1960; Barrister at Law (Middle Temple) February 1960; Certificate of Service as Master Mariner March 1960; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th May 1960; Port of Spain September 1962.

Davies, Kenneth Charles Francis; born 25th October 1912; educated Lord Weymouth's School, Warminster; m. 1941 Ella Cookson (1 s. 1944); Newspaper work with South Coast Group, Berrows Ltd. (Worcester) and Kemsley Group morning, evening and weekly papers 1932-39 and 1945-49; military service 1939-45; Commissioned in Intelligence Corps; Major; Inter-Services Security Directorate, Delhi, 1945; Temporary Senior Executive Officer, Central Office of Information, Birmingham, 1948; Senior Information Officer August 1948; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office January 1950; Wellington February 1950 to September 1954; Regional Information Officer, Calcutta, September 1954 to March 1958; reverted to Central Office of Information June 1958; Principal Information Officer September 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office February 1964; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Karachi, March 1964.

Davies, Robert Henry, MBE (1962), DFC (1943); born 17th August 1921; educated John Bright Grammar School, Llandudno, 1932-40; m. 1945 Marion Ainsworth (1 d. 1946; 1 s. 1948); enlisted in R.A.F. in 1940; served in Southern Rhodesia, South Africa and Middle East; released, Flight Lieutenant, April 1946; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1946; Executive Officer 1947; Higher Executive Officer November 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th February 1954; Delhi September 1954 to December 1957; Senior Executive Officer 13th May 1959; Ottawa August 1959 to July 1962; Chief Executive Officer 7th August 1962.

Davies, Vincent Ellis, OBE (1946); born 3rd June 1903; educated St. John's, Leatherhead, and Peterhouse, Cambridge, (Scholar); m. 1939 Rose Trench Temple (3 s. 1940, 1941, 1948; 1 d. 1944); Indian Civil Service 1926-48: served in Bihar and Orissa; in business 1949-51; Colonial Service 1953-59: Federation of Malaya, Singapore and The Gambia; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th January 1960.

Dawson, (née Cox), Lady Winifred Lucy, MBE (1936); born 23rd June 1906; educated Clapham County School 1917-22; m. 1957 Sir Vernon Dawson, KCIE (dec. 1958); Typist, India Office, 17th May
