Hum. 1958; MA; m. 1962 Rosalind Fraser; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th September 1958; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State July 1960 to June 1961 and to Joint Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State June 1961 to March 1962; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State March 1962 to January 1964; Principal (acting) 23rd September 1964.

GILMOUR, Alan James; born 2nd May 1911; educated Ellesmere College and University College, London; Editorial Services Ltd. 1935; Royal Tank Regiment 1939–45; served in North Africa and Italy; London Press Exchange, 1946; Press Office, Ministry of Works, June 1950; Assistant Information Officer, Board of Trade, July 1954; Information Officer, Ministry of Education, January 1955; Senior Information Officer, Scottish Office, (in charge London Press Office) April 1956; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Dar es Salaam, March 1958, Director December 1959, and Zanzibar January 1960; Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th December 1961; Director, British Information Office, Dar es Salaam, December 1961; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Delhi, February 1964.

GOLDS, Anthony Arthur, MVO (1961); born 31st October 1919; educated King's School, Macclesfield, 1930–38 and New College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1938–39 and 1946–48; Honours School of English; m. 1944 Suzanne Young (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1952); enlisted in ranks of York and Lancaster Regiment 1939; commissioned June 1940; R.A.C. 1941–46; served in India 1941–44; Interpreter, German P.O.W. Camp, 1945–46; Lieutenant; released May 1946; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st July 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 20th September 1949; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State
20th March 1950; Principal 14th April 1951; Calcutta and Delhi April 1951 to July 1953; seconded to Foreign Service and posted to Ankara as First Secretary January 1957; Head of Chancery August 1957 to January 1959; Karachi May 1959 to June 1961; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 24th April 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963.

GOLDSMITH, Alexander Kinglake; born 16th January 1938; educated Sherborne 1951-55 and Trinity College, Oxford, (Minor Scholar in History) 1958-61; National Service 1956-58; seconded from D.C.L.I. to Queen's Own Nigeria Regiment; 2nd Lieutenant; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; training course in Indian Affairs, School of Oriental and African Studies, October 1962; Delhi August 1963.

GOODMAN, Douglas Wickham; born 26th November 1922; educated Wanstead County High School 1932-39; m. 1950 Ann Fuller (1 d. 1962); Clerical Officer, India Office, 10th May 1939; enlisted R.A.F. September 1941; Telecommunications Research Establishment 1943-46; released August 1946; Executive Officer 3rd February 1947 (subsequently seniority from 1st January 1946); Wellington June 1951 to January 1955; Higher Executive Officer 15th June 1955; Karachi July 1955 to April 1959; Senior Executive Officer 22nd August 1961.

GORDON-SMITH, David Gerard; born 6th October 1925; educated Rugby School 1939-43 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1943-4 and 1947-48; 2nd Class Hon. Jurisprudence; m. 1952 Angela Kirkpatrick Pile (1 d. 1958; 1 s. 1961); Royal Navy March 1944 to October 1946 as T/Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; called to the Bar, Inner Temple, 1949; Legal Assistant, Colonial Office, 1st August 1950; Senior Legal Assistant 1st January 1954; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th September 1963.

GORE, Michael Edward John; born 20th September 1935; educated Xaverian College, Brighton, 1948-52; m. 1957 Monica Marina Shellish (2 d. 1958, 1960); Member, Institute of Public Relations; general reporter, Evening News, Portsmouth, 1952-55; National Service 1955; Short Service Commission, General List, for Army Public Relations Service, 1956; Staff Captain, Public Relations, Security Forces, Cyprus, 1956-59; Temporary Information Officer, Air Ministry, 1959; Deputy Command Information Officer, Middle (later Near) East Air Force, 1960-63; Information Officer February 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th June 1963; Jesselton August 1963.

GORE-BOOTH, Sir Paul Henry, KCMG (1957; CMG 1949), KCVO (1961); born 3rd February 1909; educated Eton and Balliol College, Oxford; m. 1940 Patricia Mary Ellerton (2 s.; 2 d.); appointed a Third Secretary, Foreign Office, 12th October 1933; Vienna April 1936; Tokyo December 1937; Second Secretary 12th October 1938; Shanghai October to November 1941; Washington December 1942; First Secretary 1st November 1943; member of the United Kingdom Delegation to International Food Conference, Hot Springs, 1943; U.N.R.R.A. Conference, Atlantic City, 1943; Dumbarton Oaks Conversations, Washington, and International Civil Aviation Conference, Chicago, 1944; San Francisco Conference 1945; Foreign Office 25th October 1945; Secretary to the United Kingdom Delegation to the First Meeting of the United Nations General Assembly, London, January 1946; Counsellor and Head of Refugee and United Nations Economic and Social Departments 1st July 1947; Head of European Recovery Department February 1948; Director of British Information Services in the U.S.A. 21st October 1949; Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Rangoon, 6th November 1953; Deputy Under-Secretary of State, Foreign Office, in charge of economic affairs 15th October 1956; High Commissioner in India October 1960.

GORHAM, Robin Stuart; born 15th February 1939; educated Sutton County Grammar School 1950-57 and Oriel College, Oxford, 1958-61; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; Resident Clerk December 1961 to September 1962; Ottawa November 1962 to 1964.

GRANT, Kenneth; born 14th April 1933; educated Woodside School, Glasgow; m. 1960 Irene Mary Veronica Bluett (3 d. 1961, 1962, 1964); National Service 1952 to 1954; British Railways 1954-55; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th May 1955; Accra October 1957 to January 1959; Executive Officer 1st March 1960; Calcutta November 1960 to February 1963; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

GRATTAN, Patrick Henry; born 19th November 1942; educated Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, 1961-64; Second Class Honours in History; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1964.

GREATOREX, Cecil Ernest, MBE; born 2nd January 1920; educated English School, Cairo, Victoria College, Alexandria, and American University, Cairo; m. 1941 Regina Mary Savides (1 d. 1943); Société Egyptienne des Industres Textiles 1938-40; Commissioned 1941; Special Services, Libyan Arab Force, 1942; Civil and Political Affairs Officer, Cyrenaica, 1943-44; Staff Major, Political Affairs, Cyrenaica
and Tripolitania, 1945-47; Political Liaison Officer to King Idris of Libya 1944-47; Political Affairs Officer, Civil Affairs Agency, Cairo, 1947-48; Political Liaison Officer to Chief Administrator, Tripolitania, 1948-52; Temporary Second Secretary, British Embassy, Libya, 1952-55; First Secretary 1955-56; First Secretary, Foreign Office, 1956-58; Principal Information Officer, Colonial Office, October 1958; Enugu October 1958 to December 1961; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; local Senior Information Officer (Acting Principal Information Officer); Information Officer 20th February 1961; Regional Information Officer, Lahore, April 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner May to August 1963; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Dar es Salaam, December 1963.

GREENHILL, Basil Jack; born 26th February 1920; educated Bristol Grammar School 1932-38 and Bristol University 1938-40 and 1945-46 (T. H. Green Scholar in Modern Studies); Philosophy and Economics Honours Class II Division I 1946; BA; m. (1) 1950 Gillian Stratton (dec. 1959) (1 s. 1955); m. (2) 1961 Ann Giffard (1 s. 1964); enlisted R.N.V.R. August 1941; commissioned October 1942; transferred to Air Branch May 1943; Lieutenant (A); on staff of Director of Naval Air Radio, Admiralty, June 1944; released October 1945; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd September 1946; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 13th May 1948, to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 23rd September 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Dacca, Karachi and Peshawar August 1950 to February 1954; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, between November 1952 and April 1953; member of United Kingdom Delegation to 9th Session of United Nations General Assembly in New York 1954; seconded to Foreign Service and posted to British Embassy, Tokyo, April 1955 to March 1958; member of the United Kingdom Delegation to the United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea, Geneva, 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, May 1958 to December 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st December 1958; Ottawa, September 1961 to August 1964.

GRIER, Patrick Arthur, OBE (1963); born 2nd December 1918; educated Lancing College 1932-35, Lausanne University 1935-36 and King's College, Cambridge, 1936-39; BA 1939; MA 1946; m. 1946 Anna Fraembs (1 d. 1962); military service 1939-47; Major R.A.; served with Indian Mountain Artillery, NWFP and Burma; Kreis Resident Officer of Mönchen-Gladbach (Military Government of Germany) 1946-47; Nigerian Administrative Service 1947; Administrative Officer Class III 1952; Clerk to Executive Council, Northern Nigeria, 1953-54; seconded to West African Inter-territorial Secretariat, Accra, for Anglo-French liaison 1955-57; Administrative Officer Class II, Northern Nigeria, 1958; Principal Assistant Secretary to Governor of Northern Nigeria 1959-63; Administrative Officer Class I 1960; retired from H.M.O.C.S. 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th May 1963; Canberra March 1964.

GRIEVE, Walter Fraser; born 30th April 1913; educated Merchiston Castle School, Edinburgh, Edinburgh University and Clare College, Cambridge; Historical Tripos Parts I and II Class II Division I; BA 1934; m. 1949 Patricia Mary Alston-Roberts-West (1 s. 1955); Publishing and Journalism 1934-39; Fire Service, London and India, 1939-43; Royal Indian Engineers, India, Burma and B.M.A., Malaya, 1943-46; Captain: Malayan Civil Service June 1946; Secretary to Ministry of Works, Posts and Telecommunications 1955; retired under Malayanisation scheme June 1961; Indian Tea Association 1961-62; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 20th January 1964; Dar es Salaam February 1964.

GRIFFITH, Owen Glyn, MVO (1954); born 19th January 1922; educated Oundle School 1936-40 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, 1940-41; m. 1949 Rosemary Earl (2 s. 1957, 1959); military service, Welsh Guards, 1941-43; served in Algeria and Tunisia 1942; wounded; released in November 1943; District Officer, Uganda, 1944-51; Assistant Secretary 1951-52; Private Secretary to Governor 1952-54; District Commissioner 1954-61; Permanent Secretary, Uganda Ministry of Commerce and Industry (later Economic Affairs), 1961-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

GROVE, Harold John; born 22nd August 1915; educated Alleyn's School, Dulwich, 1924-32; m. 1956 Irene Arbon (2 d. 1957, 1960); Royal Corps of Signals 1940; served in North Russia, France, Belgium and Holland; released 1946; Clerical Officer, Burma Office, 2nd December 1946; Executive Officer 24th September 1951; Calcutta November 1952 to February 1956; Salisbury August 1959 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer (local) August 1959; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Zomba July 1964.

GRUBB, Geoffrey Harold; born 3rd February 1930; educated Salt High School, Yorkshire, 1940-48; m. 1953 Pamela Betts (3 d. 1955, 1958, 1961); Executive Officer, Colonial Office, September 1948; H.M. Forces October 1948 to June 1950; Higher Executive Officer, Colonial Office, 6th March 1956; seconded to Western
Region of Nigeria as Private Secretary to the Governor January 1959 to November 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 13th February 1961; Nairobi December 1963 to June 1964; Mombasa June 1964; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 14th August 1964.

GWINNETT, Frank Edward; born 17th August 1915; educated Salisbury School and East Kildonan High School, Winnipeg, Canada; m. 1946 Joan Adeline Smith (1 d. 1947); Gloucester Regiment 1936–40; R.A.S.C. 1940–46; Warrant Officer Class I; served in India, Burma and North-West Germany; Temporary Clerk II, India Office, 19th February 1946; Clerical Officer 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

HALL, Alfred Charles; born 2nd August 1917; educated Oratory School and Polytechnic, London; m. 1946 Clara Strunina (5 s. 1946, 1954, 1956, 1959, 1963); London County Council 1937; war service 1939–41; Foreign Office: Temporary Secretary, North Africa, Saudi-Arabia, Iran and U.S.S.R., 1942–46; Press and Information Officer, London County Council, 1946–49; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office (Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Ottawa) 16th August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary Principal Information Officer) with effect from 1st August 1949; Principal Information Officer 1st May 1953; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, August 1955; Deputy Director, British Information Services, India, December 1956 to 1960; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Services, Nigeria, 1960–63; Director, British Information Services, Nigeria, (local Chief Information Officer (B) June 1961; Chief Information Officer (BI) (temporary) June 1963; Director of Information Services, Australia, January 1964.

HALL, Harold Percival, CMG (1963), MBE (1947); born 9th September 1913; educated Royal Military College, Sandhurst; m. 1939 Margery Dickson (twin s. 1940; 1 s. 1943); Indian Army 1933–37 and 1939–43; Indian Political Service 1937–39 and 1943–47; Principal, Colonial Office, 1947; Assistant Secretary 1955; Office of the United Kingdom Commissioner-General for South-East Asia: North Borneo and Sarawak 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th September 1963; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuching, September 1963.

HALL, Ralph Issott; born 11th October 1903; educated Mill Hill School; m. 1941 Phyllis Spencer (1 s. 1945); on staff of Civil and Military Gazette, Lahore, 1923–31; sub-editor, Times of India, 1937; joined Royal Indian Naval Volunteer Reserve in 1939 as Paymaster-Lieutenant and called up 3rd September 1939; released for service as Information Officer, Government of India, April 1940; Assistant Press Adviser, Government of India, November 1941 to October 1942; Deputy Director of Information, Government of Bombay, October 1942 to April 1946; deputy News Editor, Times of India, June to November 1946; Press Officer (Specialist), India Office, 2nd December 1946; Senior Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer, Melbourne, August 1959; local Principal Information Officer 4th July 1959; Principal Information Officer April 1964.

HALL, Wilfrid Edward; born 11th March 1911; Bermuda 1934–40; military service 1939–46; Ghana (Gold Coast) 1947–57; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th February 1958; Lahore March 1958; Rawalpindi November 1959; Chittagong October 1961; Colombo March 1962 to August 1963; Dar es Salaam (local Senior Information Officer) June 1964.

HALLILEY, Alec Addison, MBE; born 19th January 1912; educated Christ's Hospital, Royal Military College, Sandhurst, and St. Andrews University 1948–51; 1st Class Honours, School of History; m. 1943 Rosemary Constance Campbell Ogilvie (2 s. 1944, 1952; 1 d. 1945); Indian Army 1936–48 (acting Lieutenant-Colonel); Senior Lecturer, Department of Modern Subjects, Royal Military Academy, Sandhurst, 1951–55; Head of Department 1955–61; Head of Planning and Research Unit (Senior Research Officer), Commonwealth Relations Office, (seconded from War Office) 23rd May 1961; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 1st February 1964.

HAMILTON, William Aitken Brown, CMG (1950); born 3rd June 1909; educated Aberdeen Grammar School and Aberdeen University; 1st Class Honours Classics 1931; MA; m. 1936 Barbara Gano (1 s. 1948); Assistant Principal, Board of Education, 2nd November 1931; Private Secretary to Permanent Secretary 1st August 1934; Principal 19th October 1936; Assistant Public Relations Officer 3rd November 1936; Publicity Officer 18th May 1937; Principal, Physical Recreation Committees, 1st June 1937; Joint Secretary to Committee on Nursing Services 4th December 1937; on loan to Ministry of Food 25th October 1939; Head of Division 1st July 1942; Assistant Secretary 1st November 1943; returned to Ministry of Education 1st November 1944; Under-Secretary and Director of Establishments 1st November 1946; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (Director of Establishments and Organisation), Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1949; seconded to United Nations as Director of Personnel March 1959 to April 1962.
HAMMETT, Harold George; born 2nd August 1906; educated St. Olave's 1918-25 and Clare College, Cambridge, 1925-28; Classical Tripos Part I Class II; History Tripos Part II Class II; BA 1928; m. (1) 1936 Daphne Margaret Vowler (1 s. 1937); m. (2) 1947 Natalie Moira Sherratt (1 d. 1949; 1 s. 1953); Malayan Civil Service 1929-57; served in Federated Malay States (Selangor and Negri Sembilan), Straits Settlements (Malacca, Penang and Singapore) and Unfederated Malay States (Johore, Kedah and Kelantan); commissioned R.A.F. February 1942; P.O.W. (Sumatra) 1942-45; retired from post of Resident Commissioner, Malacca, on Merdeka (Independence) Day 31st August 1957; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th November 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, July 1964.

HAMPSHIRE, George Peter, CMG (1963); born 1st December 1912; educated Repton and Oriel College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hon. Mods. and 2nd Class Lit. Hum.; m. 1956 Eve Buhler; Assistant Principal, War Office, 24th October 1935; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 12th February 1937; Principal 19th June 1939; Assistant Secretary, Control Office for Germany and Austria, 1st January 1946; Foreign Office, German Section, April 1947; Treasury September 1948; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office (Secretary, Finance, Ottawa) September 1948 to June 1951; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 16th July 1951; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, February 1953 to March 1955; Imperial Defence College 1956; seconded to Foreign Service and posted as Counsellor, Buenos Aires, August 1957 to February 1960; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st July 1961; Director of Establishments and Organisation 1st October 1962.

HANBURY, Clement John; born 15th October 1913; educated Monmouth 1925-31; m. 1937 Joan Bull (1 d. 1944); Assistant Clerk, Lydney Guardians Committee, 1932-37; Assistant Estates Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1937-40; Relieving Officers Certificate, Poor Law Examination Board, 1939; County District Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1940-42; enlisted Royal Armoured Corps May 1942; commissioned, Royal Army Service Corps, April 1943; Captain; released October 1946; Battery Commander, Royal Artillery, Territorial Army, 1949-53; County District Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1946-48; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, July 1948; Headquarters Auditor 1953-56; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th April 1956; Delhi November 1957; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 1st September 1961; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962; Canberra June 1964.

HAND, Ronald Richard; born 24th February 1924; educated Epsom Grammar School; m. 1954 Nancy Irene Oliver (1 s. 1960; 1 d. 1961); R.A.F. 1942-46; Clerical Officer, India Office, 10th December 1946; Delhi July 1949 to February 1953; Executive Officer 25th July 1953; Karachi July 1955 to July 1957; Peshawar April 1959 to April 1961; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Jamaica January 1963.

HANKINS, Muriel, MBE (1961); born 5th October 1924; educated Mary Datchelor Girls' School, Camberwell, and Municipal College, Bournemouth; Clerk, Woolwich Borough Council, January 1942; Temporary Clerk, India Office, February 1944 to August 1946; re-engaged 10th March 1947; Clerical Assistant 24th May 1948; Clerical Officer 22nd July 1949; Executive Officer 31st December 1955; Salisbury 1956; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

HANWELL, Reginald Thomas; born 24th November 1906; m. 1940 Rose Ersser; Messenger, G.P.O., 8th January 1921; Sorter 17th June 1925; Clerical Officer, India Office, 21st January 1935; Higher Clerical Officer 7th December 1945; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

HARRIS, Anthony David; born 13th October 1941; educated Plymouth College 1952-60 and Exeter College, Oxford, (Exhibitioner) 1960-64; 2nd Class Honours in Lit. Hum.; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1964.

HARRISON, Francis Anthony Kitchener; born 28th August 1914; educated Winchester and New College, Oxford; Classical Honour Mods. Class I; Lit. Hum. Class II; MA; m. 1955 Sheila Stevenson (2 s. 1956, 1960; 1 d. 1957); Assistant Principal, India Office, 1st November 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 17th February 1941; Principal 30th August 1943; Delhi September 1949 to September 1951; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st January 1954, (substantive) 7th November 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, 31st March 1956 to 24th August 1959; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, August 1961 to August 1964.

HAWKINS, George Henry; born 15th May 1921; educated Greenwich Central School, London, 1932-37; m. 1943 Helen Adams (2 d. 1945, 1955; 1 s. 1949); volunteered and enlisted Royal Navy June 1940; served as Radar Operator, North Atlantic and Malta convoy escort duty, March 1941 to March 1942; attached R.A.F. for liaison duties April to September 1942; seconded to Royal Norwegian Navy, Coastal Forces Group, for special operations against enemy-occupied Norway, January to October 1943; Instructor, R.N. Training Establishment (Radar), November 1943 to March 1946;
released March 1946; Petty Officer; Temporary Clerk, India Office, April 1946; Clerical Officer (Reconstruction Competition) 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 24th May 1951; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959; Canberra, October 1952 to January 1956; Cape Town June 1960; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961; Vice-Consul, Capetown, June 1962 to October 1963; Nairobi July 1964.

HAYDEN, Jack Llewellyn, OBE (Military), U.S. Legion of Merit; born 26th April 1903; educated Strand School and King's College, London; m. 1931 Margaret Acklam; Ministry of Information, Press Censorship, 1939–41; war service 1941–46; Lieutenant-Colonel 1943; Foreign Office (Information Officer, Northern Italy) 1946–47; Commonwealth Relations Office (Information Officer, Melbourne) 15th September 1949; Information Officer, with seniority from 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 10th January 1952; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, October 1953; Director, British Information Services, New Zealand, June 1956; Senior Information Officer 20th January 1958; delegate to meeting of SEATO Council of Ministers, Wellington, 1959; Principal Information Officer (local) 1st April 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Information Centre, Marlborough House, August 1963; Disestablished 2nd November 1963.

HAYWARD, Robert; born 21st June 1911; educated Haberdashers' Aske's; m. (1) 1933 Mildred Fields (1 d. 1935; s. 1936); m. (2) 1960 Violet L. Goodall (2 d. 1960, 1962; s. 1963); Reporter or Sub-Editor, Daily Herald, Daily Sketch, Daily Mail, Daily Express, and Assistant Picture Editor, News Chronicle, 1930–39; war service September 1939 to September 1945 (commissioned); Sub-Editor, Daily Mail, 1945, Daily Sketch, 1947; Ifunda Technical Training Centre (Principal), Overseas Food Corporation, Tanganyika, December 1947; Assistant to Chief Mechanical Engineer, Geita Gold Mining Company, Tanganyika, 1949; East African Standard, Nairobi, 1950; Editor, Baraza (Swahili language newspaper) and Tazama (Swahili language weekly magazine), 1955; Temporary Senior Information Officer September 1961; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Uganda; substituting Director, B.I.S., December 1961 to March 1962, January to March 1963 and from April 1964; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th October 1962.

HEAD, The Rt. Hon. Antony Henry, Viscount Head of Throope in the County of Wilts., PC (1951), GCMBG (1963; KCMG 1961), CB (1946), MC (1940); born 19th December 1906; educated Eton and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst; m. 1935 Lady Dorothea Ashley-Cooper (2 s.; 1 d.); commissioned in the 15th/19th Hussars 1926; Life Guards 1928; Brigade Major, 20th Guards Brigade, 1940; Assistant Secretary, Imperial Defence Committee, 1940–41; Staff Officer with the Guards Armoured Division in the United Kingdom; served in Combined Operations Headquarters; Brigadier; took part in the planning of invasion of Europe as Army representative with the Director of Plans for Amphibious Operations; Member of Parliament for Carshalton 1945; Secretary of State for War 1951–56; Minister of Defence 1956–57; High Commissioner in the Federation of Nigeria 1st October 1960 to November 1963; High Commissioner in Malaysia October 1963.

HEAP, Peter William; born 13th April 1935; educated Bristol Cathedral School and Merton College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hons. P.P.E. 1959; m. 1960 Helen Wilmending; National Service, Gloucestershire Regt. and Gold Coast Regt., 1934–36; 2nd Lieutenant; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1959; Dublin July to November 1960; Ottawa November 1960 to December 1962; Colombo (local Principal) March 1963; Principal (acting) 8th May 1964.

HELLINGS, Donald Edward Herbert, MBE (1963); born 16th May 1923; m. 1948 Margaret Kirby (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); Post and Telegraph Officer, G.P.O., 2nd September 1941; joined R.A.F. July 1942, served as Navigator, Bomber Command (Europe) and Transport Command (S.E. Asia); returned to G.P.O. January 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd August 1949; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Wellington February 1953 to February 1956; Salisbury August 1956 to August 1959; Higher Executive Officer (local) 1st April 1959, (substantive) 18th June 1959; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 8th November 1960 and Parliamentary Clerk 6th February 1961; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1963, (substantive) 6th September 1963; Nicosia September 1963.

HENNINGS, John Dunn; born 9th June 1922; educated Ipswich School 1932–41 and University College, Oxford, (Open Exhibitioner) 1941–42 and 1945–47; 2nd Class Finch Honour School of Modern History 1947; m. 1953 Joanna Reed (2 s. 1957, 1959); military service 1942–45, Flight Lieutenant, General Duties, R.A.F.; Assistant Principal, Foreign Office (German Section), 1947; Control Commission for Germany (British Element) 1947–49; Special Assistant to the Financial Adviser, Berlin, 1948–49; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1949; Principal 1951; Secretary, British Guiana Constitutional Commission, 1950–51; seconded West African Inter-Territorial Secretariat, Accra, 1953–55; Attaché for Colonial Affairs, British Embassy, Washington,

Biographical Notes

1960-63: Commonwealth Relations Office

HEPTINSTALL, Leslie George; born 20th August 1919; educated Thames Valley County School and London University; BSc (Econ), 2nd Class Honours; m. 1949 Marion Nicholls (1 d. 1954); military service 1939-46; Captain, Royal Artillery; served in Middle East, Mediterranean and North-West Europe; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1st October 1948; Principal 16th April 1951; seconded to West African Inter-Territorial Secretariat, Accra, 1955; Acting Chief Secretary 1958; Acting Administrator, West African Research Office, 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office 8th February 1961; Wellington May 1962 to June 1964; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, (local Assistant Secretary) September 1964.

HERDMAN, John Mark Ambrose; born 26th April 1932; educated St. Edward's School, Oxford, 1946-50 and Trinity College, Dublin, 1950-54; Class II Honours in Modern History and Political Science; BA 1954; MA 1962; m. 1963 Elizabeth Anne Dillon; H.M.O.C.S., Kenya, 1955-64; served in Central, Coast, Northern and Rift Valley Provinces; Temporary Administrative Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd June 1964.

HICKLING, Ronald; born 3rd January 1915; educated Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Mansfield; m. 1947 Doreen Arnold (twin s. 1950; 1 d. 1959); war service, Fleet Air Arm, 1943-46; with R.C.A.F. 1944; Editorial Staff, Nottingham Guardian, 1946-48; Regional Press Officer, North Midlands, Central Office of Information, February 1948; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer with seniority from 1st August 1949; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Union of South Africa, August 1949 to January 1954; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Karachi, January 1954; Deputy High Commissioner (acting), Peshawar, February to April 1956; British Information Services, Lahore, May 1956 to May 1957; Principal Information Officer 1st December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Cyprus, May 1962 to June 1964; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, September 1964; Chief Information Officer (B) (local).

HICKMAN, John Kyrie; born 3rd July 1927; educated Tonbridge School (Scholar) 1941-45 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1945-48; History Tripos, Parts I and II Class I; BA 1948; m. 1956 Jennifer Love (1 d. 1960; 1 s. 1964); military service (commissioned in Royal Artillery) 1948-50; Assistant Principal 15th October 1948; War Office 25th May 1950; Principal 1st August 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st June 1958; Wellington July 1959 to April 1962; Assistant Secretary-General, Zanzibar and Kenya Independence Conferences, September to October 1963; seconded to Foreign Office May 1964.

HICKS, Reginald Jack; born 22nd January 1922; educated Enfield Grammar School; m. 1946 Jean Sims (1 d. 1949); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Works, July 1938; R.A.F. October 1941; flying training and instructor in U.S. Army Air Corps 1942-43; served in Middle East, India, Burma and Malaya (No. 28 (FR) Squadron) 1944-46; Flight Lieutenant; demobilized and returned to Ministry of Works October 1946; Executive Officer (in absentia) November 1944; Chief Clerk, Ministry of Works, Delhi, (Temporary Higher Executive Officer) January 1951 to November 1951; Higher Executive Officer November 1951; seconded to the Public Services Commission, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, May 1957 to December 1957; Senior Executive Officer 20th March 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st November 1961; Enugu (local Chief Executive Officer) January 1964.

HIGGINS, Desmond; born 22nd January 1930; educated King's Hospital, Dublin; BSc (Econ), London University (External), 1957; m. 1953 Julia Halsall (3 s. 1953, 1956, 1959); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Supply, 1947; National Service with the Royal Navy 1949-51; Executive Officer 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st May 1956; Delhi October 1957 to November 1959; Assistant Information Officer, Lagos, November 1960 to April 1962; Salisbury (local Information Officer) April 1962; Information Officer 1st September 1963.

HOCKENHULL, Arthur James Weston; born 8th August 1915; educated Clifton College and Exeter College, Oxford; Honours Jurisprudence 1936; BA; MA; m. 1955 Rachel Ann Kimber (2 d. 1957, 1959); Colonial Service in Malaya, Singapore, Cyprus and British Guiana 1936-57; seconded to Foreign Service in China 1938-40; interned, Singapore, 1942-45; Principal Information Officer 29th April 1957; Director, British Information Services, Kuala Lumpur, 1957; Director, British Information Services, Singapore, 1958-63; Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th September 1963; local Chief Information Officer (B) 1st January 1964; Director, British Information Services, Malaysia, January 1964.

HODSON, Peter Reginald Lyster; born 30th October 1935; educated Wimbledon College 1947-54; m. 1962 Sheila Whitehouse; National Service 1955-57; Executive Officer, H.M. Stationery Office, February 1957 (seniority from 22nd February
1955); Commonwealth Relations Office 30th October 1961; Karachi May 1962 to June 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964; Lahore September 1964.

Honeyball, Phyllis Ada; born 14th March 1905; educated Winterbourne Road School, Thornton Heath, and Pitman's College, Croydon; Research Assistant, Ministry of Information, December 1939; in charge of Administration, M.O.I. Photographic Unit, Accra, Gold Coast, October 1942 to December 1943; Information Department, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1946; Assistant Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer (local), Winnipeg, August 1958 to August 1961; Information Officer 1st August 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Information Centre, Marlborough House, March 1962 to August 1963; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 19th August 1963.*

Horner, John Bayley Middleton; born 9th February 1907; educated Radley College; m. (1) 1940 Raymonde Heygate (d. 1942); m. Controller, Press and Publications, Control Commission for Germany, 1945-48; Temporary Principal, Colonial Office, July 1948; Principal 1949; Secretary-General, International Rubber Conference, London and Rome, 1951; British Delegate, Standing Closer Association Committee, Port of Spain, 1957; Assistant Secretary 12th November 1962; Principal Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 12th November 1962.

HUNT, Sir David Wathen Stather, KCMG (1963; CMG 1959), OBE (Military); born 25th September 1913; educated St. Lawrence College, Ramsgate, 1927-32 and Wadham College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1932-37; 1st Class Honour Mods. and 1st Class Lit. HUNTER, Alistair John; born 9th August 1936; educated Felsted 1950-55 and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1957-60; 1st Class Honours, English; BA; m. 1963 Gillian Bradbury; R.A.F. 1955-57; qualified as Interpreter in Mandarin Chinese; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th April 1961; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State June 1961 to July 1963; Kuala Lumpur September 1963; Principal (local) May 1964; Principal (acting) 23rd September 1964.

JACKSON, Ernest; born 27th September 1905; educated Johnston School, Durham City; m. 1931 Margaret Watson (1 d. 1936); Durham Board of Guardians 1921-27; Westmorland County Council 1927-35; West Sussex County Council 1935-48; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, 5th July 1948; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th May 1956; Kuala Lumpur March 1957 to June 1960; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th July 1961; Delhi September 1961.

JAMES, Sir (John) Morrice (Cairns), KCMG (1962; CMG 1957), CVO (1961), MBE (Military); born 30th April 1916; educated Bradfield and Balliol College, Oxford; m. 1948 Elizabeth Piesse (2 d. 1948, 1950; 1 s. 1956); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd October 1939; served in Royal Navy and Royal Marines 1940-45; released with rank of Lieutenant-Colonel; Principal (in absentia) 10th March 1944; Capetown/Pretoria March 1946 to April 1947; Assistant Secretary 12th April 1949; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, April 1952 to November 1953; Imperial Defence College Course January 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Karachi, January 1955; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) February 1957; accompanied Prime Minister as adviser on his visits to India, Pakistan, Ceylon, New Zealand and Australia January to February 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, October 1958 to July 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 4th November 1958; High Commissioner in Pakistan October 1961.

KING, John Edward; born 30th May 1922; educated Penarth Grammar School; m. 1956 Mary Beaton (2 d. 1957, 1962); enlisted Rifle Brigade 1941; Royal Military College, Sandhurst, 1942; served with Royal West African Frontier Force in Africa, India and Burma (Chindits); Mentioned in Despatches; Staff Captain, Mons O.C.T.U., Aldershot; released 1947; Cadet, Nigerian Administrative Service, 1947; Second Devonshire Course, Universities of Cambridge and London and School of Oriental and African Studies, 1948-49; Administrative Officer Class III 1950; Private Secretary to Federal Minister 1952; Administrative Officer Class II 1956; Administrative Officer Class I 1959; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Lagos Affairs, 1960; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Education, 1962; Founder Member, Nigerian Council for the Advancement of Art and Culture, 1957; Leader, Nigerian Delegation to Inter-territorial Research Conference, Accra, 1957; represented Nigeria on U.K. delegation to Special Session of C.C.T.A. in Ghana 1958; Member, Provisional Council of the University of Lagos 1963; retired from H.M.O.C.S. 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st November 1963.

LAIRD, Edgar Ord, MBE (1958); born 16th November 1915; educated Rossall School 1929-34 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, 1935-38; Mathematical Tripos Part I Class III, Geographical Tripos Part I Class II (II) and Part II Class II (I); BA (1938); m. 1940 Heather Lonsdale Forrest (4 d. 1944, 1952, 1953, 1956); Surveyor, Colonial Survey Service, Uganda Protectorate, February 1939; commissioned in East African Engineers October 1939 (later transferred to Royal Engineers); served in East

LANCASTER, Joan Cadogan, MA, FSA, FRHistS; born 2nd August 1918; educated Charles Edward Brooke School and Westfield College, London, (Exhibitioner); 2nd Class Honours in History 1940; BA; MA (Paleography and Diplomatic) 1943; Associate of the Library Association 1943; Assistant Archivist, City of Leicester, and Assistant Librarian, University College, Leicester, 1940-43; A.T.S. 1943-46; Librarian, Command School, London, 1945-46; Archivist, City of Coventry, 1946-48; Assistant Librarian, Institute of Historical Research, 1948-60; Assistant Keeper, 1st Class, India Office Records, 19th April 1960; Honorary Editor of Archives 1957-63; author of "The Coventry forged charters: a reconsideration", Bibliography of historical works issued in the United Kingdom, 1946-56, etc.

LARMOUR, Edward Noel; born 25th December 1916; educated Royal Belfast Academical Institution 1928-35, Trinity College, Dublin, 1935-40 (Classical Sizar; Foundation Scholar; Kitchener Scholar; 1st Class Honours in Classics) and Sydney University, N.S.W., 1941-42; m. 1946 Nancy Bill (1 s. 1949; 2 d. 1951, 1960); joined Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers September 1940; Burma Civil Service (Class 1) April 1942; commissioned 14th Punjab Regiment 1943; Major; released September 1946; Deputy Secretary to Governor of Burma August 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th May 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Wellingto n February 1951 to May 1954; seconded to Foreign Service and posted to Singapore September 1954; Counsellor (local) January 1957; Assistant Secretary 2nd December 1957; Canberra October 1961 to June 1964; substituting Deputy High Commissioner 3rd May 1962 to 25th July 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Lagos, (local Assistant Under-Secretary) September 1964.

LEADBITTER, Nicholas Andrew; born 22nd May 1916; educated St. Edward's School, Oxford and Queens' College, Cambridge; BA Honours 1937; m. 1951 Judith Long; commissioned Indian Army 27th January 1939; Assistant Military Attaché, Teheran, 1946-47; retired with rank of Major 27th October 1948; commercial work 1948-52; B.B.C. 1952-57; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 27th January 1958; Accra January 1958; Acting Principal Information Officer January to September 1959; Karachi February 1960; Acting Principal Information Officer and Deputy Director, British Information Services, October to December 1963 and December 1963 to March 1964.

LE BAILLY, William Francis Grahame; born 17th October 1904; educated Wellington College 1918-22 and Brasenose College, Oxford, (Exhibitioner) 1922-27; 2nd Class Hon. Mods. and Lit. Hum.; BA 1926; MA 1931; m. 1946 Cecelia Edith Minchin (née Gardner) (1 adopted s. born 1950; 1 adopted d. born 1951); I.C.S. 1927; Deputy Commissioner 1932; Colonization Officer, Bahawalpur State, 1934-37; Secretary to Financial Commissioner, Punjab, 1937-40; Deputy Commissioner, Delhi, and Chairman, Delhi Municipality, 1942-46; Chairman, Delhi Improvement Trust, 1945-

Biographical Notes

46; retired 1947; Solicitor's Articlecl Clerk 1947-48; Deputy Secretary, Oxford Regional Hospital Board, 1948-52; Secretary to Ministry of Works, Federation of Malaya, 1952-55; Administrator, Petaling Jaya New Town, Malaya, 1956-59; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th January 1960.

LE BRETON, David Francis Battye; born 2nd March 1931; educated Winchester College 1945-49 and New College, Oxford, 1950-54; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; MA; m. 1961 Patricia June Byrne; Colonial Administrative Service and H.M.O.C.S., Tanganyika, 1959-63; Private Secretary to Governor 1959-60; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th May 1963; Principal 3rd July 1963; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations September to December 1963; Zanzibar April 1964; Principal (acting) 8th May 1964; Lusaka September 1964.

LEE, George Ranson; born 26th September 1925; educated Leeds Grammar School 1936-44; m. 1955 Anne Black (1 d. 1962); military service 1944-47; seconded Indian Army (6th Gurkha Rifles) 1945; released with rank of Captain December 1947; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, November 1949 (seniority 1st January 1946); Commonwealth Relations Office 4th January 1954; Karachi May 1955 to May 1958 (Private Secretary to the High Commissioner October 1956 to May 1958) Higher Executive Officer (local) 26th October 1956; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Secretary, Basutoland Constitutional Discussions November to December 1958; Madras December 1959 to February 1963; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Principal 1st August 1963; Secretariat, Meeting of Commonwealth Trade Ministers, London, March 1964 and Commonwealth Finance Ministers' Meeting, Kuala Lumpur, September 1964.

LEES, Frederick; born 14th October 1924; educated Rock Ferry High School, Birkenhead, and Liverpool University; Honours School of Geography 1949; BA; Colonial Office Devonshire Course, London University, 1949-50; m. 1956 Mary Yvonne Wright (1 step-s. 1954, 1 s. 1957); Malayan Civil Service 1950-62; Senior Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1964; Singapore, May 1964.

LENNARD, Thomas Jay, MBE (1954); born 14th May 1921; educated Clifton College and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge; m. 1944 Mary Pat Poole (1 d. 1948; 1 s. 1953); Colonial Administrative Service 1942; Gold Coast; Cadet March 1942, Assistant District Commissioner May 1942, District Commissioner May 1951; Tanganyika: Assistant Secretary and Assistant Public Relations Officer March 1952; Cyprus: Deputy Director of Information Services September 1955, Senior Administrative Officer January 1958, Member of Executive Council June 1960; retired from Her Majesty's Overseas Civil Service April 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 31st October 1960; Secretary, Oversea Migration Board, 1962-64.

LE TOCQ, Eric George; born 20th April 1918; educated Elizabeth College, Guernsey, 1928-36 and Exeter College, Oxford, 1936-39; 2nd Class Honours School of Modern Languages; m. 1946 Betty Esdaile (2 s. 1951, 1953; 1 d. 1957); commissioned in Royal Engineers October 1939; served in North Africa March 1942 to September 1943, Italy September to December 1943, and in Austria and Greece; Major; released March 1946; teacher of modern languages and mathematics, Monmouth School, 1946-48; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1948; Karachi October 1948 to November 1950; Principal 8th May 1950; Dublin April 1953 to January 1955; Accra January 1957 to August 1959; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 14th July 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs, Entebbe, April 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Kampala, October 1962 to June 1964; Canberra September 1964.

LEWIS, David Charles; born 8th June 1928; educated Northampton Engineering College; London Diploma in Economics; m. 1953 Joan Lilian Curry; Temporary Clerk, Royal Armoured Corps; Record Office January 1947 to February 1948; Clerical Assistant, Ministry of Pensions, February 1948 to August 1963; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Pensions and National Insurance, September 1953 to March 1956; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th March 1956; Kuala Lumpur September 1957 to October 1959; Delhi January 1960 to March 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

LEWIS, Ernest Gordon, OBE (1958), MBE (Military) (1943); born 26th September 1918; educated Otago Boys' High School and Otago University, New Zealand; m. 1949 Jean Margaret Smyth; military service 1939-46, Greece, Crete, Western Desert and Italy; Middle East Staff College, Haifa; Lieutenant-Colonel; Mentioned in Despatches; Nigerian Administrative Service 1946; Class II 1955; Commissioner, Turks and Caicos Islands, 1955-58; Administrative Officer Class I, Nigeria, 1959; Permanent Secretary 1960-62; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th November 1962; Karachi December 1962; Principal 4th February 1964.
Lewis, Peter Brigstocke; born 15th October 1923; educated privately, at Birbeck College 1941-42 and Queen Mary College 1945-48, London University; Ordinary Seaman, Royal Navy, 31st August 1942; Midshipman, R.N.V.R., June 1943; Sub-Lieutenant, October 1943; served at sea in Western Approaches Command; released December 1945; Temporary Assistant Principal, Ministry of Education, 11th August 1948 to 31st March 1950; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th May 1950; Executive Officer 9th July 1951; toured Basutoland, the Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland December 1951 to February 1952; Delhi 1953-57; Higher Executive Officer 21st December 1955; Cape Town/Pretoria October 1959 to August 1962; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961 to August 1962; Senior Executive Officer 1st August 1963.

Lintott, Sir Henry John Bevis, KCMG (1957: CMG 1948); born 23rd September 1908; educated Edinburgh Academy, Edinburgh University and King's College, Cambridge; m. 1949 Margaret Orpen (1 s. 1950; 1 d. 1954); Assistant Principal, H.M. Customs and Excise, 1st April 1932; Board of Trade 1935; Principal 1st October 1937; Ministry of Economic Warfare 2nd September 1939; returned to Board of Trade 14th October 1940 as Principal Private Secretary to the President; Assistant Secretary 17th November 1941; Principal Assistant Secretary 18th April 1942; Principal Establishment Officer 11th September 1944; Under-Secretary 1st January 1946; loaned to Organization for European Economic Co-operation in Paris 10th May 1948 as Deputy Secretary-General; Deputy Under-Secretary of State, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th October 1956; High Commissioner in Canada November 1963.

Lister, Victor Arthur; born 10th January 1929; educated St. Clement Danes, Holborn Estate Grammar School; m. 1953 Eluned Thomas (2 s. 1956, 1962; 2 d. 1957, 1959); Clerical Officer, India Office, 7th October 1946; National Service 1947-49; Delhi September 1949 to June 1952; Madras July 1952 to February 1953; Canberra September 1955 to October 1958; Executive Officer 1st September 1959; Bombay December 1959 to February 1962; Delhi March 1962 to February 1963; Singapore June 1963 to August 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964; Kuching August 1964.

Long, Cecil Charles; born 10th March 1923; educated Northern Polytechnic, London; m. 1947 Deidre Beatrice Cornier (1 s. 1950; 1 d. 1952); London Telecommunications Region 26th December 1939; served with Royal Signals in India and Burma 1942-46; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th July 1949; Delhi March 1951 to July 1952; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Pretoria/Cape Town August 1952 to May 1955; Colombo February 1957 to April 1959; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Kaduna September 1960 to December 1963; Ottawa July 1964.

Lovitt, Cyril Arnold, MBE (1963); born 20th September 1920; educated Hornsey County School 1931-37; m. 1946 Dorothy Edwards (3 s. 1947, 1948, 1956; 1 d. 1950); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 30th August 1937; seconded to Palestine Government as Grade K Clerk December 1939; Temporary Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R., 1st May 1942; Temp. Lieutenant, R.N.V.R., December 1944; demobilized July 1946; returned to Dominions Office September 1946; Higher Clerical Officer (assimilated to Executive Officer) 10th February 1947; Higher Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Canberra December 1949 to October 1952; Madras February 1953 to September 1956; Kuala Lumpur (local Senior Executive Officer) 18th October 1957 to 3rd June 1961; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Dublin January 1963; Chief Executive Officer 1st October 1963.

Lucas, Edward, MVO (1961); born 4th June 1929; educated Manchester Central Grammar School 1940-47; m. 1958 June Rainbird (2 s. 1960, 1963); National Service, Royal Engineers, 1948-50; Executive Officer 20th May 1948; Ministry of Food 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 11th January 1954; Dacca 1956-58; Karachi (local Higher Executive Officer) 1960; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Kuala Lumpur May 1964.

Lushington, Geoffrey Franklyn, Brigadier (retd.), CBE (1955; OBE 1951); born 21st August 1908; educated Highgate School and R.M.A., Woolwich; m. 1950 Betty Webb (1 d. 1954; 1 step-d. 1946); commissioned Royal Artillery 1929; served in India 1936-40 and Middle East 1940-43; Staff College 1941; Middle East Planning Staff 1943; served in N.W. Europe 1944-45; B.A.O.R. Planning Staff 1948-51; Military Adviser in Iraq 1953-55; C.R.A. and Deputy Commander 1955-60; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th August 1960; Principal 22nd August 1960; seconded to the Colonial Office for service in the Office of United Kingdom Commissioner, Singapore, 18th July 1962; Singapore September 1963.

Lythgo, Wilbur Reginald, OBE (1964); born 7th June 1920; educated Palmer's School, Grays, 1931-37; m. 1943 Patricia Smith (2 s. 1945, 1947); Clerical Officer, Home Office, 23rd June 1937; mobilized with R.A.S.C. (T.A.) 1st September 1939; served as N.C.O. in U.K., France, Belgium and Holland 1939-41; commissioned in Indian Army 1942 and served in India-Persia and Iraq; released with rank of
Captain June 1946; Executive Officer (in absentia) 1st July 1942; Higher Executive Officer 18th September 1947; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 16th March 1948 and transferred 1st September 1950; British Information Services, India, March 1948 to January 1954 (local Senior Information Officer 6th October 1953); Senior Executive Officer 23rd July 1955; Delhi July 1956 to October 1959; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 30th November 1959; Chief Executive Officer 16th February 1961; Ottawa July 1962; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st February 1964.

McAllister, Richard Andrew; born 10th December 1941; educated Farnborough Grammar School and Caius College, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1960–64; Historical Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class II Division I; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1964.

McBain, David Malcolm; born 19th January 1928; educated Sutton County School; graduated Institute of Transport 1954; evening student, London School of Economics, October 1955 to May 1958; m. 1951 Audrey Evison (1 s. 1956; 2 d. 1959, 1963); Executive Officer, Ministry of Civil Aviation, 1946; National Service, Germany, 1947–49; 2nd Lieutenant, R.A.O.C.; returned to Ministry of Civil Aviation March 1949; Assistant Airport Manager, Castel Benito, Libya, 1949–52; Assistant to Civil Air Adviser, Delhi, 1953–54; Commonwealth Relations Office 2nd September 1957; Delhi (local Higher Executive Officer) 1958–61; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Nairobi December 1963.

McBrinn, Henry; born 29th December 1925; educated Belfast Technical High School; m. 1954 Caroline Anita Wilson; Messenger, General Post Office, 1940; Postman 1944; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th April 1948; Delhi March 1955 to March 1957; Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Karachi 1958 to 1960; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963; Zanzibar 1963.

McCafferty, Christine; born 14th December 1927; educated St. Margaret's Convent, Edinburgh; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of National Insurance (Scotland), August 1946; Clerical Assistant April 1948; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 27th September 1948; Karachi December 1949 to December 1951; Executive Officer (temporary) 19th November 1957; Executive Officer 1st September 1959; Lagos September 1960 to July 1963; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

McConville, Michael Anthony, MBE (1959), Hon. KMN (Malaya) (1962); born 3rd January 1925; educated Mayfield College and Trinity College, Dublin; 2nd Class Moderatorship in Modern History and Political Science 1950; MA, 1959; m. 1952 Beryl Jerrett (2 s. 1953, 1954; 4 d. 1956, 1958, 1961, 1962); Royal Marines 1943; Lieutenant with Nos. 43 and 45 Royal Marine Commandos in Jugoslavia, Italy (wounded) and Hong Kong; Malayan Civil Service 1950–61; Administrative Officer, Segamat, 1957–59; Commissioner of Lands and Mines, Pahang, 1959; Chairman, Border War Executive Committee, 1960–61; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th September 1961; Principal November 1961; member of British Delegation to ECAFE, Tokyo, 1962 and Manila, 1963; Colombo July 1963.

McEntee, Peter Donovan, OBE (1963); born 27th June 1920; educated Haileybury College 1934–37; m. 1945 Mary Elizabeth Sherwood; military service 1939; Lieutenant, King's African Rifles; service in Abyssinia, Ethiopia, Somaliland, Madagascar and Burma; released (Major) 1945; District Officer, Colonial Service, 1946; Senior Assistant Secretary and African Courts Officer 1959; Senior District Commissioner and Principal of the Kenya Institute of Administration 1960; retired from Colonial Service 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th September 1963; Lagos January 1965.

McGee, John; born 2nd November 1919; m. 1945 Aidé Grossi (2 s. 1949, 1957); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, G.P.O., 1936; Overseer Instructor, G.P.O. Counter Training School, 1948; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 1949; Executive Officer 1955; Higher Executive Officer July 1962; seconded to Central African Office 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office May 1964.

McIndoe, William Ian; born 11th March 1929; educated Sedbergh School 1942–47 and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, 1947–51; Classical Hon. Mods. Class I; Lit. Hum. Class II; MA; m. 1954 Irene Mudie (2 d. 1957, 1963; 1 s. 1959); National Service 1951–53 (2/Lt. with 2 R.H.A. in Germany); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th October 1953; Canberra May 1956; Principal 20th June 1958; Salisbury June 1958 to March 1962; Private Secretary to Secretary of State June 1962; Private Secretary to Secretary of Cabinet August 1963.

Mackilligin, David Patrick Robert; born 29th June 1939; educated Winchester and Pembroke College, Oxford; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics 1961; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st August 1961; Salisbury May to August 1962; Karachi September 1962.
McKinney, Ian Martin; born 3rd June 1930; educated Royal Grammar School, Lancaster, and Queen's University, Belfast; BSc (Econ.); m. 1960 Carol Wickham-Jones; reporter, *Belfast Telegraph*, 1953–54; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, H.Q., Northern Ireland District, 1954–55; served Royal Artillery 1955–57; commissioned 1956; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1958–59; Temporary Information Officer 1959–60; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1960; Information Officer, Accra, June 1960 to May 1963; Montreal September 1963 to March 1964; Ottawa March to May 1964; Vancouver May 1964.*

MacLennan, Sir Ian Morrison Ross, KCMG (1957; CMG 1951); born 30th October 1909; educated Hymers College, Hull, 1918–28 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1928–32; 2nd Class Honour Mods. 1930; 1st Class Philosophy, Politics and Economics 1932; MA; Gladstone Research Student, St. Deiniol's Library, Hawarden, 1932–33; m. 1936 Margherita Jarratt (1 d. 1938; 1 s. 1940); Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 31st October 1933; accompanied Agricultural Adviser, Colonial Office, on tour to West African Colonies October 1935 to February 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State, Dominions Office, 15th February 1937; Ottawa April 1938 to April 1943; Principal 2nd January 1939; Private Secretary to Secretary of State December 1943 to May 1944; Capetown/Pretoria May 1945 to August 1948; Assistant Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th May 1946; United Kingdom High Commissioner in Southern Rhodesia February 1951, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland October 1953 to May 1955; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (in absentia) 7th May 1954; High Commissioner in Ghana 1957 to 1959; Ambassador, Dublin, January 1960 to 1963; High Commissioner in New Zealand March 1964.

McMullen, Murray; born 29th June 1909; educated Imperial Service College 1923–27 and Jesus College, Oxford, 1928–31; 2nd Class Honours, School of Modern Languages; BA 1931; m. 1945 Fulvia Schenk; war service with Intelligence Corps 1940–46; Temporary Research Specialist, Ministry of Information, 1946; Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1948; Principal, Colonial Office, 1956; Director, British Information Services, Kenya, 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 18th July 1962; Kuching 1963 to October 1964.

McNeill, Major-General John Malcolm, CB (1963), CBE (1959); born 22nd February 1909; educated Imperial Service College and Royal Military Academy, Woolwich; m. 1939 Barbara Marsh (2 d. 1940, 1944); commissioned Royal Artillery 1929; served in Western Desert, Sicily, Italy, North-West Europe and Burma 1939–45; Imperial Defence College 1952; Secretary, Joint Planning Staff and Deputy Secretary, Chiefs of Staff Committee, 1953–55; Commandant, School of Artillery, 1959–60; Commander, British Army Staff, and Military Attache, Washington, 1960–63; Principal Staff Officer to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations 7th September 1964.

Macdonochie, Kenneth John; born 1st July 1911; educated King's College School 1921–29 and University of London 1934–36; 2nd Class Honours in French; m. 1939 Muriel Crowther (1 s. 1942; 1 d. 1944); BBC (Home Service) 1936–41; R.A.F. 1941; commissioned 1943; Russian interpreter with Photographic Reconnaissance Unit, Murmansk, 1944; British Military Mission, Moscow, 1945; demobilized 1946; rejoined BBC (European Service) 1946–58; seconded to Colonial Office as Temporary Principal Information Officer 1958; United Kingdom Information Officer, Ibadan, 1958–61; Temporary Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; resigned from BBC 7th September 1961; Senior Information Officer 8th September 1961; Montreal September 1963 (local Principal Information Officer).

MacPhee, Norman; born 24th May 1918; educated Dunvegan School, Skye; m. 1944 Ruby May Henderson; Army 1939 to January 1946; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Pensions and National Insurance, February 1946; Executive Officer October 1958; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 12th May 1959; Madras April 1960 to April 1962; Higher Executive Officer (local), Freetown, 31st May 1963; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

McQuiggan, John, MBE (1955); born 24th November 1922; educated St. Edward's College, Liverpool; m. 1950 Elsie Hadler (3 s. 1956, 1959, 1963; 1 d. 1961); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 26th February 1940; enlisted in R.A.F. 1st June 1942; West Africa 1943–44; Italy, 1945; Malta 1946; Instructor in Mathematics and Geography under R.A.F. Educational and Vocational Training Scheme 1946; demobilized January 1947 and returned to Dominions Office; Executive Officer 14th November 1947; Canberra July 1950 to May 1954; Higher Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; joint Secretary (Administration) to United Kingdom delegation to Commonwealth Finance Ministers' Conference, Sydney, January 1954; Lahore November 1954; British Information Services, Lahore, (acting Regional Information Officer) 4th May 1957 to 29th March 1958; Senior Information Officer (local), Canberra, 15th May 1958 to 2nd May 1961; Acting Director, United Kingdom Information Services in Australia,
March to July 1959; Senior Information Officer 1st October 1960; Regional Information Officer, Enugu, (local Principal Information Officer) December 1961 to June 1964; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1963; Director, British Information Services, Uganda, September 1964.

MacRae, Alastair Christopher Donald Summerhaves; born 3rd May 1937; educated Rugby, Lincoln College, Oxford, (2nd Class Honours in English Literature 1961) and Harvard University (Henry Fellow in International Relations); m. 1963 Mette Wilbert (1 d. 1963); National Service with Royal Navy (Commissioned) 1956-57; Dewar Travel Scholarship in Africa 1958; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th September 1962; Dar es Salaam January 1963.

Maher, John Desmond; born 17th January 1922; educated De la Salle College, Weaste, 1933-38; m. 1949 Elizabeth Marian Entwistle (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1953); Assistance Clerk, Unemployment Assistance Board, June 1938-41; served with Royal Navy April 1941 to January 1947; Ty S/Lt (S), R.N.V.R., August 1945; Assistant Secretary to Capt: Air (East Indies) 1946; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, September 1948; Captain, R.A., (T.A.R.O.) 1955; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1960; Delhi 1st May 1961.

Mann, Stanley Robert; born 19th July 1922; educated Santley School and Morley College, D.C.; m. 1952 Freda Ilett (1 d. 1958); General Post Office 1941; war service 1942-46; Royal Navy (Communications Branch): Western Approaches (Russian and North African Convoys), Nore Command (Patrols), Portland Command (Staff); Postal and Telegraph Officer 1948; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, 1949; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th May 1957; Delhi January 1958 to February 1960; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Karachi April 1962.

Manvell, Eric Manvell; born 20th June 1916; educated Queen Mary's School, Basingstoke; m. 1937 Joan Irene Welding (2 s.; 2 d.); sub-editor, Central News, Fleet Street, 1933-37 and Hampshire Chronicle 1937-40; volunteered 1940, Coldstream Guards; commissioned into Royal Hampshire Regiment October 1940; Adjutant, 70th Battalion, 1942-43; G.S.O. III, 146 Brigade, 1944-45; Mentioned in Despatches; G.S.O. II (Press) and D.A.D.P.R., H.Q., Ist Corps, 1945-46; Lieutenant-Colonel 1946; substantive Major, R.A.R.O.; edited Monthly Report of the Control Commission for Germany from 1946-52; Registrar, United Kingdom High Commission, Germany, 1952-55; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th January 1956; Canberra April 1956; Information Officer 18th December 1957; Regional United Kingdom Information Officer, Brisbane, 1958; Senior Information Officer 1st October 1960.

Marsh, Gilbert Lingard; born 15th December 1907; educated Osborne House School and Southern College of Art; member of the Institute of Public Relations; freelance publicity overseas (U.S.A., South America, etc.) 1928-38; enlisted Coldstream Guards October 1939; commissioned Royal Hampshire Regiment April 1940; transferred Royal Armoured Corps 1942; served North Africa (8th Army) and Palestine (as DAPM); demobilized with rank of Captain; Central Office of Information July 1947; Temporary Senior Information Officer and deputy to Chief Regional Officer (Southern Region); Information Officer, Air Ministry, 1954; Information Staff, MEAF, Egypt and Cyprus, 1954-56; National Savings Committee 1958; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1959; Calcutta 1960; Regional Information Officer, Madras, October 1962 to March 1963; seconded to Central African Office (temporary Senior Information Officer) October 1963 to March 1964.

Marsh, James Kenneth; born 5th March 1924; educated Russell School, Addington; m. 1951 Beryl Cooling, R.A.F. 1944-48; Sergeant Pilot 52 and 110 Squadrons; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd October 1949; Delhi March 1955 to March 1957; Karachi March 1958 to May 1960; Port of Spain August 1962 (local Higher Executive Officer); Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.*

Martin, Roger John Adam; born 21st January 1941; educated Westminster School and Brasenose College, Oxford, (Exhibitioner), 1960-64; 2nd class honours in Modern Languages; Voluntary Service, Provincial Administration, Northern Rhodesia, 1959-60; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1964.

Martin, Stanley William Frederick; born 9th December 1934; educated Bromley G.S. 1945-53, University College, Oxford, 1955-58 (Second Class Honours in Jurisprudence) and Inner Temple (Scholar); m. 1960 Hanni Hansen (1 s. 1962); National Service 1953-55 (2nd Lieut. R.A.S.C.); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st August 1958; Assistant Private Secretary to the Secretary of State September 1959 to April 1962; Canberra (local Principal) June 1962; Principal 25th October 1962; Kuala Lumpur March 1964.

Martin, Victor Cecil; born 12th October 1915; educated Jesus College, Cambridge; Classical Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Part II Class I; Assistant Principal, Office
of Works, 14th October 1938; Ministry of Education 9th January 1939; military service October 1939 to December 1945; Major; Intelligence Corps; served in Persia and Iraq Command October 1941 to September 1945; Principal 1st January 1945; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 29th April 1948; transferred December 1949; Delhi February 1951 to April 1954; Delhi December 1956 to January 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.

MASEFIELD, John Thorold; born 1st October 1939; educated Repton School (Scholar) 1953-58 and St. John's College, Cambridge, (Exhibitioner and Scholar) 1958-62; Classical Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Archaeological and Anthropological Tripos Parts I and II Class I; m. 1962 Jennifer Trowell (1 d. 1964); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1962; Private Secretary to the Permanent Under-Secretary of State 12th August 1963; Kuala Lumpur October 1964.

MASH, Walker Sidney Joseph; born 19th January 1913; educated Stonehouse Street School, Clapham S.W.4; m. 1951 Edna Nicholls; enlisted R.A.M.C. September 1939; served in France and East Africa Command; demobilized QMS September 1945; Temporary Assistant, India Office, 5th November 1945; Clerical Officer 1st January 1950; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

MATTHEWS, Frederick; born 5th September 1919; educated Mosley and Birmingham Schools of Art; Diploma in Art and Design; m. 1948 Hebe Moulaki (3 children); enlisted Royal Warwickshire Regt. 1939; B.E.F., France, "Vickforce", 1940; 24th (Guards) Independent Brigade Group, London District, 1940-41; Commissioned, Royal Irish Fusiliers, 1942; Italy 1944; Staff Captain, 3 Corps, Salerno, 1944; Greece 1944; Major, Staff H.Q., Land Forces, Greece, 1945; released 1946; resident Athens 1947; Consultant, E.C.A. Information Services, Athens, 1949-52; Production Officer, Public Information Office, Government of Cyprus, 1956-59; Senior Information Officer, Government of Cyprus, London Office, 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th March 1960; Calcutta (local Senior Information Officer) April 1960 to June 1963; Senior Information Officer 1st August 1963; Director of Information Services, Cyprus, (local Principal Information Officer) July 1964.

MIDDLETON, Donald King; born 24th February 1922; educated King Edward's School, Birmingham, Saltley College and St. Luke's College, Exeter; Certificate in Education (distinction); m. 1945 Elizabeth Ryder (1 d. 1949); Civil Defence Corps 1942-46; Regional Organiser, Midland Region Blood Transfusion Service, 1946-52; Administrative Officer (Publicity), Birmingham Regional Hospital Board, 1952-58; Information Officer, Ministry of Health, 1958-61; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 15th September 1961; Lagos (local Senior Information Officer) September 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st April 1963; Senior Information Officer 1st August 1963; Principal Information Officer (local) September 1964.

MILES, Frank Stephen, CMG (1964); born 7th January 1920; educated Daniel Stewart's College, Edinburgh, and St. Andrew's University, (Scholar) 1938-42; MA in History; Commonwealth Fund Fellowship, Harvard University, U.S.A., 1946-47; degree of Master in Public Administration; m. 1953 Joy Theaker (3 d. 1956, 1958, 1960); enlisted as rating in Fleet Air Arm January 1942; commissioned October 1943; Lieutenant (A) Observer; released July 1946; Assistant to Curator of Historical Records of Scotland, Edinburgh, 1947-48; Temporary Assistant Principal, Scottish Home Department, 18th February 1948; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st May 1948; Wellington February 1949 to April 1952; Principal 1st July 1952; Dacca February 1954; Lahore August 1955 to May 1957 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner May to June 1956); Accra August 1959 to May 1962 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner February to May 1962); Kampala September 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Dar es Salaam, June 1963 (Acting High Commissioner 15th June 1963 to 16th July 1964); Assistant Secretary (acting) 2nd April 1964.

MILES, John Edwin Alfred, OBE (1961: MBE 1952); born 14th August 1919; educated Hornsey County School 1930-37; m. 1952 Barbara Ferguson (2 s. 1956, 1958; 1 d. 1960); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 15th February 1937; joined Queen's Royal West Surrey Regiment May 1940; commissioned in North Staffordshire Regiment February 1941; attached Royal Indian Army Service Corps February 1942; Major August 1943; served in India, Persia, Iraq, Palestine and Egypt; released September 1946; Higher Clerical Officer (later Executive Officer) (in absentia) 1st December 1944; returned to Dominions Office August 1946; Wellington May 1948 to June 1951; Higher Executive Officer 3rd February 1951; Principal 14th August 1952; Calcutta July 1953 to November 1956; Adviser, Governor-General's Office, Port of Spain, June 1961; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to Governor of Jamaica November 1961; Kingston August 1962; Wellington June 1964.

MILLS, Frank; born 3rd December 1923; educated King Edward VI Grammar School, Nuneaton, 1934-42 and Emmanuel
