Biographical Notes

College, Cambridge; m. 1953 Trilby Foster (1 s. 1959; d. 1961); served in R.A.F.V.R. 1942-45 as radar mechanic; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st November 1948; Karachi February 1949; Dacca May 1949 to January 1951; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 1st December 1952; Principal 29th September 1953; Secretary, United Kingdom Delegation to the Colombo Plan Conference, Ottawa, September to October 1954; Cape-town/Pretoria January 1955 to March 1958; Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 2nd June 1960; Kuala Lumpur August 1962; Assistant Secretary (local) September 1963; Singapore December 1963.

MILTON, Derek Francis; born 11th November 1935; educated Preston Manor County Grammar School 1947-54 and Manchester University 1956-59; Honours Class II Division I in Politics and Modern History; BA; m. 1960 Helge Kahle (1s. 1963); National Service in Royal Air Force 1954-56; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 12th October 1959; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations September to December 1960 and March to April 1961; Secretary to Pearl Mission of assessment into hurricane damage in British Honduras 1961; Assistant Private Secretary to Commonwealth and Colonial Secretary September 1962 to January 1964; accompanied Lord Landsdowne to Malaya May 1963; Principal 22nd December 1963; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st January 1964.

MINOGUE, Martin Michael; born 23rd December 1937; educated King James' Grammar School, Knaresborough, 1950-57 and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, (Minor Scholar) 1959-62; Historical Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class II, Division I; National Service with R.A.F. 1957-59; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th September 1962; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st January 1964.

MOLYNEUX, John Anthony; born 1st August 1923; educated Lancing College 1937-41 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1946-48; Honours Degree in Lit. Hum. 1948; MA; m. 1958 Patricia Dawson (3 s. 1960, 1961, 1962); enlisted as radar mechanic in Royal Navy November 1941; commissioned January 1944; served in North Sea Patrol 1942-43 and in Pacific 1944-45; released April 1946 as T/Sub-Lieutenant (Sp. Sc.), R.N.V.R.; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 6th April 1949; Delhi August 1950 to December 1952; Principal 1st July 1952; Karachi September 1955; member of United Kingdom Delegation to the Council Meetings in Karachi of S.E.A.T.O. March 1956 and of the Baghdad Pact June 1957 and January 1959; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, August to December 1957; Canberra May 1959 to May 1962; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to Governor of Northern Rhodesia (local Assistant Secretary) May 1964; Lusaka October 1964.

MONSON, William Bonnar Leslie, CB (1964), CMG (1950); born 28th May 1912; educated Edinburgh Academy and Hertford College, Oxford (Scholar); 2nd Class Honours, Classical Hon. Mods.; 1st Class Honours, Modern History; BA 1934; m. 1948 Helen Isobel Browne, MBE (1949); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd October 1935; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 1938; Acting Principal 1938; Colonial Office 1939; Assistant Secretary 1944; Chief Secretary, West African Council, 1947; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1951; Leader, British Colonial and Dependent Territories Delegations at International Rubber Study Group, Copenhagen 1953, Colombo 1954, Monrovia 1955 and at U.N. Tin Conference, Geneva, 1953; member U.K. Delegation, U.N. Sugar Conferences, New York, 1956 and Geneva 1958; member U.K. Delegation, F.A.O. Conference, Rome, 1957; High Commissioner in Zambia 24th October 1964.

MOON, Peter James Scott; born 1st April 1928; educated Uppingham and Worcester College, Oxford; called to Bar; m. 1955 Lucile Worms (2 d. 1957, 1962); Assistant Principal, Home Office, 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office 1954; Capetown/Pretoria 1956 to 1958; Principal 24th March 1958; Colombo February 1960 to May 1963; Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 12th August 1963.

MOORF, Anthony Becroft, MRI (1959); born 26th May 1928; educated Milton Academy, U.S.A., Cheltenham College 1940-46 and Oriel College, Oxford, 1948-52; 2nd Class Hons. Modern Languages; m. 1959 Catherine Maxwell (1s. 1961); Colonial Administrative Service and H.M.O.C.S., Tanganyika, 1952-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, May 1963; Secretariat, Colombo Plan Consultative Committee, August 1964.

MOORE, Philip Brian Cecil; born 6th April 1921; educated Cheltenham College 1934-40 and Brasenose College, Oxford, (Classical Scholar 1940); m. 1945 Joan Ursula Greenop (2 d. 1949, 1951); R.A.F. Bomber Command 1940-45; Prisoner of War, Germany, 1942-45; Assistant Principal, Admiralty, 1947; Assistant Private Secretary to First Lord of the Admiralty 1950-51; Principal 1951; Principal Private Secretary to First Lord of the Admiralty 1957-58; Assistant Secretary December 1958; seconded to the Colonial Office as Counsellor in United Kingdom Commission, Singapore, 1960-61; Deputy United Kingdom Commissioner,
Singapore, 1961–63; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th September 1963; Deputy High Commissioner, Singapore, (local Assistant Under-Secretary of State) September 1963.

MORETON, John Oscar, MC; born 28th December 1917; educated St. Edward's (Scholar), 1931–36 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1936–39; 2nd Class Classical Hon. Mods.; MA; m. 1945 Margaret Katherine Fryer (3 d. 1946, 1950, 1952); 99th (Royal Bucks Yeomanry) Field Regt., Royal Artillery, 1939–46; France and Belgium 1940; India and Burma 1942–45; MC, Kohima, 1944; Major; Assistant Master, Uppingham School, 1946–48; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1948; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 1949–50; Principal 1950; seconded to Government of Kenya 1953–55; served as Deputy Secretary, Cabinet Office, and as District Officer; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1955; Principal Private Secretary 1956–59; Assistant Secretary 28th September 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office 5th September 1960; Lagos June 1961 to 1964; acting High Commissioner August to September 1962.

MORGAN, Francis Raymond; born 30th December 1918; educated Lutterworth County School; m. 1941 Gertrude Betty Ellingworth (2 d. 1943, 1948; 1 s. 1950); war service 1939–46; commissioned Royal Artillery 1939; served in France 1940, Belgium, Holland and Germany 1944–45; Military Government, Germany, 1945–46; Major; released September 1946; Temporary Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1948; Information Officer 1949; seconded to Colonial Office November 1954 and transferred October 1958; Senior Information Officer, Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Trinidad, 1954–57; in charge United Kingdom Information Office, Jamaica, October 1957 to October 1959; Acting Director, United Kingdom Information Office, West Indies, December 1958 to July 1959; Principal Information Officer 1st December 1959; Director, British Information Services, Uganda, 1st December 1959 to April 1964; Commonwealth Relations Office 9th October 1962; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, August 1964.

MORGAN, James Conwy; born 16th April 1910; educated Malvern College and Brasenose College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hon. Mods.; 1st Class Lit. Hum.; BA 1933; m. 1933 Cicely Mary Normen Cobb (1 s. 1936; 2 d. 1939, 1942); Cadet, Tanganyika, 1934; Assistant District Officer 1936; District Officer (in absentia) 1946; military service 1939–47; K.A.R.; Lieutenant-Colonel; Senior Civil Affairs Officer, B.M.A., Somalia; Mentioned in Despatches; Principal, Colonial Office, 1947; Assistant Secretary 1955; attached to Monckton Commission 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1962; on temporary loan to Colonial Office October 1962 to March 1963; seconded to Central African Department March 1963 to March 1964; Chief of Staff to Chairman of Dissolution Committee A.

MORGAN, William David James; born 3rd October 1922; m. 1944 Joan Lucas (1 d. 1950); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 27th March 1940; enlisted R.A.S.C. March 1942, served in Italy and Palestine; demobilized and returned to Dominions Office 5th February 1947; Executive Officer 5th February 1948; Delhi October 1951 to September 1953; British Information Services, Delhi, (local Higher Executive Officer) October 1953 to March 1957; Higher Executive Officer 18th October 1954; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 20th May 1960; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 19th March 1962, (substantive) 1st September 1962; Senior Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 1st February 1964.

MORLEY, Sir Alexander Francis, KCMG (1959; CMG 1955), CBE (1948); born 6th January 1908; educated Rugby 1920–26 and Queen's College, Oxford, 1926–30; 1st Class Classical Hon. Mods. 1928; 2nd Class Lit. Hum. 1930; BA; m. 1939 Hedy von Landesberger-Antburg (1 d. 1944); Assistant Principal, India Office, 20th October 1930; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State December 1933; Principal 13th March 1936; Adviser to Indian Government delegations to 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 24th International Labour Conferences 1936–38; Secretary to Indian Delegation to Brussels Nine-Power Conference November 1937; on loan to Ministry of Aircraft Production 17th July 1940 to 17th March 1942; attached to United Kingdom Delegations, Commonwealth Communications Conference and U.N.R.R.A. Council, 1945; Assistant Secretary, Burma Office, 31st December 1945 to 14th December 1947; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations General Assembly January 1946; on loan to Treasury for service as Economic Adviser to Lord Privy Seal 15th December 1947; returned to Commonwealth Relations Office 19th April 1949; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, March 1950 to February 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st June 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, February 1956; High Commissioner in Ceylon December 1957 to June 1962; High Commissioner in Jamaica August 1962.

MORTLOCK, Charles Geoffrey; born 4th July 1920; educated St. Edward's College, Malta, Shooter's Hill School and London University (Senior County Exhibitioner) 1939; m. Yvonne Gittus (Croix de Guerre) (2 d. 1947, 1961); B.B.C. 1940–42; leader
writer, Kemsley Newspapers, 1942-44; Features Editor, Overseas Press Department, British Council, 1944. Director of Department 1955; Temporary Senior Information Officer, C.O.I., 1947; London Editor, *British Magazine*, 1947-49; Editorial Adviser, Allied Malta Newspapers, 1950-52; State Information Officer, Penang and Province Wellesley, 1952-54; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, 1954; Nigeria 1954-58; Information Officer 1957; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1959; Senior Information Officer, Chittagong, November 1959 to July 1961; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, (local Principal Information Officer) November 1961; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Nigeria, June 1963 to August 1964; Acting Director, British Information Services, Nigeria, October 1963 to February 1964; Publication: *The Flowing Bowl*.

Moss, Victor Eric: born 6th July 1933; educated Bec Grammar School, Tooting; m. 1962 Anne Robarts; National Service 1952-54; Clerical Officer, Crown Agents, 29th January 1951; Executive Officer 24th September 1952; seconded from Crown Agents to H.M.O.C.S. for service with Nyasaland Government 1958-61; Commonwealth Relations Office 7th May 1962; Salisbury October 1962; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Mousley, Norman Victor: born 12th August 1919; educated West Norwood Central School; m. 1947 Olive Lamburn (1 s. 1949); Royal Army Service Corps January 1940 to April 1946, served in Africa, Sicily and Italy; T.C. II, India Office, June 1946; Clerical Officer 15th May 1948; Karachi January 1952 to April 1955; local Executive Officer April 1954; Executive Officer November 1957; Canberra October 1958 to April 1962; Higher Executive Officer September 1963.

Moynihan, Martin John, MC; born 17th February 1916; educated Birkenhead School and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1934-38; PPE; MA; m. 1946 Monica Hopwood (1 s. 1952; 1 d. 1954); Travelled in Germany 1938; Assistant Principal, India Office, 27th February 1939; commissioned 1940; Indian Army (Q.V.O. Corps of Guides Frontier Force Regiment), served on North West Frontier and in Burma (wounded, MC); released November 1945; Principal 31st January 1944; Delhi, Madras and Bombay October 1946 to November 1948; Joint Secretary, Commonwealth Supply and Production Meeting, September 1951; Karachi October 1952; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, March 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, (local Assistant Secretary) December 1954 to February 1956; Assistant Secretary 30th January 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, 1956-58; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur (with periods as Acting or substituting High Commissioner) January 1961 to September 1963; Deputy High Commissioner, Port of Spain, January 1964.

Napier, Major Frederic Seymour: born 14th August 1917; educated Bishop Foy School, Waterford; m. 1947 Gwen Jones (2 d. 1948, 1951; 1 s. 1957); Shell-Mex and B.P., Ltd. 1937-40; Army 1940-63; served in India and SEAC; post-war service in BAOR, Malaya, Cyprus, NATO (Allied Forces, Southern Europe) and Hong Kong; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963; Information Officer 31st January 1964; Nicosia July to August 1964; Bombay November 1964.

Napier and Ettrick, 14th Baron Napier of Merchistoun, 5th Baron Ettrick and 11th Baronet of Nova Scotia, Rt. Hon. Sir Francis Nigel; born 5th December 1930; educated Eton College and R.M.A., Sandhurst; m. 1958 Delia Mary Pearson (1 d. 1961; 1 s. 1962); commissioned in Scots Guards 1950; served Malaya 1950-51; Adjutant, 1st Battalion Scots Guards, 1955-57; Equerry to H.R.H. The Duke of Gloucester 1958-60; retired 1960; a Member of the Queen's Bodyguard for Scotland (Royal Company of Archers); Deputy Ceremonial Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th August 1962.

Neale, Kenneth James, OBE (1959): born 9th June 1922; educated Hackney Downs School; m. 1943 Dorothy Willett (3 s. 1945, 1947, 1949; 1 d. 1951); Clerical Officer, Tithe Redemption Commission, 15th May 1939; Royal Navy October 1941; commissioned November 1942; Lieutenant 1944; served in Europe, North Atlantic, Mediterranean, East Indies and Pacific; released August 1946; Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, 1st August 1947; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1st March 1951; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 1954; Principal 14th September 1955; seconded as Secretary for the Interior and Local Government, Cyprus, June 1957; Deputy Administrative Secretary (Internal Security), Cyprus, 1958; attended United Nations and Council of Europe as Adviser; returned Colonial Office August 1959; seconded Central African Office March 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st April 1964 Assistant Secretary (temporary) 13th April 1964.

Needham, George; born 9th April 1910; educated Barrow-in-Furness Grammar School and Universities of Durham (MA), Montpellier and Breslau; m. 1954 Hermine
Bauer (1 s. 1956); Assistant anglais, Lycée Henri IV, Béziers, 1934–35; Lecturer at University of Breslau 1935–39; Reuters, Fleet Street, 1939; B.B.C. Foreign Listening Digest 1939–42; Principal, War Office and Foreign Office, 1942–45; Austrian Control Commission: Head of University and Higher Education Branch, Chairman of the Allied Quadripartite Committee on Universities, Vienna, 1945–48; Information Services, Control Commission, Germany, 1948–51; Foreign Office 1951–59; British Consul (Information), Munich; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st December 1959; Information Officer (Acting Senior Information Officer) 20th February 1962; member of United Kingdom Delegation to Brussels Conference October 1961 to April 1962; Senior Information Officer, Toronto, 3rd May 1962.*

Newsam, Richard William, cvo (1961); born 23rd June 1918; educated St. Paul's 1931–36 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1937–39 and 1945–46; MA with war time degree in History; m. 1952 Joan Rostgard (1 s. 1956); commissioned in R.A.S.C. 1939; served with East African forces in Kenya, Abyssinia, Ceylon and Burma; released with rank of Captain 1945; temporary Administrative Assistant, Colonial Office, 1946; Assistant Principal 1946; Principal 1947; seconded to Nigeria, 1952–53; Commonwealth Relations Office 27th May 1957; Colombo July 1958; Karachi February 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st July 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th June 1963.

Nicholas, John William; born 13th December 1924; educated Holly Lodge Grammar School, Birmingham, and Birmingham University 1942–43 and 1947–49; Honours History; m. 1947 Rita Jones (2 s. 1949, 1953); Army 1944–47; commissioned Royal Warwicks; seconded to The Rajput Regiment, Indian Army; served in India and Burma; Assistant Principal, War Office, 11th July 1949; Principal 13th November 1954; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office 23rd September 1957; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 1st April 1958; Kuala Lumpur October 1957 to February 1961; British delegation to Colombo Plan Conference, Melbourne, November 1962; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to Governor of Nyasaland January to July 1964; Deputy High Commissioner, Zomba, July 1964.

Nightingale, William Denis; born 2nd April 1913; educated Hampton Grammar School, Middlesex; m. 1940 Wendy Franklin (twin s. 1946; 2 d. 1941, 1948); war service 1939–45; volunteered as private 1939; commissioned 1942; served in Abyssinia, Egypt and Italy; First South African Infantry Division; Sixth South African Armoured Division; Central Mediterranean Training Centre, Benevento, (seconded to British Army as instructor in Armoured Tactics with rank of Major); Odhams Press, London, 1931; North Somerset Independent (Frome) 1932; Bristol Evening World 1933–34; Argus South African Newspapers 1934–56; for two years Vice-President of the South African Society of Journalists; Daily Express, London, 1956–58; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st January 1958; Editor-in-Chief, British Information Service, Delhi, April 1958; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, May 1960; local Principal Information Officer May 1960; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, May 1963.

Norris, Eric George, CMG (1963); born 14th March 1918; educated Hertford Grammar School 1928–36 and St. Catharine's College, Cambridge, 1936–39; Mathematics Tripos Part I Class II 1937; Natural Science Tripos Part II Class III 1939; m. 1941 Pamela Crane (3 d. 1942, 1944, 1950); Assistant Master, Nautical College, Pangbourne, September 1939 to April 1940; enlisted in ranks of Royal Signals April 1940; commissioned May 1941; served in Germany July 1945 to October 1946; Major; released October 1946; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd December 1946; Dublin February 1948 to September 1950; local Principal 16th November 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Karachi March 1952; Lahore October 1953 to August 1955 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner in Lahore July to September 1954, in Peshawar September to December 1954); Delhi October 1956 (local Assistant Secretary); Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay, November 1957 to March 1960; Assistant Secretary 2nd December 1957; Imperial Defence College 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, (local Assistant Under-Secretary) 23rd September 1962.

Norris, Percy Leonard; born 17th April 1928; educated Chiswick Polytechnic; m. 1951 Angela Chandler (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); Temporary Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 1945–47; National Service, Royal Navy, 1947–49; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 1949; Executive Officer 1954; British Solomon Islands 1956–58; Commonwealth Relations Office 3rd March 1961; Kuala Lumpur September 1961; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

Nunn, Frederick Norman; born 13th November 1907; m. 1932 Eileen Turner (1 s. 1933; twin d. 1939); Assistant Clerk, Clare Rural District Council, July 1927 to March 1930; General Clerk, Surrey County Council, April 1930 to September 1934; Settlement Officer, Portsmouth City Council, October 1934 to June 1939;
O'LEARY, Terence Daniel; born 18th August 1928; educated Dulwich College and St. John's College, Cambridge; BA 1950; Historical Tripos Class II Division I 1951; m. 1960 Janet Douglas Berney (twin s. 1960); military service 1946-48; commissioned in Queen's Royal Regiment; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 17th August 1953; Resident Clerk March 1954 to March 1956; Wellington May 1956 to March 1958; Principal April 1958; Delhi February 1960; Dar es Salaam February 1962 to June 1963.

OLIVER, Lieutenant-General Sir William Pasfield, KCB (1956: CB 1947), KCMG (1962), OBE, DL; born 8th September 1901; educated Radley College and Royal Military College, Sandhurst; m. 1938 Elizabeth Margaret Brind (1 s. 1943; 1 d. 1941); Chief of General Staff, G.H.Q., Middle East, (Major-General) 1945-46; Major-General 1949; Chief Army Instructor, Imperial Defence College, 1949-50; Chief of Staff, Eastern Command, January 1951 to December 1952; Principal Staff Officer to High Commissioner, Federation of Malaya, 1953-54; General Officer Commanding Berlin (British Sector) 1954-55; Vice-Chief of the Imperial General Staff 1955-57; Colonel, The Queen's Own Royal West Kent Regiment, 1949-59; Principal Staff Officer to Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations September 1957 to 1959; High Commissioner in Australia November 1959.

O'REGAN, John William Hamilton, OBE (1955); born 22nd March 1913; educated Marlborough College 1925-32 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1932-35; 2nd Class Honours Botany 1935; MA; m. 1941 Joan Caldecott (3 s. 1943, 1947, 1950); Cadet, Ceylon Civil Service, 1935; Private Secretary to Governor 1938-41; Assistant Government Agent, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Trincomalee; Controller, Internal Purchase Scheme, 1944-1950; Deputy Colonial Secretary, Jamaica, 1950-56; acted as Colonial Secretary on several occasions; Permanent Secretary, Western Region, Nigeria, 1956; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Works and Surveys, Federal Government of Nigeria, 1958-62; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th August 1962; Kampala September 1962.

ORMFORD, Richard Caton; born 22nd January 1915; educated Winchester College 1928-33 and New College, Oxford, 1933-37; 2nd Class Honour Moderations and Lit. Hum.; BA; m. 1947 Elizabeth More (2 d. 1949, 1956; 2 s. 1952, 1954); Assistant Principal, India Office, 11th October 1938; joined Royal Armoured Corps as Trooper November 1941; commissioned October 1942 in Indian Armoured Corps and served initially in India and in 1944-45 in Burma; wounded;

OAKELEY, Rowland Henry; born 28th January 1909; educated Clifton College 1922-27 and New College, Oxford, 1927-30; Honours Modern History; qualified in Chinese Written Language and Amoy Colloquial 1934; m. 1940 Diana Hayward (twin s. 1941; 2 d. 1946, 1947); Malayan Civil Service 1931-58; Chinese Affairs and Labour Departments; interned, Singapore, 1942-45; Commissioner for Labour, Federation of Malaya, 1954-57; Secretary to Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare 1957-58; retired under Malayanization scheme 1958; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th May 1959; Principal 14th January 1960; an Adviser to the Government Delegation, Forty-fourth International Labour Conference, Geneva, June 1960.

O'BRIEN, Terence John, MC; born 13th October 1921; educated Gresham's School, Holt, 1935-40 and Merton College, Oxford, 1940-41 and January 1946-47 (Postmaster); 2nd Class Honours in History; MA; m. (1) 1950 Phyllis Mitchell (dec.); m. (2) 1953 Rita Reynolds (1 s. 1954; 2 d. 1957, 1959); enlisted in ranks of R.A. December 1941; commissioned May 1942; served in North-West Europe; MC March 1945; Captain May 1945; released in Class B January 1946; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 14th April 1947; Colombo December 1949 to January 1952; Principal 10th March 1952; seconded to Treasury November 1953 to December 1955; Canberra May 1956 to November 1958; Kuala Lumpur October 1960; Joint Secretary to Inter-Governmental Committee on Malaysia, Jesselton, September 1962 to September 1963; Delhi November 1963; Assistant Secretary 2nd April 1964.

O'CONNOR, John Terence; born 16th April 1922; educated St. Ignatius College, Stanford Hill, 1933-38; m. 1948 Peggy Ellis (2 s. 1952, 1955); Clerical Officer, India Office, 30th May 1939; enlisted R.A.F. January 1941; served in Southern Rhodesia, India and Burma; rejoined India Office July 1946; Executive Officer 8th January 1948; Cape Town December 1950 to May 1954; Higher Executive Officer 3rd August 1955; Canberra January 1956 to July 1959; Delhi March 1961 to March 1964; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1963.
Captain; released December 1945; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State for India 10th December 1945; Principal 29th August 1946; Bombay June 1951 to May 1953; Wellington December 1956 to May 1959; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 17th October 1960; Calcutta March 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner 11th April to 24th September 1962.

Osborne, Gwendoline Anne; born 3rd February 1920; educated Beal Grammar School, Ilford, 1931-35; Secretary, Whitbread's Brewery, 1935-39; Typist, Tithe Redemption Commission, 1939-42; Cypher Clerk, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1942; Clerical Officer 19th October 1943; Karachi May 1952 to November 1955; Karachi February 1956 to November 1958; Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Canberra January 1959 to April 1962; Dublin June 1962; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Overton, David; born 22nd April 1919; educated Sir George Monoux Grammar School, Walthamstow; m. 1946 Mary Pye (1 d. 1948); Local Government 1936-39, 1946-50; military service 1939-46; commissioned 1942; Captain 1945; served with the R.W.A.F.F. and the 14th Army; Superintendent, B.N.B.C., National Central Library, 1950; Deputy Librarian, Imperial Institute Library, 1952; Librarian 1953; Deputy Librarian, Commonwealth Relations Office and Colonial Office, 1954 and Department of Technical Assistance 1961.

Oxley, Humphrey Leslie Malcolm, OBE (1956); born 9th October 1909; educated Epsom College 1922-27; m. 1945 Frances Bowden (twin s. 1947); entered solicitor's office as articled clerk 1928; qualified as solicitor and enrolled 1933; Junior Legal Assistant, India Office, 23rd September 1933; appointed Commissioner for Oaths April 1934; Assistant Solicitor 13th March 1944; Senior Legal Assistant, Commonwealth Relations Office and Colonial Office, 1st January 1950; Assistant Legal Adviser 25th August 1961.

P

Packe, William Wilkinson; born 1st January 1916; m. 1957 Doris Ivy Weston; Royal Army Medical Corps April 1940 to December 1946; Warrant Officer Class I; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 17th February 1947; Clerical Officer 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 24th December 1954; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

Pares, Peter; born 6th September 1908; educated Lancing College 1922-27 and Jesus College, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1927-30; 2nd Class Classical Tripos Part I and 2nd Class History Tripos Part II; BA; H.M. Consular Service 1930; served in various Consular posts in U.S.A., Cuba, Czechoslovakia, Hungary and Roumania; First Secretary, Washington, 1944-46; seconded to Control Commission for Germany 1946-48; Foreign Office 1949-52; Consul at Casablanca, Morocco, 1952-55; Deputy Consul-General, Frankfurt, Germany, 1956-57; Consul General, Asmara, Ethiopia, 1957-59; Assistant Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th April 1959; Regional Information Officer, Quebec, July 1963.

Parsons, Edwin Thomas Andrew; born 23rd May 1927; educated Public Central School, Plymouth, 1938-42; m. 1948 Lucy Edith Cook (1 s. 1952; 1 d. 1954); General Post Office 1942; Royal Navy June 1945 to November 1947; Clerical Officer, Exports Credits Guarantee Department, March 1949; evening student, City of London College, 1954, 1955 and 1957, qualified as Associate Member of the Institute of Export; Executive Officer June 1956; Commonwealth Relations Office November 1961; Madras March 1962 to March 1964; Higher Executive Officer (local) July 1964 Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964; Nairobi July 1964.

Pauncefot, Bernard Edward; born 8th April 1926; m. 1956 Patricia Anne Leah; R.A.F.V.R. and military service 1944-48; Regular Army Reserve of Officers from 1948; Metropolitan Police Civil Staff 1948-52; seconded to Colonial Office 1953; Information Officer, Malaya, 1953-56; H.M.O.C.S. 1957; Tanganyika Information Services 1957-63; retired from H.M.O.C.S. under Tanganyika Africanisation scheme as Principal Information Officer (Deputy Director) 1963; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, October 7th 1963; Member of Institute of Public Relations.

Pendleton, Peter Reginald; born 12th February 1932; m. 1955 Nora Grace Elizabeth Young (5 s. 1956, 1957, 1959, 1960, 1961); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, 21st February 1949; National Service 1950-52; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th December 1953; Bombay 1955; Delhi 1958; Information Officer 6th August 1961; Lahore August 1961 to June 1964; Karachi October 1964.

Pepper, Denis Stephen Wetherell; born 7th December 1912; educated Bedford Modern School; m. 1949 Joan Gregson (née Alexander) (1 step-s. 1939; 1 step-d. 1945; 1 s. 1953); commercial advertising 1932-40; Coldstream Guards 1940; commissioned Royal Warwickshire Regiment; Special Operations Executive 1943, served in Egypt and Italy; released as Major
1946: Information Officer, Foreign Office, 1946-56; served in Thailand, Indo-China, China and Cyprus; commercial advertising 1956-59; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1959; Lagos February 1960; Enugu April 1960; Kaduna August 1960 to December 1962; Benin (local Senior Information Officer) July 1964.

PETERS, William, MVO (1961), MBE (1959); born 28th September 1923; educated King Edward VI Grammar School, Morpeth, 1935-41 and Balliol College, Oxford, (Domus Exhibitioner) 1942 and 1946-48; 2nd Class Honours Lit. Hum.; BA 1948; MA 1948; m. 1944 Catherine Bailey; enlisted in Queen's Royal Regiment 1943; commissioned in India to King's Own Scottish Borderers 1944; seconded 9th Gurkha Rifles; released as Captain May 1946; appointed H.M. Overseas Civil Service September 1948: First Devonshire Course at Oxford and London Universities 1948-49; Administrative Officer Class IV, Gold Coast, February 1950; Class III September 1953; Class II, Ghana, July 1957; Deputy Secretary to Regional Commissioner, Northern Ghana, January 1958; Secretary July to November 1958; retired from H.M. Overseas Civil Service August 1959; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th July 1959; Principal 31st December 1959; Dacca September 1960; Acting Deputy High Commissioner July to October 1962; Nicosia November 1963.

PHILIP, John Clark; born 27th February 1920; educated Acland Central 1931-34; m. 1942 Dorothy Turpin (2 s. 1946, 1948; 1 d. 1954); Sorting Clerk, G.P.O., 7th January 1939; R.N.V.R. 1939-46; Sub-Lieutenant; P. and T.O. 24th May 1948; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 8th August 1949; Executive Officer 24th December 1952; Higher Executive Officer 11th June 1958; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th October 1960: Delhi (Private Secretary to High Commissioner) January 1961 to April 1963; Karachi April 1963 to May 1964; Lahore (local Senior Executive Officer) May 1964; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 14th August 1964.

PHILLIPS, Kenneth; born 1st May 1928; educated Carre's Grammar School, Sleaford, Lincs. and Aylesbury Grammar School; m. 1960 Margaret Oakley (1 s. 1962; 1 d. 1964); Executive Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, May 1949; Commonwealth Relations Office 23rd April 1951; Lahore March to June 1953; Peshawar June 1953 to March 1955; Calcutta July 1956 to March 1957; Accra May 1960 to May 1963; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960, Colombo December 1963.

PHILLIPS, Albert Edward; born 12th November 1919; m. 1950 Marjorie Phyllis King (2 s. 1951, 1954); Counter Clerk and Telegraphist 26th April 1936; war service 1941-46; Royal Navy (Communications Branch); served in Iceland and Malta; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd August 1949; Delhi (local Executive Officer) September 1952 to February 1956; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; British Information Services, Johannesburg, July 1959 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

PHILLIPS, Douglas Herbert Charles; born 4th November 1924; educated Cardinal Vaughan School, Kensington; m. 1950 Olwen Laverick (1 d. 1954); Royal Navy 1943-46; service in Australia and Ceylon 1945-46; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Civil Aviation, December 1946; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1948; Executive Officer 30th August 1949; Karachi December 1950; Peshawar December 1952 to May 1953; Calcutta January 1954 to May 1957; Higher Executive Officer (local) 28th January 1954, (substantive) 13th June 1955; Bombay September 1959 to December 1962; Senior Executive Officer (local) 3rd September 1959; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Departmental Training Officer April 1963; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 1st October 1963, (acting) 14th August 1964.

PICKARD, Cyril Stanley; born 18th September 1917; educated Alleyn's School and New College, Oxford; 1st Class Honours School of Modern History 1939; m. 1941 Helen Strawson (3 s. 1946, 1948, 1954; 1 d. 1950); Assistant Principal, Home Office, 2nd October 1939; military service January 1940 to July 1941; Captain; released to Foreign Office for special appointment with Office of Minister of State, Cairo, July 1941 to May 1944; Principal 1st March 1943; served with U.N.R.R.A. in Middle East and Germany on approved employment terms May 1944 to October 1945; returned to Home Office 1st November 1945; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st June 1948; Delhi September 1950; Canberra (local Assistant Secretary) August 1952 to March 1955; Assistant Secretary 7th November 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, September 1958 to March 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary (temporary) 8th October 1962, (acting) March 1964; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st April 1964.

PLANT, Jack; born 1st February 1925; educated Salford Grammar School 1936-41; m. 1947 Nancy Roddick (2 s. 1948, 1953); served in Royal Navy 1942-46; commissioned (Midshipman) 1943; Sub-Lieutenant 1944; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1946-47; Clerical Officer January 1948; Executive Officer June 1950; Commonwealth Relations
Office 2nd June 1954; Colombo February 1955 to March 1957; Accra (local Higher Executive Officer) May 1957 to June 1960; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Karachi (local Senior Executive Officer) November 1961; Senior Executive Officer 1st August 1963.

PLENTY, Alan Gerald; born 13th August 1925; educated Hampton Grammar School 1937-42; m. 1946 Iris Panton (1 s. 1964); Royal Navy (Combined Operations) 1943-46; Clerical Officer, War Damage Commission, March 1947 to September 1953; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1953; Executive Officer 31st December 1955; British Information Services, Karachi, April 1956 to April 1958; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

PORTER, Patrick Basil; born 15th March 1921; educated London School of Economics and Political Science, University of London; Honours degree in History 1950; BA; Post Graduate Certificate in Education 1951; Academic Diploma in Education 1952; m. 1950 Margaret Rudge (twin s. 1956; 1 d. 1958); R.A.F. 1941-46; 3209 Servicing Commando; served in India, Burma, Normandy, French Indo-China and Siam; History Master, Carshalton, 1951-53; Education Officer, Western Nigeria, 1953-56; Editor for London Publisher 1956-58; Temporary Information Officer, Reference Division, Central Office of Information, 1958; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, 1959; Lagos 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; Information Officer 17th July 1962; Auckland (local Senior Information Officer) February 1963; author of How the People of Britain are Governed.

POTTER, James Aked; born 17th August 1914; educated Saffron Walden School, University College, London, and Heidelberg University; m. 1950 Theresa von Keisenberg; Colonial Office 1939-42; Air Ministry (Intelligence) 1942-43; Political Intelligence Department, Foreign Office, 1943-48; German Section 1948-50; travelled in New Zealand, Canada and U.S.A. 1950-54; locally employed Temporary Assistant Information Officer 1954-56; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1956; Toronto June 1957; Information Officer (local Senior Information Officer) 21st February 1958; Perth 2nd January 1961; Senior Information Officer 1st August 1963.

POVER, Alan John; born 16th December 1933; educated Salesian College, Thornleigh, 1945-52; National Service 1953-55; Executive Officer, Ministry of Pensions and National Insurance, 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office 9th October 1961; Lagos April 1962; Higher Executive Officer (local) 10th July 1963; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

PRESTON, Myles Park; born 4th April 1927; educated Liverpool Institute High School 1938-45 and Clare College, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1945-48; Mathematical Tripos Part I Class I 1946, Part II Senior Optime, 1948; MA 1952; m. 1951 Ann Betten (1 s. 1955; 1 d. 1957); Instructor Lieutenant (f.), Royal Navy, 1948-51; Assistant Principal, Admiralty, 15th November 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st September 1953; Delhi September 1954 to November 1956; Principal (temporary) 28th January 1957; Principal 6th August 1957; Lagos 1959-62; Kampala 1964.

PRICE, Robin Murray; born 2nd May 1932; educated Blundell's School 1946-51 and Queens' College, Cambridge, 1951-54; 2nd Class Honours English Literature; MA; Commerce 1954-56; Assistant Librarian, House of Lords, 1957-63; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th November 1963.

PRICE-JONES, Gwilym; born 30th June 1906; educated Jesus College, Oxford, 1924-28; Greats 1928; National Library of Scotland, Edinburgh, 1932-40; Assistant Principal, Department of Health for Scotland, 1940; Principal 19th November 1943; Ministry of Town and Country Planning, London, 1946-51; General Register Office (International Branch) 1951-55; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 2nd January 1956, transferred 1st April 1957.

PRITCHARD, Sir Neil, KCMG (1962: CMG 1952); born 14th January 1911; educated Liverpool College 1920-29 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1929-33 (Gibbs Scholar 1931); 1st Class Honours Modern History; BA 1932; m. 1943 Mary Burroughes (1 s. 1945); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd October 1933; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 5th October 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 22nd April 1938; Assistant Secretary to Rhodesia and Nyasaland Royal Commission April 1938 to March 1939; Principal 2nd February 1939; Capetown/Pretoria April 1941 to September 1945; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1946; Dublin April 1948 to October 1949; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 28th December 1950; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, May 1954 to February 1957; Deputy High Commissioner, Canberra, June 1957 to June 1960; Deputy Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 1st July to 30th November 1961; British High Commissioner, Tanganyika, 9th December 1961 to 11th July 1963; Deputy Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 23rd September 1963; Deputy Under-Secretary of State 1st April 1964.
PUGH, John Arthur; born 17th July 1920; educated Brecon Grammar School 1931-37 and Bristol University 1952-54; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, June 1937; Royal Navy June 1941 to October 1945; Executive Officer (in absentia) June 1942; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, October 1947; Senior Executive Officer, Ministry of Pensions, September 1954; loaned to Gold Coast Administrative Service and served in Ministry of Health and Prime Minister's Office August 1955 to June 1958; Adviser on Organisation and Methods to Ghana Government under United Kingdom/Ghana Technical Co-operation Scheme October 1958 to October 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 4th April 1961; Lagos (local Chief Executive Officer) June 1962; Chief Executive Officer 1st October 1963; Principal 22nd July 1964.

PURCELL, Robert Michael; born 22nd October 1923; educated Ampleforth College 1937-41; commissioned 1943 in 60th Rifles; served in Italy 1944-45 and Palestine 1946; released 1947; Colonial Administrative Service, Uganda, and H.M. Overseas Civil Service 1949-62: District Officer 1951; Assistant Secretary 1952; Sabbatical year, Oxford, 1957-58; District Commissioner 1959 and 1962; retired from H.M.O.C.S. 1963; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1964; Principal September 1964.

Q

QUINN, Geoffrey Dawson; born 28th September 1929; educated St. David's County High School, Pembrokeshire, and Mayfield School, Goodmayes, Essex; m. (1) 1954 Ninette Adair; m. (2) 1962 Gabrielle Challoner, SRN (1 d. 1963); National Service, R.A.S.C., Aldershot and Singapore, 1948-49; Editorial staff: British United Press, London; United Press, Singapore; B.B.C.; Associated Press and National Trade Press, London, 1945-56; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Central Office of Information, August 1956 to August 1957; Temporary Information Officer, Export Publicity and Fairs Branch, Board of Trade, August 1957; Information Officer 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1963; Accra October 1963.

R

RAFTERY, Peter Albert; born 8th June 1929; educated St. Ignatius College; m. 1952 Margaret Hulse (4 d. 1953, 1955, 1957, 1959); Clerical Officer, India Office, October 1946; National Service 1947-49; Delhi January 1950 to January 1954; Executive Officer February 1956; Peshawar March 1956 to April 1959; Information Officer (local) 5th November 1959; Cape Town November 1959 to May 1962; Acting Regional Information Officer February to September 1960 and March to May 1961; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961 to December 1962; Vice-Consul, Cape Town, May to December 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Kuala Lumpur January 1963; Nairobi February 1964.

RAINSFORD, Frederick Fitzpatrick, Air Commodore (retd.), CBE (1949), DFC (1943); born 12th December 1909; educated Campbell College and Queen's University, Belfast; Batchelor of Agriculture 1935; m. (1) 1939 Dorothy Kitty Ralph (2 d.); m. (2) 1949 Winifred Audrey Meyer (1 d.: 1 s.); farmed in Kenya 1929-31; commissioned in R.A.F. (Special Reserve) 1936; Mentioned in Despatches 1940; short service commission 1936; permanent commission 1947; qualified R.A.F. Staff College 1943; served mainly in Bomber Command until 1945; Commanded 148 Squadron (Middle East) 1941-42 and 115 Squadron (United Kingdom) 1943; Transport Command 1945-46; Deputy Director of Air Transport, Air Ministry, 1947-49; Directing Staff, R.A.F. Staff College, 1949-51; Headquarters, F.E.A.F., 1952-55; Commanded Recruit Training Stations 1955-57; Air Attaché, Greece, 1957-60; Directing Staff, Royal Naval War College, 1960-62; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th April 1962; Madras February 1964.

RAPER, Timothy Charles Hartcup; born 19th June 1922; educated Sherborne School 1935-40, Keble College, Oxford, 1940 and London School of Oriental and African Studies 1946-48 and 1960-61; 2nd Class Honours (Division I) in Sanskrit; military service 1941-46; served with Intelligence Corps in India and Burma; commercial work 1949-59; Temporary Executive Officer, India Office Library, 16th October 1961; Assistant Keeper, Class II, 21st May 1963.

RATCLIFFE, Marjorie Louise; born 24th August 1904; educated Southall Secondary School; Typist, India Office, 31st August 1925; General Post Office, Birmingham, 1st November 1926; India Office 6th July 1931; Shorthand-Typist 1st January 1933; Clerical Officer 10th October 1939; Executive Officer 28th March 1945; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

REDPATH, Alexander William, CBE; born 4th September 1909; educated Worksop College and R.M.C., Sandhurst (King's Cadet); m. 1936 Rosemary Brenda Cotesworth (2 s. 1939, 1943); commissioned Indian Army 1929; 3/12th Frontier Force; A.D.C. to Governor, N.W.F. Province; entered Indian Political Service 1934 (I.P.S. political, administrative and law examinations); P.A. to A.G.G., Rajputana, (Political and Secretariat training); Assistant Commissioner (under
administrative and judicial training), Multan, Punjab; Under-Secretary to A.G.G. (Sub-Judge, Magistrate and J.P.), Central India; Assistant Political Agent (District Magistrate, Senior Sub-Judge, Collector), Gilgit; Under-Secretary to Resident, Punjab States; Secretary to Resident, Eastern States; Political Agent, Bengal States; 1st Secretary and Counsellor (acting), British Legation, Kabul, Afghanistan; Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan; retired from I.P.S. 1948; Bursar, Radley College, 1949-51; contract service with Government of Pakistan 1952-58; Deputy Secretary and Joint Secretary to Government in Cabinet Secretariat; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st July, 1958.

REED, Adrian Harbottle; born 5th January 1921; educated Hele's School, Exeter, 1933-39 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, (Exhibitioner) 1939-41; Hist. Trip. Part I Class II Division I 1941; BA 1947; m. 1947 Doris Duthie (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1952); enlisted in Royal Artillery September 1941; commissioned January 1942; served in Iraq, Persia and Italy October 1942 to July 1945; Captain; employed with Control Commission for Germany 1946; released March 1947; Assistant Principal, India Office, 18th June 1947; Lahore January 1948 to April 1950 (local Principal 1st March 1949); Principal 17th July 1950; U.K. Delegation to U.N. General Assembly 1951; Salisbury July 1953 to May 1956 (Acting High Commissioner May to August 1955); Dublin October 1960 to October 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 15th October 1962, (substantive) 1st July 1963.

REID, Dougal Gordon; born 31st December 1925; educated Sedbergh School 1939-43 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, 1944 (R.N. and R.M. Short Course) and 1947-48 (Colonial Service Course); m. 1950 Georgina Elizabeth Johnston (twin s., one dec., 1952); Royal Marines 1944-46 (Lieutenant); Cadet, Sierra Leone, 1949; Assistant District Commissioner 1952; District Commissioner 1956; Clerk to the Executive Council 1957-58; seconded to Colonial Office as Principal 1958-60; Admin. Officer, Grade II, 1961; Permanent Secretary 1960-62; retired from H.M.O.C.S. April 1962; Arthur Guinness Son and Co. (Park Royal), Ltd., 1962-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th July 1963; Accra June 1964.

REISS, John Henry; born 26th March 1918; educated Bradfield College; m. 1943 Dora York (1 s. 1945; 2 d. 1945, 1947); war service with East African Forces 1939-42; Officer in Charge, African Section, Kenya Government Information Services, 1945; Officer in Charge, Kenya Information Services, 1949; Director of Information, Kenya, July 1954 to August 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1959; Senior Information Officer 12th February 1960; Principal Information Officer (temporary) 1st April 1960; Johannesburg August 1961; seconded to Foreign Service 1st December 1961; Wellington February 1963; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963.

REITH, Martin; born 6th December 1935; educated Royal High School of Edinburgh; m. 1964; Scottish Home Department; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1954; R.A.F. 1954-56; Calcutta 1957-59; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Kampala September 1962.

RENWICK, John Stanley; born 10th November 1920; educated Heaton Grammar School; m. 1946 Kathleen Mary Ross (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1952); Army 1939-46; served in France, Belgium, Iraq, Iran, India, Egypt; Executive Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food, 1948; Treasury 1953-58; Higher Executive Officer 19th April 1956; Adviser on Organization and Methods, Ghana, 1958-60; Commonwealth Relations Office 4th April 1961; Lagos May 1951; Kaduna August 1963 to March 1964; Senior Executive Officer 1st August 1963; Secretary, United Kingdom Referendum Observers, Malta, 1964; Zomba July 1964.

REYNOLDS, Frank Arrowsmith; born 30th March 1916; educated Addey and Stanhope School and London University; FCII 1948; LLB (2nd Class Honours) 1950; m. 1938 Joan Lockyer (1 s. 1943; 2 d. 1946, 1953); Royal Insurance Co., Ltd. 1934-40 and 1947-50; military service 1941-46; Lieutenant, R.E.; attached Indian Engineers in India, Burma and Siam; Colonial Administrative Service, Tanganyika: Cadet 1950, District Officer 1952, retired 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th January 1962; Principal 12th December 1962; Bombay December 1963.

RICHARDS, Denis Edward; born 25th May 1923; educated Wilson's Grammar School and St. Peter's Hall, Oxford, (Colonial Services Course); m. 1947 Beryl Brown (2 d. 1949, 1952); Royal Navy 1941-46; Lieutenant R.N.V.R.; Gold Coast (Ghana) 1948-60; District Administration 1948-51; Establishment Secretary's Office 1952-56; Secretary, Salaries and Wages Commission, 1956; Ministry of Finance 1957-60; retired July 1960; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd May 1960; Principal 12th July 1960; Karachi June 1961.

RIDGEON, Martin; born 16th July 1933; educated Bromley County Grammar School; m. 1963 Ethne Mary Juliana
Daniel (1 d. 1963): National Service. Royal West Kent Regiment, in Malaya and R.A.S.C., 1952-54; 2nd Lieutenant; Sub-Editor, Reuters, 1954-55; Staff Correspondent, British United Press, Vancouver and Toronto, 1955-57; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Central Office of Information, May 1958; Assistant Information Officer December 1958; Information Officer June 1960: seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office June 1961; Colombo July 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office April 1964.

Rigney, Howard Ernest; born 22nd June 1922; educated University of Western Ontario, Canada, (Honours in English and French; BA) 1941-45, University of Toronto (MA in English 1947) 1945-46 and Université de Paris 1948-50; m. 1950 Margaret Grayling Benn (1 s. 1956); lecturer in English, University of British Columbia, 1946-48; Central Office of Information October 1953 to November 1956; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, November 1956; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, February 1957; Senior Information Officer 16th December 1957; Principal Information Officer (local) April 1958; Regional Information Officer, Montreal, September 1960 to July 1963; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960.

Roberts, Donald Reginald; born 25th June 1927; educated Public Central Secondary School, Plymouth; m. 1948 Norma Simpson (1 s. 1950; 2 d. 1957, 1960); General Post Office 1943; National Service, Royal Engineers, 1945-48; served in Germany; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1949; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Food, October 1949; Commonwealth Relations Office September 1953; Madras September 1954 to October 1956; Cape Town (local Executive Officer) June 1958 to June 1961; Executive Officer September 1959; Kingston July 1962; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Robins, Kenneth Harold; born 19th March 1917; educated Gravesend Junior Technical School; m. 1946 Eileen Goldsmith (1 d. 1948); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, G.P.O., 1935-39; Clerical Officer, Air Ministry, February 1939; R.A.F.V.R. April 1940 to March 1946; Clerical Officer March 1946; Executive Officer 1st April 1951; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1962; Karachi July 1964.

Robinson, William Douglas, OBE (1945); born 5th November 1907; educated Epsom College, Surrey; m. 1948 Phyllis Spridell (née Boden) (1 d. 1949); Indian (Imperial) Police 1927; King's Police Medal 1947; retired 1947; Deputy Inspector-General, West Pakistan Police, 1947-49; Deputy Commissioner, Federation of Malaya Police, 1950-53; Assistant Commissioner, Cyprus Police, 1955-57; Director of Intelligence, Cyprus, 1957-59; Temporary Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th January 1963.

Rogers, Martin Hartley Guy; born 11th June 1925; educated Marlborough College 1939-43 and Jesus College, Cambridge, (Classical Scholar) 1947-49; Law Tripos Class II Division I; m. 1959 Jean Chinn (1 d. 1961; 1 s. 1962); enlisted September 1943; commissioned Royal Lincolnshire Regiment July 1944, served with B.A.O.R. and in Middle East 1945-47; Captain; released August 1947; Temporary Assistant Principal, Ministry of National Insurance, 8th August 1949; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th October 1949; Assistant Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 10th May 1950 to 8th July 1951; Karachi November 1951 to October 1953; Principal 20th September 1953; seconded to the Government of the Federation of Nigeria March 1956 to November 1957; Canadian National Defence College September 1960 to July 1961; Ottawa August 1961; Adviser to Jamaican Ministry of External Affairs January to August 1963.

Romeral, George Arthur; born 8th August 1923; educated St. Ignatius College, Stamford Hill, 1934-40 and The Polytechnic, Regent Street, London, 1952-57; Diploma in Management Studies 1957; graduate Member of Institute of Personnel Management; m. 1953 Elizabeth Christina Bradley (2 s. 1954, 1956; 2 d. 1961, 1963); served with the R.A.F. 1942-46; Clerical Officer, General Post Office, 18th November 1946; Executive Officer 8th June 1950; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 22nd February 1956; seconded as Training Officer, Ministry of Communications, Nigeria, February 1959 to May 1962; Higher Executive Officer (in absentia) 1st January 1961; Inspector of Engineering and Scientific Establishments, General Post Office Headquarters, (Temporary Senior Executive Officer) November 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st July 1964; Delhi November 1964.

Rose, Brian; born 26th January 1930; educated Canford School, Dorset, 1943-47; m. 1952 Audrey Barnes; national service with Intelligence Corps, Austria, 1948-50; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, May 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th May 1954; Peshawar 1955-56; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Ottawa 1958 to 1961; Kingston (local Senior Executive Officer) July 1962; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

Ross Williamson, Reginald Pole; born 25th January 1907; educated privately and at Emmanuel College, Cambridge; BA 1930; MA 1935; m. 1932 Eileen Buchanan; accompanied British Museum expeditions
to Upper Egypt 1930–31 and Ur of the Chaldees 1931–32; Editor of The Bookman 1934; attached to Sunday Observer 1934–39; Adviser on Research in Film Industry 1934–43; Specialist, Ministry of Information, 12th September 1939; Admiralty (Press Division) 9th October 1939; Dominions Office (Press Attaché, Dublin) 9th August 1943; Senior Information Officer with seniority from 1st August 1949; Regional Information Officer, Bombay, April 1953; Senior Executive Officer January 1955; Dublin 31st January 1955; Regional Information Officer, Cape Town, March 1957 to July 1962; Melbourne (local Principal Information Officer) January 1963.

Routhwaite, Denis Christopher; born 11th January 1922; educated Fettes College 1935–40 and St. John's College, Cambridge, 1940–41; Royal Engineers 1940; commissioned 1941; served with Indian Engineers in Persia, Iraq and North Burma; released as Captain December 1946; H.M. Overseas Civil Service 1947–54; served as Administrative Officer Class IV and Class III in Northern Nigeria; Manpower Controller, Qatar Petroleum Company, 1954–55; H.M. Overseas Service 1955–62; served as Administrative Officer Class III and Class II in Northern Nigeria; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, March 1963; Political Adviser, Gan, August 1963 to April 1964; Temporary Senior Information Officer June 1964.

Rowdon, Leslie Raymond Horace; born 24th October 1915; educated Emanuel School; m. Doris Peckover (1 s.); military service 1940–46; released with rank of Captain; Theatrical Manager and Press Officer until 1951; free-lance exhibition deviser for Government Departments 1951–56; Temporary Information Officer, Central Office of Information, April 1956; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th June 1958; Johannesburg July 1958 to September 1961; Information Officer 17th February 1959; local Senior Information Officer April 1960; Senior Information Officer 26th April 1962; Regional Information Officer, Madras, April 1963; Regional Information Officer, Calcutta, (local Principal Information Officer) September 1964.

Rumbold, Sir (Horace) Algernon (Fraser), KCMG (1960: CMG 1953), CIE (1947); born 27th February 1906; educated Wellington 1920–24 and Christ Church, Oxford, (Open Scholarship) October 1924 to December 1927; 2nd Class History School; BA; m. 1946 Adél Hughes (2 d. 1948, 1950); Assistant Principal, India Office, 1st January 1929; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State April 1930 to 1933 and to Permanent Under-Secretary of State December 1933 to September 1934; Principal 24th September 1934; Assistant Secretary 26th July 1943; Deputy High Commissioner, Capetown/Pretoria, September 1949 to February 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 7th November 1955; Temporary Deputy Under-Secretary of State 1st December 1958; Chairman of the Committee on Territorial Questions (Dissolution of Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland) August 1963; Deputy Under-Secretary of State 1st January 1964.

Rumsey, Alfred William Henry; born 23rd February 1910; m. 1938 Carol Read (1 d. 1954); Post Office 1927; Admiralty 1939; Higher Clerical Officer, India Office, 21st January 1946; Executive Officer 20th May 1946; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th August 1947; Wellington November 1954 to June 1958; Kuala Lumpur (local Higher Executive Officer) June 1959 to March 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Delhi July 1962.

Rutter, Alma Doris, MBE (1948); born 12th May 1911; educated Putney Business Training College; Shorthand-Typist, India Office, 21st September 1936; Clerical Officer 8th December 1942; Superintendent of Typists 1942; Personal Assistant to the Secretary of State for India 1945 and to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations 1948; Executive Officer 16th April 1952; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; seconded to Colonial Office December 1961 to September 1962.

Rymer, Garnet Alexander; born 31st January 1915; educated Westcliff High School, Essex; m. 1944 Sylvia Petts; R.A.F. (Administration) 1931–46; served in Iraq, Kurdistan, India, South Africa and West Africa (Sierra Leone); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 1st November 1946; Executive Officer 1st March 1951; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Lagos August 1960 to July 1963.

Sales, Norman Amos, MBE (1956); born 13th September 1911; educated Warehousemen, Clerks and Drapers Schools, Purley, and Hastings Central School; m. 1940 Esmé Turner (2 s. 1941, 1946); 3rd Class Clerk, Supreme Court of Judicature, 1st October 1932; Admiralty April 1941; Higher Clerical Officer 1942; on loan to Office of United Kingdom High Commissioner in India: Delhi September 1947, Bombay May 1950 to March 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st January 1948; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st September 1950; Ottawa June 1955 to August 1959; Senior Executive Officer 17th April 1956; Chief Executive Officer 1st March 1961; Delhi March 1962.

Samples, Reginald McCartney, DSO (1942), OBE (1963); born 11th August 1918; educated Rhyl Grammar School and
University of Liverpool 1935-40; B.Com.; m. 1947 Elsie Hide (2 s. 1947, 1949; 1 step-d. 1938); R.N.V.R. (Air Branch) 1940-46; Lieutenant (A); Central Office of Information March 1947 to August 1948 (Economic Editor of Overseas Newspapers); Commonwealth Relations Office 25th August 1948; British Information Services, India: Economic Information Officer, Bombay, October 1948. Editor-in-Chief, Delhi, April 1952, Deputy Director, Delhi, September 1953; Information Officer 25th January 1952; Senior Information Officer 23rd May 1953; Principal Information Officer (local) 9th September 1953; Principal Information Officer 8th November 1955; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, 1st November 1956; Chief Information Officer (B) 1st December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Canada, July 1959.

SAUL, Jack; born 12th June 1914; educated Purston National School and Dewsbury Technical College; m. 1949 Eileen May Parker; military service September 1939 to November 1945; Sergeant, Parachute Regiment; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 1946; Clerical Officer 1st January 1947; Executive Officer 1st March 1951; Peshawar December 1951; Karachi January 1953 to March 1955; Calcutta May 1957 to November 1960; Higher Executive Officer (local) 20th April 1957; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Salisbury July 1961 to July 1964.

SAVINGER, Ivan Edward Atkinson; born 17th July 1927; educated Brentwood School, Appleby Grammar School and Culford School; m. 1951 Joyce Tabenor (2 s. 1954, 1956); R.A.F. 1945-48; Reporter, *Bury Free-Press*, 1943-45 and 1948; Reporter and Music Critic, *Nottingham Guardian* and *Evening Post*, 1949-52; Reporter and Music Critic, *Birmingham Gazette*, 1952-54; Reuter's Desk Editor 1954-56; Assistant Public Relations Officer, Vauxhall Motors, Ltd., 1956-58; Senior Sub-Editor and News Reader, Federal Broadcasting Corporation, Salisbury, Southern Rhodesia, 1958-60; Head of News, Tanganyika Broadcasting Corporation, 1960-63; B.B.C. Home Reporter, News and Current Affairs, (sound and television) 1962-63; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st November 1963; Information Officer 4th February 1963; Singapore December 1963.

SCANLON, Peter; born 14th May 1924; educated Rugby School, Oxford and London Universities; m. 1949 Elizabeth Britton (1 s. 1956; 1 d. 1958); studied Japanese at London University 1942-43; military service in Intelligence Corps 1944-47; Devonshire I course at Oxford and London 1947-48; Sarawak Civil Service 1949; Assistant Resident, Brunei, 1950-51; studied Chinese and Malay, London University, 1952; District Officer, Miri and Bintulu, 1952-58; Principal Assistant Secretary (Finance), Sarawak, 1959-61; District Officer, Sibu, 1961-64; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st July 1964; Principal 9th September 1964.

SCOTT, Annie Campbell, MBE (1962); born 29th October 1915; educated Melrose Grammar School; enlisted Auxiliary Territorial Service February 1941; Sergeant, Royal Signals, October 1942; served at H.Q. Northern and South-Eastern Commands and at War Office; released February 1946; Temporary Clerk, Dominions Office, 4th February 1946; Clerical Officer 25th July 1949; Executive Officer 1st September 1959; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

SCOTT, David Aubrey; born 3rd August 1919; educated Charterhouse 1933-38 and Birmingham University (Scholar) 1938-39; reading for BSc (Mining Engineering); m. 1941 Vera Ibbitson (1 d. 1942; 2 s. 1944, 1952); R.A. November 1939; Chief Radar Adviser to Egyptian Army 1945-47; Public Relations Officer, Decca Navigator Company, 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, January 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State January 1949; Principal 20th September 1949; Capetown/Pretoria January 1951 to August 1953; Joint Services Staff College September 1953 to April 1954; seconded to Cabinet Office July 1954 to March 1956; Secretariat of Prime Minister's Meeting 1955 and Malta Round Table Conference 1955; Secretary-General, Federation of Malaya Constitutional Conference, and British Caribbean Federation Conference, 1956; seconded to Foreign Service as First Secretary, Office of Commissioner-General for the United Kingdom in South-East Asia, Singapore, May 1956 to March 1958; temporary Assistant Secretary 15th December 1958; Basutoland Constitutional Discussions 1958-59; member of Committee of Officials on Review of Constitutions of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; Assistant Secretary to Monckton Advisory Commission 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Salisbury, March 1961 to November 1963; member of team of Advisers on Central Africa appointed by the Rt. Hon. R. A. Butler 1962; Imperial Defence College 1964; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, (local Assistant Under-Secretary) January 1965.

SCOTT, James Archibald, MVO (1961); born 5th March 1932; educated Dollar Academy, University of St. Andrews and the Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario; m. 1957 Elizabeth Buchan-Hepburn (1 d. 1960; 2 s. 1962, 1964); National Service with 2nd Allied Tactical Air Force 1954-56; R.Aux. A.F. 1956; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 30th October
1956; Resident Clerk March 1957; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 20th May 1957; Delhi October 1958 to 1962; Principal (local) 4th April 1961; Principal 1st August 1961; United Kingdom Mission to the United Nations, New York, May 1962.

SCOTT, Michael, mvo (1961); born 19th May 1923; educated Dame Allan's School 1933-40 and Durham University 1947-49; (Politics and Economics) 1949; BA; m. 1944 Sylvia Vincent-Barwood (3 s. 1945, 1950, 1954); enlisted in Durham Light Infantry 1941; commissioned from Indian Military Academy 1943; 1st Gurkha Rifles; Captain; released 1947; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, November 1949; Principal 14th June 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office 9th April 1957; Karachi October 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, August 1959 to January 1962; Delhi October 1963; Assistant Secretary 2nd April 1964.

SCOTT, Thomas Alastair Henderson; born 21st August 1914; educated British West Indies, France and Balliol College, Oxford, 1933-36 (Elton Exhibition 1936) and 1937-39; 1st Class Honours English Language and Literature; BA 1936; BLITT 1939; Journalism 1939-37; Royal Marines 1939-45; Major, R.M.; Central Office of Information 1946-51; N.A.T.O. International Secretariat 1951-55; Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1955; Regional Information Officer, Montreal, August 1955; Chief Information Officer (B) (temporary) May 1958; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation as Public Relations Adviser to Government of Trinidad and Tobago July 1962.

SCRAGG, Robert Thomas Frederick; born 12th November 1918; educated St. Andrew's School, Holborn (Neville Bursary) and Churchdown School, Kent; m. 1944 Hilda Roberts (1 s. 1945; 1 d. 1949); Queen's Royal Regiment 1939; war service in France, Belgium, Egypt, Libya, Tunisia and Algeria; invalided 1944; Temporary Assistant, War Office, 1944-46; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, August 1946; Executive Officer 1950; Higher Executive Officer 21st March 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st February 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th July 1961; Dar es Salaam December 1961; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 14th August 1964.

SEAR, Bertram Burlington; born 3rd April 1921; educated Wilson's Grammar School, London, 1932-37; m. 1945 Frances Mary Anderson (3 s. 1947, 1949, 1951; 1 d. 1950); Public Assistance Dept., London County Council, 1937-38; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Education, December 1938; enlisted in R.A.F. October 1940; trained as pilot in North America and South Africa: Sergeant Pilot June 1943; Flight Sergeant June 1944; Training Command, Northern Ireland, 1944-45; commissioned 1945; service in Persian Gulf 1945-46; released, Flying Officer, April 1946; returned to Ministry of Education May 1946; Executive Officer May 1947 (seniority from April 1945); Commonwealth Relations Office 19th March 1951; Madras January 1953 to March 1956; Delhi (local Higher Executive Officer) 14th April 1959 to June 1962; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959; Accra (local Senior Executive Officer) June 1964; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 14th August 1964.

SHANNON, Godfrey Eccleston Boyd, CMG (1951); born 14th December 1907; educated Wellington College 1921-26 and St. John's College, Cambridge, 1926-30; Browne Medal for Greek Epigram 1928; 1st Class in Parts I and II Classical Tripos; BA 1929; Certificate of Competent Knowledge in French 1930; MA 1938; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 27th October 1930; Private Secretary to successive Parliamentary Under-Secretaries of State 23rd January 1935 to 15th February 1937; accompanied the Duke of Devonshire to Australia and New Zealand September 1936 to February 1937; Principal 15th February 1937; served on Secretariat of Imperial Conference 1937; Wellington December 1938 to April 1941; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1943; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to the following Conferences: International Civil Aviation Conference, Chicago, and Commonwealth Air Conversations, Montreal, November 1944, Council of Foreign Ministers, London, and United Nations Preparatory Commission, London, 1945, United Nations General Assembly, London, League of Nations Assembly, Geneva, and United Nations General Assembly, New York, 1946, Council of Foreign Ministers, Moscow, United Nations General Assembly, New York, and Council of Foreign Ministers, London, 1947; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, June 1948 to January 1951 (Acting High Commissioner 6th May to 2nd August 1949); Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, (local Assistant Under-Secretary of State) November 1952 to February 1956; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 4th December 1954; United Kingdom Delegation to the Brussels Negotiations with the E.E.C. May 1962 to January 1963 and to the United Nations Trade and Development Conference, Geneva, 1964.

SHARKEY, Colum John; born 9th June 1931; educated St. Malachy's College, Belfast; m. 1962 Olive Brassil (1 d. 1963; 1 s. 1964); Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 1949-54 (attached to Government of Northern Ireland); Commonwealth Relations Office 5th April 1954; Delhi 1955;

SHAW, John Dennis Bolton, MVO (1961); born 5th July 1920; educated Manchester Grammar School 1931–38 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1938–40 and 1946–48 (History Scholar); 2nd Class Honours Modern History; MA; m. 1955 Isabel Lowe (2 s. 1957, 1961); Royal Artillery (Field) 1940–46; served in Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt, Italy and India; attached Royal West African Frontier Force 1945–46; released as Lieutenant September 1946; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 8th November 1948; Principal 6th November 1950; seconded to Sierra Leone Government October 1955; Acting District Commissioner and Acting Deputy Financial Secretary, Sierra Leone, October 1955 to April 1957; Commonwealth Relations Office 10th July 1957; Karachi November 1958 to February 1961; seconded to Foreign Office and posted to British Embassy, Washington, May 1961 to November 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 3rd December 1962, (acting) 1st July 1963.

SHEARS, Henry James; born 11th March 1918; educated Sloane School, Chelsea; m. 1940 Eileen Marguerite Sadler (2 d. 1942, 1951); enlisted Territorial Army 1939; embodied for war service 24th August 1939; Bombardier 1940; Sergeant 1941; 2nd Lieutenant, East Surrey Regiment, 1944; Acting Captain 1946; demobilized 1946 as temporary Captain; Clerical Officer, India Office, 3rd June 1947; Territorial Reserve of Officers, List 'B': Officer Commanding, 3rd Cadet Battalion, East Surrey Regiment, March 1953 to March 1954; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Cape Town April 1954 to June 1957; Dublin October 1957 to July 1961; Ottawa (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1961 to August 1964; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.
