SIMMONS, Guy Lintorn, MVO (1961); born 27th February 1925; educated Bradfield College 1939–43 and Oriel College, Oxford, (History Scholar) 1947–49; 2nd Class Honours in Modern History; m. 1951 Sheila Jacob (3 d. 1953, 1955, 1960); R.A.F. October 1943 to December 1946; Sergeant Pilot; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th July 1949; Peshawar December 1950; Lahore 1951; Dacca March 1952 to May 1954; Principal 20th September 1953; Bombay July 1958; Acting Deputy High Commissioner August to September 1958 and March to July 1960; Delhi May 1961 to March 1964.

SIMMONS, Margaret Rosalind; born 29th August 1929; educated Convent of the Sacred Heart, Maidstone, 1937–41, Henrietta Barnett School 1941–47 and London School of Economics 1948–51; 2nd Class Honours BSc (Econ); Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd November 1952; Delhi September 1954 to March 1957; Dublin June 1961 to July 1964; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 29th January 1962; Higher Executive Officer 6th July 1964.

SIMMS, Peter John; born 9th June 1927; educated Archbishop Tennyson's Grammar School, London, 1938–42 and Kingston-on-Thames Technical College 1943–45; m. 1957 Celia Dorothy Mary Gittens (3 d. 1958, 1960, 1963); Royal Navy 1945–47; Merchant Navy 1948–53; Reporter, sub-editor, News Exchange Ltd., Surrey, 1953–56; Sub-editor, Eastern Daily Press, Norfolk, 1956–58; Sub-editor, News Chronicle, 1958; Assistant Information Officer, London Press Service (North American Service), Central Office of Information, 1958–59; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th August 1959; Johannesburg 1959–62; Salisbury 1962; Assistant Information Officer 9th March 1962; Sydney 1962–63; Information Officer 1st September 1963.

SIMS, Alfred John; born 7th May 1914; educated Tollington Park School, London; enlisted Royal Engineers August 1940; released March 1946; Clerical Officer, National Insurance, June 1948; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th June 1956; Bombay July 1957 to July 1959; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 4th July 1960; Cape Town August 1960 to February 1962; Higher Executive Officer February 1962; Ottawa February 1962.

SKILBECK, Ralph Finlay Wright; born 21st October 1942; educated Minchenden Grammar School, Southgate, N.14 and Wadham College, Oxford, (Minor Scholar) 1961–64; First Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1964.
SKINNER, Douglas Maurice Ralph; born 7th October 1921; educated Glyn School, Epsom, 1932-38; m. 1945 Ivy Garner (1 d. 1946); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Education, 1st July 1938; temporarily transferred to Admiralty (Naval Intelligence) August 1939; served in Royal Navy 1942-46; returned to Ministry of Education August 1946; Executive Officer 1947; (seniority from April 1945); Commonwealth Relations Office 19th March 1951; Colombo February 1953 to March 1955; Higher Executive Officer 1st November 1953; Delhi September 1955 to November 1958; Canberra August 1959 to July 1962; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

SLATER, Gordon James Augustus; born 8th July 1922; educated Sydney, Australia; m. 1952 Beryl Oliver (1 d. 1952; 1 s. 1955); editorial staff, Sydney Daily Telegraph, 1945-46; Brisbane Telegraph, 1947-48; Parliamentary reporter, Press Association (Central News), London, 1949-52; London Daily Telegraph November 1952 to January 1958; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 6th January 1958; Karachi 29th March 1958; Acting Deputy Director, British Information Services, Karachi, 31st March 1960; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, (local Principal Information Officer) October 1960 to July 1961; Vancouver (local Principal Information Officer) October 1961 to August 1964; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963.

SLINGER, Richard; born 8th November 1924; educated Evered High School, Liverpool, 1936-41; qualified L.C.C. Exhibition to London School of Economics and Political Science in British Constitution August 1955; m. Lorna Hodge (2 d. 1947, 1948; 1 s. 1957; 1 adopted d. 1960); Royal Navy (Combined Operations) 1942-46; Royal Fleet Reservist with 5th Destroyer Flotilla 1952-53; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Works, June 1947 to August 1955; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd August 1955; Delhi February 1956 to October 1957; Calcutta February 1958 to February 1960; Lagos June 1960 to March 1962; Enugu March to August 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Lagos August 1962 to March 1963; Delhi March 1964.

SMALL, David Purvis; born 17th October 1930; educated Our Lady's High School, Motherwell; m. 1957 Patricia Kennedy (2 s. 1959, 1960); Clerical Officer, Admiralty, Bath, 8th April 1953; Executive Officer, Rosyth, 9th May 1955; Singapore January 1958 to April 1960; Naval Law Branch June 1960 to November 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office 6th November 1961; Madras April 1962 to June 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964; Ibadan August 1964.

SMALLMAN, Barry Granger; born 22nd February 1924; educated St. Paul's School 1936-42 and Trinity College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar) 1942-43 and 1946-47; Classical Tripos Parts I and II Class I; BA 1947; MA 1952; m. 1952 Sheila Knight (1 d. 1953; 2 s. 1955, 1957); Intelligence Corps 1944-46; served in Australia; released as Lieutenant 1946; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 15th December 1947; Secretary to Venn Commission of Enquiry into the Sugar Industry of British Guiana December 1948 to March 1949; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State September 1951 to December 1952; Principal 1st January 1953; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations November 1956 to March 1957 and January to April 1958; seconded to the Government of Western Nigeria as Senior Assistant Secretary, Governor's Office, Ibadan, January 1959 to October 1960; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd January 1961; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations September to December 1961 and 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Freetown, June 1963.

SMALLWOOD, John Evelyn, Commander R.N. (retd.); born 10th May 1910; educated Royal Naval College, Dartmouth, 1923-27 and Royal Naval College, Greenwich, 1931; m. 1943 Estella Dorothy Bragg (2 s. 1945, 1947); served in Royal Navy (specialised Fleet Air Arm 1933) 1927-60; Ministry of Defence 1951-52 and 1955-57; Naval Attaché, Bangkok, 1958-60; retired June 1960; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd November 1960; Principal 7th December 1960; Karachi April 1961 to July 1964.

SMEDLEY, Harold, MBE (Military) (1946); born 19th June 1920; educated Aldenham School 1934-39 and Pembroke College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar) 1939-40 and 1945-46; Classical Tripos Part I Class I 1946; MA 1948; m. 1950 Beryl Brown (2 s. 1952, 1959; 2 d. 1954, 1960); embodied in R.A.(A.A.)1940; commissioned into Royal Marines 1941; Anti-Aircraft duties in United Kingdom, Middle East and Mediterranean 1941-43; Royal Marine Commandos 1943-45 (Lieutenant); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 26th August 1946; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 17th September 1947; Wellington September 1948 to September 1950; Principal 20th September 1949; Salisbury January 1951 to November 1953; Acting High Commissioner August to October 1953; Private Secretary to Secretary of State December 1954 to January 1957; accompanied Secretary of State on visits to New Zealand, Australia, Ceylon, India and Pakistan in 1955 and to Canada 1956; Calcutta February 1957 and Delhi (local Assistant
SMITH, Victor William, CBE (1948); born 6th August 1891; educated Dean Close Memorial School, Cheltenham; m. 1936 Susie Gwendoline Martin (1 d. 1938; 1 s. 1940); joined Indian Police 1911; King's Police Medal 1924; retired 1932; Civil Assistant, War Office, 1939 to 1955; Temporary Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, January 1956.

SMITH, William Jeffrey; born 14th October 1916; educated King Edward VII School, Sheffield, 1927-35 and University College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1935-38; BA 1938; MA 1945; m. 1942 Marie Hughes (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1951); employed by Calico Printers' Association 1938 to 1940; enlisted September 1939; embodied in R.A. September 1940; commissioned June 1941; served in North Africa, Sicily and Italy; transferred to York and Lancaster Regiment March 1945; Captain; released September 1946; Assistant Principal; Dominions Office, 11th December 1946, Principal 1st August 1948; Capetown/Pretoria October 1953 to June 1956; sundry international conferences of G.A.T.T. etc.; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st March 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st July 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th July 1961.

SNELLING, Sir Arthur Wendell, KCMG (1960; CMG 1954), KCVO (1962); born 7th May 1914; educated Ackworth School, Yorkshire, 1925-31 and University College, London; BSc (Econ.) Class I Honours 1934; m. 1939 Frieda Barnes (1 s. 1948); Study-Group Secretary, Royal Institute of International Affairs, 1934-36; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 22nd October 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 2nd February 1939; accompanied him on visit to Southern Africa May to July 1939; Acting Principal 23rd May 1940; Joint Secretary to the United Kingdom Economic delegation to America September to November 1943 and to the International Monetary Conference, Bretton Woods, U.S.A., June to September 1944; accompanied Lord Keynes on Mission to U.S.A. and Canada October to December 1944; member of United Kingdom Delegation to Reparations Conference, Paris, 1945; Assistant Secretary 2nd September 1946; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, December 1947 to January 1950; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 11th September 1952; Deputy High Commissioner, Capetown/Pretoria, May 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 6th February 1956; visited India and Pakistan 1956 and 1962, Singapore 1956, Accra 1957 and Malaya 1959; High Commissioner in Ghana September 1959 to December 1961; Deputy Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 15th January 1962; Deputy Under-Secretary of State 1st January 1964.

SMITH, Arnold Terence, MBE; born 7th October 1922; educated Christ Church School, Dover, and Dover Technical College 1931-38; m. 1944 Mary James (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); Post Office August 1939-49; military service August 1939 to October 1946; commissioned 1943; served Middle East and N.W. Europe; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1949; Executive Officer April 1952; Karachi September 1952 to February 1956; Madras (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1956 to November 1959; Higher Executive Officer June 1959; Kuala Lumpur (local Senior Executive Officer) June 1961; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

SMITH, Jack Braddon; born 17th June 1929; educated Dunstable Grammar School 1937-47; m. 1958 Patricia Bruce (1 d. 1961); Open Executive Officer Examination October 1947; National Service, Royal Signals, Egypt, 1948-50; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 14th December 1953; Delhi October 1955 to October 1957; Karachi (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1958 to November 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

SMITH, Leonard Gordon, MBE (1964); born 11th March 1911; m. 1936 Ethel Poster (1 s. 1939; 1 d. 1942); counter clerk and telegraphist, G.P.O., 11th March 1928; Clerical Officer, India Office, 13th March 1933; Higher Clerical Officer 17th December 1945; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 1st November 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st March 1954; Canberra April 1954 to February 1957; Sydney January 1960 to April 1962; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.
SOWDEN, Laurence James, MBE (1960); born 22nd July 1906; educated Hugh Myddelton School, London; Telegraphist, G.P.O. (Overseas Section), 3rd September 1923; Clerical Officer, India Office, 24th July 1930; War Office (on loan) 1st January 1940; Higher Clerical Officer (temporary) 8th August 1940; Higher Clerical Officer 23rd March 1943; volunteered for Royal Navy 27th March 1942; served Western Approaches; invalided out 12th May 1943 and returned to India Office; regraded as Executive Officer with effect from 23rd March 1942; Higher Executive Officer 1st October 1960.

STANBURY, Cyril John; born 30th June 1912; educated Stonelaw School and privately; m. 1959 Sirikit Awang; war service, Air Ministry, 1939–41; Royal Air Force 1941–46; Foreign Correspondent, South America and Germany, 1946–51; State Information Officer, Kelantan and Perak, Federation of Malaya, 1953–59; Senior Information Officer, United Kingdom Commission, Singapore, 1959–63; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th September 1963; Singapore (local Principal Information Officer) January 1964.

STANLEY, Henry Sydney Herbert; born 5th March 1920; educated Eton 1933–38 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1938–40; War Degree History; m. 1941 Margaret Dixon (3 s. 1949, 1951, 1953); enlisted in ranks July 1940; commissioned in King's Royal Rifle Corps December 1940; served in North-West Europe 1944–46 and at H.Q., Control Commission for Germany; Captain; released August 1946; Temporary Officer, Grade III, Foreign Office (German Section), September 1946 to December 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th December 1947; Secretary, United Kingdom/Southern Rhodesia Financial Talks, March 1949; Principal 1st November 1949; Karachi July 1950 to December 1952; seconded to Office of High Commissioner for Basutoland, Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland October 1954 to September 1956; Capetown/Pretoria September 1956 to September 1957; seconded to Foreign Office, and posted to British Embassy, Washington, February 1959 to March 1961; Adviser to Governor of Tanganyika on Commonwealth and External Affairs, June 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Dar es Salaam, December 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office Representative in Kenya June 1963; Deputy High Commissioner, Nairobi, December 1963.

STANSFIELD, George Norman; born 28th February 1926; educated Liscard High School, Wallasey; m. 1947 Elizabeth Margaret Williams; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1942–44 and 1947–49; R.A.F. 1944–47; Clerical Officer 1949; Executive Officer, Ministry of Supply, March 1952; War Office November 1958; Higher Executive Officer 11th July 1960; Administrative Officer to Director-General of Armament Production 1960–61; Secretary of the Armament Production Advisory Committees 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office 8th November 1961; Calcutta October 1962.

STEDMAN, Robert Edward; born 24th May 1923; educated Highbury County School; m. 1946 Ivy Lillian Leach (2 d. 1949, 1954); Boy Messenger, General Post Office, 1937; Sorter, London Postal Region, 1941; R.A.F. 1941–46; Postal and Telegraph Officer, London Postal Region, 1948; Clerical Officer, Crown Agents for Oversea Governments and Administrations, 1950; Executive Officer, Crown Agents, 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st May 1962; Calcutta 1963–64; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

STEPHENS, Malcolm George; born 14th July 1937; educated Shooter's Hill Grammar School 1948–53; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th December 1953; Executive Officer 3rd February 1956; National Service May 1956 to May 1958; Accra 1959–62; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; member of Inspection Team to Kenya, Uganda, Tanganyika and the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland June to August 1962; Nairobi June 1963.

STEPNEY, William Stanley; born 10th December 1923; educated Strand School; m. 1947 Irene Allen (3 s. 1948, 1949, 1951); enlisted Royal Air Force December 1941; served in Southern Rhodesia, South Africa, Middle East, North Africa, Italy and Kenya; Warrant Officer Pilot; released December 1946; R.A.F.V.R. 1949–54; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 30th December 1946; Clerical Officer 23rd October 1947; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

STOCKWELL, James Arthur, MBE (1959); born 31st August 1921; educated Wembley County School 1931–38; m. 1943 Sheila Mewten (1 s. 1953; 1 d. 1954); Clerical Officer, India Office, 12th December 1938; enlisted in The Buffs (Royal East Kent Regiment) June 1940; commissioned in Welch Regiment July 1942; Captain October 1944; served in North-West Europe 1944–45; Mentioned in Despatches; served in Palestine and Egypt 1945–46; released October 1946; Executive Officer 29th August 1947; toured India, Pakistan, Ceylon, Canada, South Africa and Southern Rhodesia with Batterbee Mission 1951–52; Higher Executive Officer 6th March 1953; Delhi May 1953 to July 1954; Ottawa August 1955 to July 1958; Passport Officer, Capetown, May 1959 to June 1960; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Capetown/Pretoria June

**STORAR**, Leonore Elizabeth Therese; born 3rd May 1920; educated Park School, Glasgow, 1929-38 and St. Andrews University 1938-41; Political Economy and Political Science; MA; Temporary Employment Officer, Ministry of Labour, July 1941 to January 1942; embodied in A.T.S. February 1942; commissioned April 1942; A.T.S. Staff College; G.S.O. III in H.Q., B.A.O.R., September 1945 to May 1946; Junior Commander; released May 1946; Temporary Administrative Assistant, Ministry of Works, 6th January 1947; Executive Officer 20th February 1948; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1948; Principal 8th May 1950; Delhi and Calcutta November 1951 to May 1953; Salisbury May 1956 to June 1958; Colombo September 1960 to November 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 3rd December 1962, (acting) 1st July 1963.

**STORRS**, Peter John Francis; born 12th January 1916; educated Radley College 1929-33 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1934-37; 2nd Class Hons. Modern Languages June 1936; 2nd Class Hons. (1st Division) Modern History June 1937; MA; studied abroad 1938-39; Temporary Secretary, British Legation, Oslo, September 1939; member of British Mission, Northern Norway, May 1940; awarded Norwegian Military Medal; R.A.S.C. Missions to Washington 1949 and 1950; member of O.E.E.C. Delegation to International Materials Conference, and later head of O.E.E.C. Mission, Washington, 1951; Assistant Director (later Director), Commonwealth-American Current Affairs Unit of the English-Speaking Union, May 1953; Director of Public Relations, Government of Cyprus, November 1956; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th April 1959; Regional Information Officer, Calcutta, (local Principal Information Officer) May 1959; Regional Information Officer, Ottawa, May 1962; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963.

B.; m. 1942 Janet Browning (3d 1949, 1951, 1957); R.N.V.R. 1942; commissioned as Pilot, Fleet Air Arm, 1943; demobilized May 1946; Administrative Officer, Colonial Service, Tanganyika, 1946-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963; Nairobi June 1964.

**SULLIVAN**, Patrick Joseph; born 7th April 1931; educated O'Connell School, Dublin, 1942-48; Clerical Officer, Crown Agents for Oversea Governments and Administrations, 1949; National Service, R.A.F., 1950-52; Seconded Tanganyika Government 1954-57; Executive Officer 31st January 1958; Commonwealth Relation Office 24th April 1962; Delhi May 1962 to May 1964; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

**SUTTON**, Stanley Cecil, CBE (1961), MSc (Econ.); born 23rd September 1907; educated Tottenham County School, London School of Economics (MSc (Econ.), First Class Honours in Politics 1930, MSc (Econ.) in Politics 1938) and University College, London, (Diploma in Librarianship 1931); m. 1935 Elizabeth Sinclair (2 s. 1938, 1949; 2 d. 1941, 1943); Sub-Librarian, India Office Library, 17th June 1935; Assistant Keeper 17th June 1937; Keeper 1st Class 4th May 1946; Librarian 1st August 1949; in charge of India Office Records 1st March 1954; Keeper of India Office Records from April 1959.

**SYDENHAM-CLARKE**, Tredway Seymour Sydenham; born 19th January 1913; educated Charterhouse 1926-30 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1931-34; 2nd Class Modern Languages Tripos (German and Spanish); MA; m. 1940 Marjorie Gourlay (2 d. 1943, 1949); Ceylon Civil Service 1936-46; Secretary, Combined Security Bureau, Ceylon, 1940-43; Assistant Government Agent, Joint Secretary, U.K. Delegation to United Nations Preparatory Conference on Tariffs and Trade, Geneva, 1947; U.K. Trade Commissioner, Durban, Johannesburg and Cape Town, 1948-55; Courtaulds Ltd. 1955-58; Administrative Staff College, Henley, 1957; Colonial Development Corporation, High Commission Territories Region, 1958-61; Commonwealth Relations Office Security Officer 18th September 1961.

**SYKES**, Edwin Leonard; born 1st May 1914; educated Leys School, Cambridge, 1927-32, Grenoble University February to July 1933 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1933-37; History Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class I; MA; m. 1946 Margaret McCulloch; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 4th October 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 4th August 1939; military service September 1939 to April 1945; France and Belgium
(B.E.F.) November 1939 to May 1940; Major, Royal Signals, 1941; Algeria and Tunisia (First Army) November 1942 to January 1944; Washington, U.S.A., (British Army Staff) February 1944 to April 1945; Principal 2nd April 1943; Ottawa April 1945 to July 1947; seconded to Cabinet Office January 1949 to January 1951; member of Secretariat of Meetings of Commonwealth Finance Ministers 1949, Foreign Ministers 1950, and Prime Ministers 1951, and of Commonwealth Consultative Committee in London 1950; Assistant Secretary 21st May 1951; Delhi July 1952 to September 1954; Imperial Defence College 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Salisbury, July 1956 to March 1959; seconded to Colonial Office November 1961 to July 1962; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 28th February 1964.

Windle, Anthony Peter William; born 22nd February 1928; m. 1951 Helen Laing (2 s. 1952, 1957); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, General Post Office, 2nd January 1945; National Service with Royal Air Force (Signals) March 1946 to August 1948; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1949; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th August 1949; Colombo May 1951 to July 1954; Karachi July 1956 to July 1958; Bombay (local Executive Officer) July 1959 to October 1961; Executive Officer September 1959; Kingston June 1962; Higher Executive Officer 14th August 1964.

Winter, Arnold Martin; born 22nd December 1920; educated Upton House Central School, London; m. 1951 Rita Hillringhaus (1 s. 1951; 1 d. 1956); war service in R.A.F. 1941-46; Temporary Clerk II, Control Commission for Germany, September 1946; Control Officer III 10th May 1948; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th June 1951; Karachi October 1953 to March 1958; Executive Officer 24th December 1954; Colombo May 1959 to June 1961; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Nicosia September 1963.

Wolstenholme, Alan; born 3rd November 1923; educated Kimberworth Senior Boys' School, South Yorkshire; m. 1960 Rita Kathleen Grimshaw (1 d. 1961); Junior Reporter, Rotherham Express, 1939; wartime service, Merchant Navy, 1942-46; Reporter, Yorkshire Evening News, 1946-48; Reporter, Straits Times, Singapore, 1948-51; Sub-Editor, Reuters, London, 1951-52; Chief Reporter and subsequently News Editor, Malay Mail, Kuala Lumpur, 1953-63; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 28th May 1963; Kuala Lumpur May 1963; Information Officer 30th December 1963; Kuching January 1964; Kuala Lumpur January 1964.

Wool-Lewis, Cyril Eric, OBE (1951); born 17th June 1906; educated Westminster School and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1925-29; commissioned in East Surrey Regiment 1929; Assistant Commissioner of Police, Sierra Leone, 1935; Assistant District Commissioner, Sierra Leone, 1937; District Commissioner 1942; Commissioner of the Turks and Caicos Islands, B.W.I., 1946-51; seconded to the Colonial Office 1951-53; Administrative Officer Class II, Northern Nigeria, 1953; Administrative Officer Class I 1954; transferred to Nigerian Federal Government Service 1956; Staff Grade 1956; Permanent Secretary 1957; retired from Overseas Civil Service June 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd October 1961.

Woolverton, Kenneth Arthur Frederick; born 4th August 1926; educated Orange Hill Grammar School 1938-44; m. Kathleen Eleanor West; Meteorologist, R.A.F., 1944-48; Hendon Borough Council 1948-50; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 3rd April 1950; Executive Officer 19th February 1952; Higher Executive Officer 11th July 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 18th December 1961; Kingston May 1964.

Wright, John Arthur, born 10th January 1932; educated Heanor Grammar School, Derbyshire; m. 1956 Enys Ann Roberts (1 s. 1962); Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, May 1948; National Service (Royal Air Force) 1950-52; Librarian IV, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1959; Librarian III September 1962.

Wythers, John Rowland Graham, BEM (1945); born 2nd February 1918; educated Soham Grammar School, Cambs., 1929-34; m. 1945 Joyce Warren (1 s. 1946; 1 d. 1948); L.C.C. Social Welfare Department 1934-39; Relieving Officers' Certificate, Poor Law Examinations Board, 1936; Territorial Army (Royal Artillery, Heavy A.A.) 1939-42; served in Norway and North Africa; Intelligence Corps 1942; served in Persia and Iraq (Warrant Officer); L.C.C. Social Welfare Department 1946-47; Assistant Area Meals Officer, L.C.C. Civic Restaurants, 1st May 1947; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, 12th July 1948; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th December 1958; Chief Registrar 1st January 1959; Bombay December 1959 to March 1963; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 16th September 1963.

Young, Eric; born 16th November 1924; educated Maltby Grammar School, Yorkshire, 1935-42 and Sheffield University 1942-43 and 1946-48; Honours Class II Division I in English Language and Literature 1948; BA; m. 1949 Sheila Hutchinson (1 d. 1956; 2 s. 1958, 1961); Royal Navy 1943-46; served in Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and Far East; joined Sheffield Telegraph as reporter and leader-writer July 1948; sub-editor, Western Morning News, Plymouth, 1951; sub-editor and later regional news editor, Guardian, Manchester, 1953-58; visited West Africa as reporter 1958; Public Relations Officer, National Coal Board, Manchester, 1958-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, and Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office in
Tanganyika and Zanzibar, January 1960; Senior Information Officer March 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office as Deputy Director, British Information Services, Tanganyika, December 1961 to September 1963; Regional Information Officer (local Principal Information Officer), Kaduna, November 1963.

Young, Joffre Alfred; born 26th March 1915; educated Merton School; m. 1941 Ethel Violet Welfare; Post Office 1929; Clerical Officer, Savings Bank Department, 1938; Clerical Officer, Canterbury Telephone Area, 1948; Higher Clerical Officer, Shrewsbury Telephone Area, 1950; Higher Executive Officer, (Treasury Pooling Scheme), Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; Dacca October 1962.

Young, William Dempster; born 13th October 1912; m. 1940 Patricia Harrison (2 d. 1941, 1947; 1 s. 1945); enlisted Royal Artillery 1933, retired with rank of Major 1948; Clerical Officer 19th December 1947; Delhi January 1948 to August 1950; Karachi September 1951 to July 1955; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; Delhi November 1955 to November 1957; Kuala Lumpur April 1958 to August 1961; Karachi April 1962; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 1st September 1963; Higher Executive Officer 25th November 1963.

Laser rangefinding was one of the first uses suggested when the laser principle was discovered: rangefinders will be among the earliest operational applications. Advantages include independence of good light conditions, high accuracy at longer ranges and the ability to operate undetected.

Barr & Stroud invented the modern optical rangefinder and are themselves in the forefront of British laser development. Now they offer laser rangefinders, having come to an agreement with the Hughes Aircraft Company of California, who discovered the laser principle.
